load samples the private bytes twice. Nothing is read from or written to the ledger.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.40). Nothing persisted; 0.12.40 answers without the members, which a reader
of this build reads as absent.

### 1.281 Slice HS-5e (0.12.42): a Lab pointer input the foreground check refused before its intent never reached its input (#402; the W5 case of the HS-5 window on 11-05, #5 on 0.12.41: a Lab tap refused `application_not_foreground` with no input intent read effect `indeterminate`; investigation `rd-1031/backend-switch/w5-investigation.md`; coordinator work order `rd-1031/backend-switch/brief-hs-5e.md` with the coordinator's decision of 11-05, the `input_returned: false` route)

[contained-lab-operation.md](contained-lab-operation.md) (the input-returned flag, in the terminal
record's paragraph) is the contract. 1.281 was the next free number on the base `e3440565`.

**Why.** The foreground check sits in the one input path before the input's intent is written
(`HostShared::input` calls `require_foreground_application` before it drafts the `input.intent`);
its refusal is the input's own `command.rejected` with effect `not_performed` plus the
`runtime.failed` record ([application-lifecycle.md](application-lifecycle.md)). The Lab set
`input_returned` true and the effect `indeterminate` as soon as the input call came back, and only
an `input.committed` or `input.failed` changed the effect, which a refusal before the intent never
writes. So the record said "result undetermined" of a tap that was never pressed, and
`do --capture --record` recorded it as an undetermined click and left its step open
([lab-recording.md](lab-recording.md)).

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HS5E-1 | a Lab operation's `input_returned` and `effect` (the record's, and each declared attempt's) | behaviour (no shape change) | HS-5e | HS-5e | when the input fails with `application_not_foreground` or `application_foreground_unknown` (the foreground check's refusals, both before the intent write), no `input.intent` of the request after the floor exists, and the returned terminal is this action's own `command.rejected` with effect `not_performed`, the attempt (and so the record) has `input_returned` false, effect `not_performed`, no intent, action or input event, and its failure at stage `input`; a declared operation's effect stays the aggregate of its attempts. Not included: a refusal the check fenced (an adb failure with unconfirmed cleanup fails with the fence's code), `application_store_not_allowed` (a Lab operation never taps a store: `InputForeground::Assigned`), and every failure after the intent, which keeps `input_returned` true and `indeterminate` until an outcome event resolves it |
| HS5E-2 | the input-returned flag | contract sentence | HS-5e | — | true only once the input reached the device input path and wrote its intent; a refusal before that write leaves it false with effect `not_performed` |

**Tests.** Host row "#402 HS-5e" (`gate_hs5`, the fake device of HS-5b): adapted
`hs5_pointer_input_before_application_refused_by_foreground_gate` (the W5 case: receipt `failed`,
failure `application_not_foreground` at `input`, `input_returned` false, effect `not_performed`, no
intent, action or input event; the Lab client's shared verifier accepts the record, its final
command event's `not_performed` included; HS-5b's assertions unchanged); new
`hs5e_sent_input_with_unknown_result_stays_indeterminate` (an adb-touch instance whose application
runs: the tap passes the check, is sent, and its input backend fails with a transient error, so
`input.failed` carries `indeterminate`: receipt `failed` at `input`, `input_returned` true, intent,
action and input event present, effect `indeterminate`, verified by the same client). The helper
`lab_tap` now reads `lab_tap_verified`; neither test sleeps or reads the clock.

**Interface.** No step for 0.12.42: the record's shape and every word are unchanged, and the new
combination is one every earlier reader already accepts, so no reader of an earlier build refuses
an answer or a stored record. The record validator of the contract crate (on `e3440565`,
`crates/actingcommand-contract/src/runtime/lab_operation.rs` lines 574–577 for the record and
758–761 for an attempt) requires, with `input_returned` false, no intent, no input event and effect
`not_performed`, which the record keeps; the rule of lines 578–581 and 762–764 (a returned input
without an outcome event is `indeterminate`) is not met, because the input did not return. The
shared verifier (`lab_operation_evidence.rs` lines 631–635: no reported intent means no intent and
no action events; lines 702–718: only a returned input's failure stage is checked) and the
receipt's validation (`runtime.rs`, the `ContainedLabOperation` arm) take it as they take any
failure before input; the final `command.rejected` carries `not_performed`, an existing word. The
readers checked: actinglab of 0.12.41 (online `do`, through `runtime-client`'s receipt validation
and verifier; offline `resource restore`, through the same verifier), the MCP (`ac_lab_do` runs the
install's actinglab), actingctl (reads events only) and the console of UI v0.12.9 (pins 0.12.40;
sends no Lab operation; its forensics reads a Lab terminal record by its schema string only):
none refuses it. `ledger` stays [3, 6] and `runtime-client` [3, 6].

**Where it differs from the work order's letter.** The work order kept `input_returned` true and
had the validator, the verifier and the contract accept `not_performed` beside it; that
combination is one an earlier reader refuses (`invalid_lab_operation_record`, the lines above), so
it would have been an interface step. By the coordinator's decision the record states the
boundary of `input_returned` instead, and the validator and the verifier are unchanged.

**What changes live.** A Lab `do` (and `do --operation`) refused by the foreground check answers
`executed: false`, `effect: not_performed`, with its failure as before; `do --capture --record`
records nothing for it and returns the operation's error, as for any input that was not
performed. Task runs are unchanged (their effect never read this path).

**Rollback** (to 0.12.41). Nothing new persisted; 0.12.41 writes such a refusal `indeterminate`
again, and reads this build's records as failures before input.

### 1.284 Slice FS-3 (0.12.43): `confirm: "track"`, a select that finds its moving choice again on the confirmation frame (Workflow #404; the same request and design as §1.282, §2.3, §2.4, §2.6 and §3 row FS-3; coordinator work order `rd-1031/perf-407/brief-fs3.md`)

[selection-graph.md](selection-graph.md) (Select step, Execution, Confirming by tracking, Records),
[candidate-projection.md](candidate-projection.md) (Candidate-set hash, Generation step 7) and
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) (the `ledger` row of revision 7, the `package`
row of revision 7) are the contract. 1.284 was the next free number on the base `d478560c`.

**Why.** FS-1 and FS-2 (§1.282, §1.283) find every copy of a marker on the whole frame. A marker
that moves between the step's frame F1 and its confirmation frame F2 could still never be tapped:
both confirmations compare hashes that cover the click rectangles, so the move fails them.

the contract.

row "#404 FS-2b"). The FS-3 tests of §1.284 keep their names and now read `anchor_milli` in the
§2.2 tie-break (score descending, then candidate ID), through the gate and admission.

[3, 7]. No code, key or configuration key.

and the attestation stay in-process, and no record or receipt carries the new code yet.

`gpu_fallback` (design §1.2) and the spec carries it, so that slices B2 and D, which run side by
side, share one constructor. (b) `PinnedRuntimeFile::check` is here for the same reason: slice B1's
runtime initialisation and slice D's check-config both hash against the pin. (c) The tool sources
entries carry `pinned_files` (not `distributed_files`: actingd's adb pin reads the one component
with `distributed_files`), which the pin test compares. (d) The closure loader and its state are
`pub(crate)` so the closure test drives the loader itself.

**What changes live.** Nothing: no configuration selects DirectML, and no code path lists the
adapters or reads the pin yet.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.43). Nothing persisted; no configuration names `directml`.

### 1.287 Workflow #434 LAB-0 (0.12.x, before 1.00): the Lab and UI two-entry architecture, its ten slices and their order (Alice's words of 2026-11-08 in the coordinator window, 「…转发台下只分两种，一种就是来自 Lab，一种就是来自 UI。」, and her answers of 23:2x on board #434; design `rd-1108/arch-013/design-lab-ui.md` §5.5 with its §7, which wins, read on main `2ea50cf5`; coordinator work order `rd-1108/arch-013/brief-lab0.md`)

[lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) is the contract and [lab-operations.json](lab-operations.json)
the operation table v1; the planned revisions are in
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md), "Planned: Workflow #434". 1.287 was the next
free number on the base `2ea50cf5`; each later slice of #434 adds its rows under this section, as
GPU-1's slices do under §1.286.

**LAB-0 itself.** Contracts only: the two-entry contract, the operation table v1 (168 operations:
53 core, 28 debugging, 40 authoring, 47 rescue; 16 of them reserved; 170 since LAB-2 added the two
debugging rows `user-config` and `user-config set`, L2-10), the planned interface rows
and this section. No code, no test, no gate row, no CI file, no key, no code of the outcome
catalog, and no live revision raised.

**The ten slices** (design §5.5, with §7 applied; all in the 0.12 series, all before 1.00):

| Slice | Repository | Size | What | Depends on | Named tests | Interfaces |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

   LAB-6's merge commit first. So no window has actingctl present while the door refuses its `cli`
   binding.

4. All ten come before 1.00 (Alice, 11-08 22:5x: 「…给0.13版本仅留3D相关的支持，其余的全部在0.12系列完成。」,

   interface revisions of 1.00; UI-L2 leaves 1.00 one installer.

`runtime-outcomes` 1, declared [5, 27], [3, 7], [3, 6], [3, 7] and [1, 1] as before.

**Where LAB-0 differs from the design's letter.**

  (`touch-probe`, `recover`, `watch`, `release verify`, `release stage`, `adopt`, `prepare`, the

  operations for the UI list's #429 kinds (`task run`, `task stop`, `pack-schedule`,

  design's `request_kind` and `key`.
- (e) An authoring operation that is not installed is refused with actinglab's
  `lab_command_option_disabled`, not the host's `lab_module_not_installed`.
- (f) `config file commit`, `pack remove` and `pack restore` are irreversible too, as the same
  change as `config replace` and `place`.
- (g) `do`, `ensure` and `wait` are `optional` (they replay offline today), not §3.1's "必".
- (h) One operation per CLI form; LAB-5 decides how MCP presents a family (contract §13, open
  point 9).
- (i) The design's named tests predate §7: none checks that a failing guard no longer refuses, so
  LAB-3's work order names one.

- (d) MCP's `ac_config_set` and `ac_targets_set` now shape their answer with the CLI's one copy,
  which returns an encoder error where MCP's `json!` would have panicked; neither typed result can
  fail to encode, and MCP answers such an error as `ac_ladder_drill` does (`runtime`,
  `actingctl_output_failed`).

**What LAB-1b changes live.** Nothing a person or the Runtime sees.

**LAB-1b rollback** (to the release before it). Nothing persisted: code and the table's text.

the tick itself; the Runtime's `actingctl.exe` still answers `watchdog …` (actingctl's MCP

does not change: its name, its action `<root>\tools\actingwatch.exe` without arguments, its
working directory `<root>`, its trigger and its settings are what `install` registered.

actingwatch only runs `runtime\actingctl.exe`, takes no slot and speaks only through a command

subcommands attach to their parent's console (L4-7, L4-8;
[runtime-watchdog.md](runtime-watchdog.md), "Commands"). (5) The crate's developer lines go to
the sink each call names, with no default (L4-3); what actingctl and actingwatch print does not
change. (6) The table's `watchdog install` and `watchdog uninstall` rows are LAB-3's ((c)). No
test is added or changed: the sink is a parameter, so a call without one does not compile.

`state.json`, `watchdog.log` and the task are the same files.

**Outcome codes.** [runtime-outcomes.md](runtime-outcomes.md), "vocabularies" and G7: a
vocabulary's tokens equal its enum's, and a token is not an entry with a `since` of its own (G9
binds codes and locations); keys are append-only. So `guard_failed` is one token of the catalog
vocabulary `install_caveat` and one variant of `lab-ops`' `InstallCaveat`, and the pending code
`install_caveat_noted` takes the existing key `install_guards` as an optional value; no code and
no key is added. The vocabularies `install_operation_kind` (`config_replace`, `pack_place`) and
`install_step_kind` (`pack_item`) gain tokens the same way, with install-cli.md's registry. Six
locations of `actingctl` are added, pending, since 0.12.48: `install_deploy`,
`install_config_replace`, `install_alive`, `install_unlock`, `install_check_config`,
`install_ledger_verify`. Fix 1 adds, the same way, the token `hold_not_owned` to the vocabulary
`install_refusal` (one `InstallRefusal` variant), and the pending code `install_command_refused`
takes the existing key `hold_reason` as an optional value: no code and no key added. Fix 2 adds
no code, key or token: a `release-hold` with no Runtime answers the existing `runtime_not_running`,
and the `next` forms `actingctl_release_hold` and `actingctl_resume` are answer members. Fix 3
adds, the same way as `guard_failed`, the token `hold_ownership_unconfirmed` to the vocabulary
`install_caveat` (one `InstallCaveat` variant): the module could not read whether a hold is its
own (the reason does not parse, the root or its operations folder cannot be read), so `next`
leaves that `release-hold` out as before and the answer, or the composite step whose answer it
is, carries the note `install_caveat_noted` of `install_release_hold` with the read failure as
its cause; the pending code `install_caveat_noted` takes the existing key `hold_reason` as an
optional value: no code and no key added.

**Where LAB-3 differs from its work order's letter.**

- (a) The module is `crates/lab-rescue`, not `lab-ops` (L3-1); actinglab's CLI module serves its
  rows.
- (b) A request the module sends to a running Runtime stays on the CLI channel with the CLI
  envelope until LAB-6, not `lab` with the initiator: the Runtime refuses `PauseScheduling`,
  `ResumeScheduling` and `RequestShutdown` from a Lab envelope until LAB-6 deletes those origin
  gates (contract §2.4), and `BindChannel` takes no initiator before `runtime-client` 7. The
  journal records the initiator now.
- (c) A rescue row whose source command is not built is not served: `convert` (R-15e), `clean`
  (R-15d), `new` (INST-6), `prepare`, `config file …` (INST-3), `instance add` and `remove`
  (INST-5), `pack remove` and `restore`; the slice that builds the source opens the row. So
  `irreversible_journal_initiator` checks the journals of `deploy`, `rollback` and `config
  replace`, and that `clean` is not served. `mcp-config` and `mcp-entry list` are LAB-5's.
- (d) actinglab runs from `<root>\tools\` until LAB-7 moves it into the Runtime member (§7 says
  `runtime\`); `locate` takes both.
- (e) "Through MCP, `deploy`, `rollback` and `convert` always run detached" (§5) is LAB-5's: its
  tool passes `--detach`. A detached run carries the same initiator, so the module cannot decide
  it by the word without detaching again.
- (f) `deploy` without `--dir` deploys a kept build (a commit prefix of 8 hex digits or more, or a
  recorded tag); with `--dir` it passes the folder's `release-facts.json` when present. Without a
  running Runtime `deploy` and `rollback` apply the files only and start nothing (`up` starts).
- (g) `config replace` checks the file with the live build's check-config before anything
  changes, then stops; the swap is `stage_file` and `swap_file` steps, the replaced file kept as
  `actingd.config.json.prev-<ms>`; `config restore <prev>` is the same with a kept file.
- (h) `place` reuses the readers of `actingctl install`'s plan (`BundleIndex::validate`,
  `read_standard_pack_root`) and the `package` edge; fix 1 gives it its test
  (`place_holds_only_the_bundles_idle_instances`, a neutral bundle with made-up ids).
- (i) `watchdog install` still requires `<root>\runtime\actingctl.exe`, as LAB-4 (e).

**What LAB-3 changes live.** At the deploy that carries it, `actingctl.exe` answers `install`,
`start`, `restart`, `mcp-entry` and `agent-channel` from the moved code, the same way; the deploy
kit and the console are unchanged. `tools\actinglab.exe` offers the rescue rows, which act on the
root it lies in (there is no `--root`). Nothing runs them by itself. Until LAB-7 production keeps
deploying through `actingctl install` (the coordinator's deploy kit), not the module's `deploy`,
`rollback`, `place` or `config replace`: an installer of v0.12.47 or older does not read a journal
the module writes (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-10; no `install-root` raise). The module's
`release-hold` never hands back a pause it did not set, so Alice's `alice-116-scheduler-stop`
stays whatever is run.

**LAB-3 rollback** (to the release before it). actinglab no longer offers the rescue rows. A
journal the rescue module wrote does not decode in the older installer (`initiator`, `one_way`, the
kinds `config_replace` and `pack_place`): roll back only when no rescue operation is the last one
or unfinished, or finish it first.

  written `-`); (3) on an engine row, an undeclared flag after a global option given no value

#### Slice LAB-5D (0.12.52): the answer budget is the caller's, and the operation layer cuts or exports

Coordinator work order `rd-1108/arch-013/brief-lab5d.md`; the read-only surveys

and one new parameter: `actingctl mcp-serve` answers every call byte for byte as before (the same
cuts, `<block>_truncated` members, exports and warnings), and the CLI, the CLI module and
`serve --stdio` print the whole answer as before. A generated MCP server (LAB-5) has no place for
per-tool code, so the code that keeps an answer inside the budget now lives with the operations.

and `ac_perf_preset` (the row's name carries it; `force-stop` is `app stop`); `ac_remedy_set`'s

replaced by the optional `out`). Nothing reads `required_in` yet; §9.1 of the contract names

**Defaults and names that differ between today's MCP and the rows** (for the server's slice; none
changes here; from the survey's `difference` column, checked against main):

- `pause`: drain `drain_timeout_s` integer seconds 1 to 600, default 60 (MCP) against `drain`
  duration, default 300 s (row); reason default `mcp.pause` against `operator`.
- `run start`: `deadline_s` integer seconds 60 to 1800, default 1800, against `deadline` duration
  (1800 s when absent); `recovery_package` against `recovery`. A job against a waiting line:
  `ac_run_pack` answers `{handle, correlation_id, phase}` at once and submits in a job of its
  process; the row's line waits for the run's receipt, at most `wait` when given
  (`command_wait_expired`, naming the run).
- `emu start|stop|restart`: `ac_emulator` answers `{controlled}` within its 25 s call budget,
  otherwise `{handle, job_phase}` of a job of its process for `ac_get_run`; the row's line waits
  for `{controlled}`, at most `wait` when given.
- `run stop`: `ac_stop_run` sends only the stop through its live job when that MCP process
  submitted the run (that job lifts the touches), and otherwise waits for the end in a job of its
  process (`wait_s`, the front's); the row's line sends the stop and the reset and waits for them,
  up to the longest run deadline (`cancel_only`: the stop alone).
- `status`: `sections` an array of the block names (an `enum`) in MCP against a `list<string>`
  on the row, a comma list on the command line.
- `events`: `limit` 1 to 100 (MCP) against 1 to 256 (the command line), 20 when absent on both,
  though the row declares no `default` for it; `detail` default `brief` on both; `wait_s` 0 to 20
  on both (MCP's schema maximum is `events::MAX_WAIT_S`, 20); `after_sequence` against `after`,
  `event_types` an array against `type`, a `list<string>` (a comma list on the command line),
  `run_id` against `run`, `request_id` against `request`; `since_unix_ms` beside the row's
  `since`.
- `runs`: MCP's `since_unix_ms` (and `until_unix_ms`) are the row's too; the row's `since`, a
  duration back from now, stands beside it, not with it.
- `targets`: two MCP tools, `ac_resources_list` and `ac_targets_get`, against one row `targets`.
- `targets set`: MCP requires `targets` (inline); the row takes `file` or `targets`, exactly one.
- `run evidence`: `detail` default `full` on both; `limit` default 20, 100 with `summary`, on
  both; `handle` and `run_id` against one `id`. `run show`: `run_id` against `id`.
- `codes` and `runs`: `limit` default 20, 1 to 100, on both.
- `diagnose`: `task_id` against `task`; `since_unix_ms` beside the row's `since`.
- `observe`, `do`: `sample_scenes` and `scene` folded into one repeated `scene`, oldest first.
- `record mark`: `request` an object against `request_json` text.
- `facts`: `key_prefix` against `prefix`; `scope` against the switches `program` and `config` (and
  the row `config`). `summary`: `granularity` against the switches `hour` and `day`.
- `resume`: `expected_owner_epoch` and `expected_revision`, two required members, against one
  `expect` object `{owner_epoch, revision}` (`required_in: ["mcp"]`).
- `material`: `mode` (`text` or `export` into MCP's export directory) against `out`; `ac_observe`
  always exports its frame, `frame` only with `out`. `out` lets a caller of `serve` write where it
  names, as `frame --out` does; the MCP front keeps `out` for itself and passes its export
  directory.
- `config set`: `changes` objects `{key, value?}` (null clears) against `KEY=VALUE` words and the
  row `config clear`.
- `preset set`: `preset` against `name`. `devices bind|unbind`: `alias` against `instance` (an
  alias only, as noted). `resource catalog`: `server` against `catalog_server`. `evidence read`:

Global options a command reads through its flags are on its list (`--instance` of the record
actions and the env markers, `--dry-run` of `recover`, `tap-target` and `navigate`, `--game` and
`--server` of `record start` and the env markers, `--touch-backend` refused): actinglab's parser
takes them first, so these reads see nothing on the command line, and the command reads the global
option.

**The test-only recording** (`flag_args.rs`, module `reads`). A command declares its list where it
starts, right after it parses its flags (`FlagArgs::reading`; the dispatchers of `record`,
`package`, `operation` and `resource` by subcommand, before their first read; `package` and
`operation` through the test-only `hold_package_reads` and `hold_operation_reads` of
`lab_package_control.rs`). From then on every
read of those flags and of every copy of them (`bool`, `optional`, `values`, `count`, the new
`given`, and the readers built on them) is recorded on the reading thread (`reads::take`), and a
read of a name the list does not hold, or in the form the list does not give it (a switch read for
its value, an option read with `bool`), panics with the row and the name, failing the test. A
refused flag may be read in any form. Flags no command declared for (the global gates' own parse,
`FlagArgs::default()`, the helpers' tests) are not held. `FlagArgs::from_parts` builds flags the
code makes itself (the input relay's action, `resource verify`'s preflight); the struct literal is
gone. In the product build `FlagArgs` has no such field and reads as before.

**Fix round 1 (the command inventory guard).** `hold_package_reads` and `hold_operation_reads`
are functions of their own, not a test-only match in the dispatcher: the guard
`command_inventory_matches_checked_in_snapshot` takes the first match on the subcommand in a
group's dispatcher for its dispatch, and such a match read `package` with 5 of its 10
subcommands and `operation` with 3 of its 4 (94 commands, not 100). No command a person can type
moved; `ratchet/actinglab_commands.json` is unchanged.

**Work order point 4.** `FlagArgs::reading_forms(row)` holds a strict command to the forms the
register gives its flags (`own_flags::accepted`): a flag the register lists as taking a value read
with `bool`, or a switch read for its value, fails; a name off its list is left to the command's
own refusal. It is declared by `observe`, `do`, `ensure`, `wait` (checking `LAB2_SWITCHES`),
`package fmt` (`--check`) and `package loading` (`LOADING_SWITCHES`), so their existing tests
check those switch lists. `RECORD_MARK_SWITCHES` and `record stop --dry-run` cannot be checked so:
`record_flag_switch` reads a switch with `values`.

**The register.** `cli_module::own_flags::reads(row)` answers for exactly the lenient rows: the
list, its options, switches and refused flags, the option the first positional stands in for
(`tap-target` and `is-visible` `--target`, `locate` `--template`, `record candidates` and `record
amend` `--step-id`) and the count of positionals the code checks (exactly none for `touch-probe`,
`debug-package` and `export-evidence`; no count for the others, `recover --stale-capture` exactly
none on its own path only).

**Reads outside `FlagArgs`'s readers** (work order, fail loud). `package bundle`
(`--maintenance`, `--source-repository`, `--source-commit`, the root files) and `record amend`
(`--threshold`) asked the flag map itself whether a flag was given: they read it through the new
`FlagArgs::given` now, the same answer, so the recording sees it. `main.rs`'s
`record_flag_gate` and `retired_digest_flag_gate` read the raw words of every command line, to
refuse `--record` and `--tap-rect` outside their commands and the retired digest flags; they are
refusals common to every command and on no list. `refuse_repeated_options` and `record amend
--from-drift-diagnostics`'s own list (`reject_direct_drift_amend_flags`) look at every flag given,
by no name; that list lets `--holder`, `--lease-holder` and `--lease-id` through, which amend never
reads.

**Corrections of the table (work order point 6; the table follows the code).** Each makes the row
say what its command already reads; on the command line nothing changes (`recover` hands every
further flag on, and the record actions are actinglab's own words), and `serve --stdio` now takes

#### Slice LAB-5B4 (0.12.53): a flag a command does not read is refused; a switch does not swallow the next word

Coordinator work order `rd-1108/arch-013/brief-lab5b4.md`, on the coordinator's ruling of 11-11
(board #434, 6784514298 point 3; not Alice's words), after the read-only check
`rd-1111/audit-check/findings-rt-lab.md` §1 and §2. Built on LAB-5B3 (#1581) and merged with main
after it. The rule of LAB-5's earlier slices, that no command line changes what it accepts or
refuses, has one exception here, on purpose: this slice changes exactly three things, (1) a flag
an own command does not read is refused, (2) a switch takes no value from the next word but `true`
or `false`, (3) a positional a command does not read is refused; nothing else.

**What changed.**

- **The read lists are the product's** (`flag_args::reads::{FlagReads, ReadPart}`, no longer
  test-only; one list per command, no copy for tests). Each gains `positionals`: the positional
  words its command reads, in order, each of which may be absent (`<name>` any word, a bare name
  that word itself). The 24 lists of LAB-5B3, and four new ones for the own commands outside the
  table: `run_summary::RUN_LIST_READS` (`run list`), `commands/device_commands.rs` `CAPTURE_READS`
  (`capture`, `session capture`), `lab2_cli.rs` `RECEIPT_READS` and `EVIDENCE_READS` (`lab
  receipt`, `lab evidence`). A list's `row` is the command's name in its refusal (the row's name;
  the four commands' own words).
- **`FlagArgs::parse_reading(args, list)`** parses the command line of each of these 28 commands
  where it starts, before it reads or writes anything (the record actions' before their session
  directory is created; `package`'s, `operation`'s and `run`'s dispatchers through
  `package_flags`, `operation_flags` and `run_flags`, functions of their own so that the command
  inventory guard still reads each dispatcher's first match; `resource compile-maa` before
  `--repo` is read): a flag off the list is refused `unknown`; a switch of the list takes the next
  word only when it is `true` or `false`; an option takes the next word as before (none that
  begins with `--`) and at the end of the line is refused `value_missing`; a flag the list reads
  only to refuse it (`--via-daemon`, `--local`, `--state-dir`, `--touch-backend`, the readers'
  `--capture`) is read as before, for the command's own refusal; a positional beyond the list's,
  or other than the word it names, is refused `unknown`. In test builds the parse holds the flags
  to the list (LAB-5B3's recording); the explicit `reading` calls are gone.
- **The refusal** is the one the CLI module gives a row's short words (`cli_module::refused_word`,
  through `refused_words`): `validation_failed`, the message `<command>: <argument_problem>
  <word>`, the details `{argument, argument_problem}`; on actinglab's own line exit 1 and the
  developer line `ERROR actinglab: … <message>`, as `watch --frobnicate` prints; on a `--via`
  line the envelope's exit 2, as every `validation_failed`.
- **The strict commands that take switches** parse with `FlagArgs::parse_switches(args,
  switches)`: the switch rule only, their own refusals unchanged. Their switch lists are the code's
  constants (`lab2_cli::LAB2_SWITCHES`, `session_record::RECORD_MARK_SWITCHES` and
  `RECORD_STOP_SWITCHES`, `package_tool::FMT_SWITCHES`, `package_build::LOADING_SWITCHES`), which
  the register reads (`own_flags`; LAB-5B2's hand-written copies are gone). `record mark` and
  `record stop` keep reading their switches with `values` (`record_flag_switch`): `true` reads
  true, any other value they took is refused "takes no value", as before; a word after a switch is
  now a positional, which both refuse by their own check ("takes flags only"). Their refusal of an
  unknown flag is their own lists' (`RECORD_MARK_SHORTCUT_FLAGS`, `RECORD_MARK_REQUEST_FLAGS`,
  `RECORD_STOP_FLAGS`), unchanged; each switch of the two switch lists is on its command's flag
  list (checked by the slice's test), and the two lists hold every flag `record_flag_switch` reads
  (`--dry-run`, `--optional`, `--not-optional`, `--replace-click`, `--replace-transition`,
  `--no-anchor`, `--close-step` for mark; `--dry-run` for stop; by reading every call).
- **Positionals of the strict commands that counted none** (`FlagArgs::refuse_unread_positionals`,
  the same refusal): `observe` none, `do` `<target>`, `ensure` and `wait` `<page>`
  (`lab2_cli::*_POSITIONALS`), `package preflight`, `resource catalog`, `resource validate` none
  (`PREFLIGHT_POSITIONALS`, `CATALOG_POSITIONALS`, `VALIDATE_POSITIONALS`), each checked after the
  command's own flag refusal, so a line refused before keeps its refusal. Strict commands that
  checked an exact count (`tap`, `swipe`, `long-tap`, `key`, the commands with
  `expect_positionals(…, 0)`) keep their own refusal.
- **The short words**: `words::LENIENT_ON_COMMAND_LINE` is gone (the debt of "Slice LAB-5A"):
  `recover`, `debug-package` and `export-evidence` refuse an undeclared flag and a further word by
  name, as every row does. `lab_ops::core_ops::MORE_WORDS` stays (no row declares it and nothing
  writes it now; a call that carries it is refused); its doc says so.
- **The register** (`cli_module::own_flags`, tests only): `LENIENT_ROWS` is gone; its 24 rows are
  `READ_LIST_ROWS`, strict by their read list, and no kind is lenient. `reads(row)` gives their
  positionals from the list; `UNROWED_READS` lists the four commands outside the table;
  `accepted(row)` gives the positionals the verbs and the three strict commands now check and,
  `Accepted::first_positional`, the `--page` that `ensure` and `wait` read as their first
  positional.
- **`record amend --from-drift-diagnostics`** (the coordinator's ruling, handed on by LAB-5B3):
  `--holder`, `--lease-holder` and `--lease-id`, which its own pass list
  (`reject_direct_drift_amend_flags`) let through and amend never reads, are refused as every flag
  off amend's read list, and are gone from that pass list. No caller in this repository passes
  them to `record amend` (searched: only `record start` and MCP's `ac_record_start` pass
  `--holder` and `--lease-id`).
- **Left as they are** (the coordinator's ruling): `main.rs`'s `record_flag_gate` and
  `retired_digest_flag_gate`, which read the raw words of every command line, are on no list and
  run before the command, as before.
- **Contract**: `lab-two-entries.md` §9.3, a bullet "actinglab's own commands refuse a word they
  do not read" (the contract had no sentence that let them ignore one).

**Reads that rest on reading** (handed on by LAB-5B3): `recover`'s `--pack-root` and `--pages`
(with `--pack`) are now reached by a test (a planned recovery that reads them before it reads the
missing pack). The capture freshness of `recover`'s route and of `locate` (`--capture`,
`--require-fresh`, `--fresh-delay-ms`) and `navigate`'s step timing (`--step-timeout-ms`,
`--poll-ms`) are read only right before a capture or a press: after the route's resources and the
user configuration's device (an adb found on the host) are loaded, or, for `navigate`, after a
package and a frame are loaded and a live drive is built, so no command line of a test reaches
those reads without a device or a Runtime. Their lists hold them, read again for this slice
(`SCENE_READS`, `NAVIGATE_READS`), and the slice's test parses each list's line of them and reads
them in their commands' forms under the recording. No list missed a flag its command reads.

**What an operator sees after deploy.** A command line that passes a flag its command does not
read, or a word it does not read, is refused with `validation_failed` naming the word
(`<command>: unknown <word>`, exit 1; exit 2 on a `--via` line), where it was ignored; an option
left without a value at the end is refused `value_missing`. A switch followed by a word other than
`true` or `false` leaves the word as a positional: `observe --capture <alias>` is refused for its
positional (`--instance <alias>` names the instance), and `do --capture <target>`, `ensure
--capture <page>`, `wait --capture <page>` now run the capture path with that target or page. A
script that relied on an ignored flag fails loud; the table above lists an example per command.

`--require-fresh`).

**Pass-throughs** (point 2): none. No command of the work list hands its words to another program
or to a pack. Named for the coordinator: (i) `stream`'s input relay reads the words after
`--input-relay` or `--interactive-input` as its action's (`tap`, `swipe`, `long-tap`, `key`,
`text`), which checks its own count of words (the direct commands' strict check); its list takes
every word there by a new form of a list's last positional, a name ending in `...` (`<word>...`,
`flag_args::reads::takes_positional`), and without either flag `stream` reads no word but a first
`check` and refuses another. (ii) A line the global `--version` makes a version line (`cli_parse`:
`--version` anywhere hands the line's words to `version`) prints the version whatever its words, as
before; the words are the line's, not the command's. `version` typed as its own word refuses a word
(left as it is, for the coordinator to rule).

**Reads that rest on reading** (point 3). The work list's in-process tests (the corpus below, and
the existing `tests::session_status_without_runtime_is_exit_five` and
`stream_command_reports_bounded_dry_run_contract`) reach most
reads under the recording; the golden protocol (`lab run`, `lab validate`, `detect`, `env
resolve`, `env status`) and the integration tests with a Runtime (`session status --diagnostics`,
`session monitor-policy status|set|clear`, `session stream`, `session app`) run the binary, which

`gate_434_lab5b5::the_reads_that_rest_on_reading_are_on_their_lists` parses each list's line of them
and reads them in their commands' forms under the recording: `detect`'s past its scope (the task,

task, the input, the key): a line that passes the scope goes on to open the Lab's state folder
(`build_lab`), outside a test's temporary folder; `package run --out`, read after its package is
admitted; `session monitor-policy`'s (the instance, and `set`'s policy and frame): each action
connects to the Runtime after them, or refuses `--dry-run` before them. `session app`'s `--record`
is read among its words (`run_session_app_or_recorded`), not by a reader, as on main. No list missed
a flag its command reads.

**The repository's own lines** (point 4). Searched: the tests (`apps/actinglab/src/tests`,
`apps/actinglab/tests`), the goldens (`tests/golden/expected.json`, `consumers.json`) and the golden
harness's lines (`golden_protocol.rs`: the `lab validate`, `lab run`, `detect`, `env resolve`, `env

#### Slice LAB-5G4a (0.12.52): `serve --stdio --front mcp` records `Lab-MCP`; `serve` refuses values that begin with `--`

Coordinator work order `rd-1108/arch-013/brief-lab5g4a.md`, after the read-only survey
`rd-1108/arch-013/lab5g-step0-survey.md` (§2, on `5041d952`); the coordinator's rulings on board
#434: 6769399787 points 9 and 10 (an option only `serve --stdio` takes says that the front end is
MCP; the child then records `Lab-MCP` and binds on the wire as today's `--via mcp` child does,
until LAB-6; the variable's rule does not change) and 6775192250 point 16 (`serve` refuses values
that begin with `--`). On main `4116cbf4`, with LAB-5C (#1573) merged in before the tests. The
contract is [lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) §4.2, §4.3 and §8.2. G4a of the survey's
§10: nothing starts `serve` with the option until the MCP server's children (G4b).

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L5G4a-1 | `serve --stdio --front mcp` (`cli_module::serve::front`, `serve::Front`) | behaviour | LAB-5G4a | the MCP server's children (G4b) | without `--front` the words after `serve` are checked as before, byte for byte (only `--stdio`; its refusals and their texts, `serve::stdio_only`); with it, `--stdio` once and `--front mcp` once, in either order. Another value (`--front ui`: `argument` `ui`), the option twice and the option without `--stdio` (`argument` `--front`), and any other word, are `actingctl_usage_invalid` `unknown`, as `serve` refuses an unknown word; the option without a value is `value_missing` (deviation (a)). With the option, `ACTINGCOMMAND_INITIATOR` set to anything, an empty value too, is `actingctl_usage_invalid` with `variable` `ACTINGCOMMAND_INITIATOR`, before the installation and initiator check and before the loop. Each refusal is the one line `{outcome}`, exit 1, with its developer line, as `serve`'s refusals are. No other command and no row's words take the option |
| L5G4a-2 | the process's initiator under the option | behaviour | LAB-5G4a | — | the loop (`serve::serve_as`) hands the front end to `cli_module::answer`. A row actinglab's own command serves runs with its invocation's `via` set to `mcp` (`engine::line`), as the line of MCP's `--via mcp` child sets it, so `cli_module::recording_initiator` gives `Lab-MCP` on each step and mark the command adds (`record start\|mark\|step\|stop\|amend`, and `--record` where a row passes it); a rescue row (Windows) is answered with `Initiator::LabMcp` (`cli_module::rescue::answer`), so its journal carries `Lab-MCP`. The line stays the CLI module's (`own_line::exit`): the envelope is printed only on `main`'s path for a command line with `--via` (since LAB-5G4b each line under the option is carried in `{exit_code, req_id?, line}`, "Slice LAB-5G4b", L5G4b-6). `recording_initiator` and `Initiator::of_lab_process` are main's: `ACTINGCOMMAND_INITIATOR=Lab-MCP` stays refused (§4.2) |

Without the option it stays unset, as on main |

Numbers, booleans, objects and strings that begin with one dash pass. It holds for every row whichever code serves it (`core_ops`, the rescue module, actinglab's own commands), since the loop reads the line before any of them. The command line (`words::parse`) does not change |

**The problem chosen** (the work order asks which and why): `not_recognised`, "text that is none
of the spellings or forms it may take", which main gives text of a form its parameter does not
take (the command line's words for a word outside an `enum`; the operation layer for `gap --why`
with a control character). The value is a string, so `wrong_type` ("not of the type it must
have") would say something untrue, and it is given, so `value_missing`, which the command line
answers when a word that begins with `--` follows an option (LAB-5A fix 1), would too; today's
MCP server refuses the same value with the same problem (`apps/actingctl/src/mcp/lab.rs`,
`not_a_flag`), so a client of the new server sees what it sees today.

**Tests.** New: apps row "#434 LAB-5G4a": `gate_434_lab5g4a::serve_front_mcp_records_lab_mcp` and
`gate_434_lab5g4a::serve_refuses_values_that_begin_with_two_dashes` (actinglab's binary tests; an
empty configuration and a recording folder in a temporary folder; no Runtime, no device, no clock,
no sleep). The loop is driven with a front end through `serve::serve_as`; `serve::serve`, which
LAB-2's and LAB-2b's tests drive, is now that loop without one, compiled for tests only. No
existing test changed.

**Interface.** None raised: `Lab-MCP` is already one of the recording's and the journal's words
(§4.1); no code, key, location, record or vocabulary token is added, and `actingctl_usage_invalid`
with `argument`, `argument_problem` and `variable` is main's.

**Where LAB-5G4a differs from its work order's letter.**

- (a) The option without a value is refused `value_missing`, the module's problem for a flag
  without its value; the work order names no problem for it. The option is taken before or after
  `--stdio`.
- (b) "The connection the process binds": the core rows `lab-ops` serves connect through
  `lab_ops::front::client_config` as without the option (the Lab channel, no `via`). Today's
  `--via mcp` child serves none of them (its command line is actinglab's own), so it binds no such
  connection to copy, and the MCP server serves them in its own process (the survey's §2).
- (c) Found, not changed: a rescue row run with `--detach` under the option starts its detached
  run with `ACTINGCOMMAND_INITIATOR=Lab-MCP` (`rescue::detach`, `install::host::detach_with_wmi`
  give a detached run the initiator through the variable), which that run refuses by §4.2's rule;
  the caller gets `detached: true` and the run's log the refusal. The same holds wherever the rescue
  module runs with `Lab-MCP`, as the survey plans for the MCP server's own process (`deploy` and
  `rollback` detached through MCP, §5). How a detached run carries `Lab-MCP` is for the server's
  slices; nothing starts `serve --front mcp` yet.

**What LAB-5G4a changes live.** Nothing a person or a client sees: nothing starts `serve` with
`--front mcp` yet. `serve --stdio` refuses a string value that begins with `--`, which before
reached the row's command as a flag. The command line and today's MCP server do not change.

**LAB-5G4a rollback** (to the release before it). Nothing persisted that an older build cannot
read: a recording or journal written under the option carries `Lab-MCP`, one of the six words.

#### Slice LAB-5E (0.12.52): every offered row says in one sentence what it does

Coordinator work order `rd-1108/arch-013/brief-lab5e.md`, after the read-only surveys
`rd-1108/arch-013/lab5a-step0-survey.md` §7 and `rd-1108/arch-013/lab5g-step0-survey.md` §1 and
§6; on main `39c0c935`. The coordinator's ruling (board #434, 6769399787, point 13): the rules that
hold for every tool are written once, in the MCP server's instructions (a later slice); each row
gets one short sentence of its own, optional in the schema, shared by the command line's help and
the MCP description; long usage goes to the manual. The contract is
[lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) §9.1 and §9.2. No command prints anything new.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L5E-1 | the operation's member `help` (string, optional) | contract table, reader | LAB-5E | — | `table::Operation::help` and `table::MAX_HELP_BYTES` (160); the reader takes it and refuses nothing it took before; in the file on its own line directly before the row's `output`, away from the lines other slices change (`module`, `params`) |
| L5E-2 | one sentence on every offered row | contract table text | LAB-5E | — | 138 rows: core 45, debugging 26, authoring 36, rescue 31 (every row actinglab offers, `words::offered`, the rescue module's 29 on Windows, where it runs, and the three planned rows of slice LAB-5 that LAB-5's server offers itself: `record draft`, `mcp config`, `mcp entries`); 13,624 bytes in all, the longest 139 (`status`). A row no program offers (reserved, or planned and not served) has none |

**The rules of a sentence** (the work order's point 2, now §9.1's): English, plain ASCII, at most
160 bytes, one sentence or two short ones, beginning with a verb in the third person ("Reads…",
"Pauses…", "Lists…"); it says what the operation does and on what and, where a caller must know it
to use the row at all, what comes back or what to call next ("…; run evidence pages what it did
step by step"); no rule every row shares (budgets, handles in general, exports, cursors, what
`irreversible` means: the instructions); no MCP tool name (`ac_…`; a row is named by its words); no
game word; no path of a machine; nothing the row's parameters already say. Sources: the row's
`output`, `notes`, `source` and parameters, the code that serves it, and the description of the
MCP tool it replaces (`apps/actingctl/src/mcp/tools.rs` and the tools' files), whose first sentence
was usually kept.

**Where today's MCP description and the code disagreed** (the code won; no row's other members
change):

- `pause`: `ac_pause` answers `{paused, owner_epoch}` and names them for `ac_resume`; the row's line
  answers the Runtime's result without `owner_epoch` (`core_ops`, `pause`). The sentence names no
  answer member.
- `resume`: `ac_resume` lifts only the pause the caller read; the row without `expect` lifts the
  scope's pause, whatever it is. The sentence says the scope's pause.
- `run start`: `ac_run_pack` answers a handle at once; the row's line waits for the run's receipt.
  The sentence says the receipt.
- `frame`: `ac_observe` always exports the frame; the row answers its material ref and writes a
  file only with `out`. The sentence says the ref.

Two rows whose `output` and code differ, without an MCP tool: `monitor set|clear` answer the
instance's monitor status (`configure::set_monitor`, `configure::clear_monitor`), where `output`
says the policy; `run show` answers the run's status without steps (`run_show::answer`, as its
notes say), where `output` names steps. Each sentence follows the code; `output` is left as it is.

**Where the command line could show it later** (not decided here): `command_cap`
(`apps/actinglab/src/commands/capabilities.rs`) builds each entry of `command_capabilities()`, the
list that `help` (`cli_information::help_data`), `list commands` (`cli_information::run_list`) and
`capabilities` (`capabilities::run_capabilities`) print. The table's rows have no entry there today
(the CLI module's refusal names the table, `cli_module::USAGE`); an entry could take its row's
`help`, or the offered rows could gain entries of their own. `actinglab help`, `list commands`,
`capabilities` and every row's line print byte for byte what they printed.

**Readers of the table.** Only `crates/lab-ops`' reader parses it (`table::operation_table`, the
embedded copy, and `table::read_operation_table`): actinglab's CLI module (`cli_module::table`,
`words`, `serve`) and the tests of `lab-ops` and actinglab use its rows; the neutrality guard reads
the file as text. None refuses the member. The console's repository reads its own pinned copy: a
strict reader there must accept `help` when it next raises its pin.

**Tests.** Changed: `lab_ops_table_complete` (LAB-1) also checks every `help`: ASCII, 1 to
`MAX_HELP_BYTES` bytes on one line (no control character), no `ac_`, no two rows alike; the
requirement it pins grows by the work order's point 3. New: apps row "#434 LAB-5E",
`gate_434_lab5e::lab5e_offered_rows_have_help` (actinglab's binary tests; the embedded table only):
every row actinglab offers and every planned row of slice LAB-5 has a `help` that is not blank. The
neutrality guard's words: no test of `lab-ops` or actinglab can reach its list (neither depends on
`tools/actinglab-architecture`, and a copy of its words in a guarded crate would trip the guard), so
the guard's own test `c2_runtime_code_contracts_defaults_and_fixtures_are_project_neutral`, which
reads `contracts/lab-operations.json` line by line, checks each sentence on its own line.

**Interface.** None raised: an optional member; the schema string stays; no code, key, location or
vocabulary token is added.

**What LAB-5E changes live.** Nothing a person, a client or the Runtime sees; nothing reads `help`
yet but the table's tests.

**LAB-5E rollback** (to the release before it). Nothing persisted: code and the table's text.

| L5G1-3 | `lab_ops::front::Connection` (`Connect(Front)`: a connection made for the call as that front connects, `front::config`; `Kept(&RuntimeClient)`: the caller's), `Connection::per_call` (`Connect(current())`), `Connection::reach`, `Reached` (`Made`, `Kept`; `Deref` to the client, `into_client`), `front::config(front, state_root)` | new type | LAB-5G1 | `core_ops` | the connection input. Every row that reads the Runtime takes it, each of the three ways: the words of a command of `lab-ops` (`dispatch_on` of `overview`, `diagnose`, `events`, `run_list`, `run_evidence`, `remedy` with `dispatch_rows_on`, `routine_summary`, `perf_preset`, `evidence_read`, `observe_export`; each `dispatch` is its `dispatch_on` with `Connection::per_call()`, so actingctl is unchanged) and the parameters read on a client. `codes`, `gap`, `packs` and `devices` read no Runtime. A kept connection is used as it is: a detail `ACTINGCOMMAND_DETAIL` asks for is the caller's to set on it |

**What stayed in actinglab, and why.** The place of the program (`cli_module/place.rs`: the root
from its own place, the state root from the selected configuration or
`ACTINGCOMMAND_RUNTIME_STATE_ROOT`), its developer text and `lab_operation_completed`: they are
actinglab's, and are given as `Caller`. The words (`words.rs`: the short words, `serve`'s JSON,
`offered`, the kept flags), the routing (`cli_module::route` and `answer`), the engine of
actinglab's own commands (`engine.rs`, `own_line.rs`), `serve`'s loop and the printing.
`cli_module::core_ops` is now a small module of `cli_module.rs`: `answer` calls the moved code
with `caller()` (connected per call as the program in force, as before), and for LAB-5C's test it
re-exports the names that test reads.

**A row a kept connection does not serve as a connection made for the call does.** `shutdown
--wait` closed its connection before it waited for the Runtime to end (`shutdown::wait`); on a kept
connection it drops only a clone, and the caller's connection stays open while the wait reads the
shutdown. Served so, not reconnected; the server's slice decides whether its front closes its
connection first. **What one call leaves on a kept connection for the next:**

- The client holds the connection for each whole exchange, so on a kept connection a long exchange
  blocks every other call that shares it: `run start` until its receipt, `run stop` without
  `--cancel-only` up to the longest deadline a run may have, and a `--wait` that expired and left
  its worker waiting for the receipt on a clone of the connection.
- A failed exchange leaves the connection answering that failure to every later call.
- So a caller that keeps connections (the MCP server) gives each write its own connection and drops
  a connection after a failure, as today's MCP server does (`apps/actingctl/src/mcp/operator.rs`,
  `begin_write`; `runtime.rs`, `connect_fresh` and `failure`). With a connection made for each
  call, which is all actinglab uses, none of this arises.

**Left for the second slice** (the work order's cut): the budget (`Option<&Budget>` into `answer`
and the steps of the eleven reads that shape, the line carrying `Fitted.exported` as a warning);
the cursor binding (`CursorBinding` into `events` and `diagnose`'s errors page, actinglab passing a
fresh one; `runs`' and `codes`' cursors bind to no session today, each carries its own position and
query fingerprint, so a binding there would change what actinglab prints and takes: a ruling is
needed); the MCP front (`Front::Mcp`: channel `mcp`, envelope (Cli, Cli), and the test that it
equals the configuration `apps/actingctl/src/mcp/runtime.rs` builds). **Rows without answer
shaping** (for the server's slice to bound): every row of `core_ops` but `status`, `diagnose`,
`events`, `schedule`, `runs`, `run evidence`, `codes` (cut), `facts` (whose read `config` shares),
`packs`, `remedy` (the read, MCP's `ac_remedy_get`; `remedy set|lift` have none) and `summary`
(export). The second slice must also settle:

- `Caller.completed`: the code `lab_operation_completed` is actinglab's own
  (`apps/actinglab/src/codes.rs`), so another program cannot build it today; a registry decision.
- A caller must refuse the members a row does not declare itself, as actinglab's words do; the
  moved code does not refuse them on every row.
- `status` answers `watchdog: null` unless the caller sets the watchdog block
  (`overview::set_watchdog_block`), as actinglab does on Windows.
- Relative paths in parameters resolve against the caller's current directory.

**Tests.** New: apps row "#434 LAB-5G1" (`gate_434_lab5g1` in actinglab's binary tests, against the
runtime client's scripted Runtime, `test_support::ScriptedRuntime`; no device, no clock, no sleep):
`lab5g1_three_ways_serve_on_a_kept_connection` (`codes`, `events`, `resume`) and
`lab5g1_debugging_rows_serve_on_a_kept_connection` (`run start` and `reset` refused by the Runtime,
`run stop --cancel-only`, `drill`): the moved code on a kept connection answers the line and exit
code the CLI module prints for the same words, the request and correlation ids each run issues
masked; both connections carry the same requests after their handshake (`codes` none); no other
connection is made. No existing test changed: `gate_434_lab5c` reads `core_ops::offline_words`,
`handed_words`, `material_read`, `MaterialRead` and `material_written` through actinglab's
`cli_module::core_ops` as before; `gate_434_lab2`, `gate_434_lab2b`, `gate_434_lab5a`,
`gate_434_lab5d` and `lab_ops_table_complete` are untouched.

**Interface.** None raised: nothing on the wire, in the ledger or in a file changes; no code, key,
location or revision is added.

**What LAB-5G1 changes live.** Nothing a person, a client or the Runtime sees.

**LAB-5G1 rollback** (to the release before it). Nothing persisted: code only.

**What an operator sees after deploy** (since fix 2). The authoring operations are served
everywhere, inside an installation root or outside any, whatever the key says: recording, package
and resource checks and the other authoring operations run through the installed actinglab (also
by today's MCP author tools, which start it). They are listed (`help`, `list commands`,
`capabilities`) only with the key: outside any root, or inside one whose selected configuration
says `lab_module_authoring: true`. Production's key is true, so nothing a person or a client sees
changes there. On an installation without the key the authoring rows are not listed in `help` and
still run; where its configuration cannot be read, a listing says so on its developer line.
`standard-pack check`, a core row since fix 1, is listed and served everywhere. To list the
module, the selected configuration gets `"lab_module_authoring": true` (the installer's Lab page;
until the rescue module's writers exist, through the configuration replace the deploy uses); it is
read at the next listing, no restart needed. An unpacked Tools package outside any root is
unaffected.

2026-11-11). The rescue module's `place` (and `actingctl install pack place`, the same code,
`crates/lab-rescue/src/install/place.rs`) runs `<root>\tools\actinglab.exe --json standard-pack
check --root <game root>` as its post-check, and an installation without the authoring module must
still place packages (§8.1: the authoring module is detachable, the rescue module part of the Lab
core). So the row's `module` is `core` (L5F-7): it is always listed and served, whatever the key
says, and 34 rows are listed by the key (L5F-4); `standard-pack compose` stays an authoring row.
`place.rs`'s post-check needs no change: its command line is that row's, and since fix 2 nothing
stands before any command (L5F-2), so the check reaches its command wherever the root's key
stands.
Nothing else of the rescue or core module starts actinglab with an authoring row: the rescue
module's other children are actingd (`unlock`) and, for `--detach`, its own rescue row run again;
`lab-ops`' `app launch|restart|stop` run actinglab's `session app`, a core row's command (MCP's
author tools, in actingctl's MCP front, start actinglab with authoring rows, as "What an operator
sees after deploy" says). The debugging
and core lines that add to a recording (`do --capture --record`, `capture --record`, `session app
--record`) are listed everywhere; they need a recording `record start` began.

not offered, and `actingctl install config lab-options` is documented with its codes registered

#### Slice LAB-5G5a (0.12.57): the MCP entry's second generation is a second program, `actingcommand-mcp-entry-g2`, that starts `actinglab-mcp.exe`

Coordinator work orders `rd-1112/brief-lab5g5a.md` and `rd-1112/brief-lab5g-common.md`, after the
read-only survey `rd-1108/arch-013/lab5g-step0-survey.md` (§7 and §8, on `5041d952`) and the
read-only survey of 2026-11-12 of how a deploy places the entry (`rd-1112/agent-report-lab5g5a-step0.txt`,
on `dffd6263`); on main `dffd6263`. The contract is [install-cli.md](install-cli.md), "The MCP
entry", and [lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) §8.1.

**The ruling** (the coordinator's of 2026-11-12 on board #434, not the owner's words; it replaces
ruling 6 of 6775192250, "the entry in the repository becomes generation 2 and the placed g1 is never
touched"): the second generation is a **second program with its own file name**. `apps/mcp-entry`
and the file `actingcommand-mcp-entry.exe` stay byte for byte generation 1 (child
`actingctl mcp-serve`, plan `actingctl mcp-entry plan --entry-protocol 1`), and the bytes at
`tools\actingcommand-mcp-entry.exe` are generation 1 in every build; generation 2 goes only into
`mcp-entry\g2\`, never into `g1\`; `actingctl mcp-serve` and `mcp-entry plan --entry-protocol 1`
stay until the slice that removes actingctl, after the owner's registrations have moved. **Its
reason** (the survey of 11-12): no code of the installer writes under `<root>\mcp-entry\` (a deploy's
file plan covers `tools\` and `runtime\` only); placing `g1` is a copy of
`tools\actingcommand-mcp-entry.exe` by hand, as install-cli.md and the release notes of every
earlier build say. Had that Tools file become generation 2, a person or a script following those
documents would put generation 2 into `g1\`, where the registered words (`mcp-serve --tier …`)
would reach a server that refuses tiers, and a rollback would make one file name mean two
generations.

The index is regenerated |

**What the entry reads of the plan's answer** (for LAB-5G5b, which builds the row `mcp plan` to
it; the answer is the CLI module's `--json` line, the members at its top level):

- `entry_protocol`: an unsigned integer that must be 2; any other value, or none, makes the whole
  answer a refusal (no build taken, no switch, the doubling wait of a refusal).
- `switch`: a boolean, whether the installed build differs from the `--current-build` given.
- `build`: `{commit, manifest_sha256}`, both strings; other members are not read. `commit` is the
  build the status file records for the child, and compared with the next plan's.
- `child`: an array whose first element is a string, the path of the server program to start for
  a switch (found as L5G5a-3 finds it); later elements are not read, and the entry's own words
  follow it.
- `tunables`: `{poll_ms, settle_ms, verify_timeout_ms, drain_max_ms, refused_retry_max_ms}`, five
  unsigned integers (`install.mcp_entry.*`); read from a refusal too, which then sets the wait.
- `outcome`: any value, kept as the status file's `last_plan.outcome`.
- Not read: `reason`, and every other member. Any of the first five missing or of another type
  makes the answer a refusal, as in the first generation.

**Today's reader of the status files** (`crates/lab-rescue/src/install/mcp_entry.rs`, `list_with`,
read only): it lists every `entry-*.json` of `mcp-entry\state\` as JSON, judges only `pid`,
`process_created_at_unix_ms` and `started_at_unix_ms` (the same members the second generation
writes), and prints the rest as `status`; it checks neither `schema_version` nor
`entry_generation`. So a file of generation 2 is listed beside generation 1's, neither refused nor
misread; the reader is not changed.

**Left for later slices.** The rescue row `mcp plan` and the second generation's registration
snippet (`mcp config`) are LAB-5G5b's. Packaging (the build's `--bin` and `$toolFiles`, the exact
Tools file list of `scripts/windows-tools/`, which an older copy refuses an extra file by, and the
installer's fixtures) is LAB-5G6's, as is the installer's side: its reconnect notice counts running
entries by the first program's image name (`install/plan.rs`), and a running `actinglab-mcp.exe`
under the root blocks a deploy that replaces it (the survey's §7, the coordinator's ruling 5).
Placing the program in `g2\` is a manual step until an installer step exists, which creates under
`g2\` only.

**Tests.** New: apps row "#434 LAB-5G5a". The first generation's logic tests, copied with the
package and adapted to it (`src/tests.rs`: E-1 to E-11, E-13, E-14, E-16, E-18 to E-25; its child,
the server's words and tool names, a plan of protocol 2, its codes and inspect list, generation 2
in E-11), and five new ones: `mcp_entry_g2_child` (the register's named test, LAB-5 row above:
`runtime\` then `tools\`, looked for again at each fresh start, the words after `--` unchanged),
`g2_client_is_kept_and_the_other_words_pass_unchanged`, `g2_watched_files_are_the_manifest_and_the_server`,
`g2_the_plan_is_asked_of_actinglab_with_protocol_2` and `g2_the_plan_answer_is_read_for_protocol_2_only`;
the process test, copied and adapted (`tests/entry_process.rs`,
`mcp_entry_g2_process_pipes_a_session_and_switches_once`: the real binary with the fake as
`tools\actinglab-mcp.exe` and `tools\actinglab.exe` of a temporary root prints generation 2, gives
the server the words after `--` and not `--client`, writes a status file of generation 2 and
switches once). No existing test changed: the first generation's tests run unchanged.

**Interface.** None raised: `entry_protocol` 2 is the contract between the second program and the
plan row LAB-5G5b builds, not a declared interface; the status file keeps its place, name, schema
and members; three codes in the catalog only (`runtime-outcomes` stays 1). Nothing on the wire, in
the ledger or in a file a released peer reads changes.

**What LAB-5G5a changes live.** Nothing: the program is built and tested in CI and is in no release
or Tools archive until LAB-5G6; the placed first-generation entry and every registration keep

**LAB-5G5a rollback** (to the release before it). Nothing persisted: a status file the program

**Where the new server records and today's tool for the same operation does not, and the
reverse** (for the coordinator to decide; none smoothed over):

- New records, today's MCP server has no tool for the operation: `remedy lift`, `config clear`,
  `monitor set`, `monitor clear`, `offset`, `facts publish`, `emu selfcheck`, `shutdown`,
  `wake-test`, `task stop`, `pack-schedule set` and `reset` (each: the card and the client action).
- New records more than today's tool: `targets set` (`ac_targets_set`) and `remedy set`
  (`ac_remedy_set`) record the client action on an (Agent, Adapter) connection without the card
  today; the new server sends the card too, on (Cli, Cli). `evidence read`
  (`ac_evidence_confirm_read`) records no provenance today (its operation is a client action of
  its own, on (Agent, Adapter)); the new server sends the card and a client action `ac_evidence_read`
  before it, on (Cli, Cli).
- The same records with other values: `control_id` is the new tool's name, so it differs where the
  tool is renamed (`run start` `ac_run_start` for `ac_run_pack`, `run stop` `ac_run_stop` for
  `ac_stop_run`, `emu start|stop|restart` `ac_emu_*` for `ac_emulator`, `drill` `ac_drill` for
  `ac_ladder_drill`, `preset set` `ac_preset_set` for `ac_perf_preset`); `run stop` names no
  instance (the row has no instance parameter), where today's tool names the run's. `pause`,
  `resume`, `config set` record as today (`mcp_write_provenance_as_todays_server` holds `pause`).
- Requests: a write that names an instance reads the status twice (once on the kept connection
  for the client action, once on its own connection by the serving code, which resolves the
  instance itself); today's tools read it once.
- Today records and the new server does not: none among the served rows. The Lab tools' client
  action after a capture (ruling 12) belongs to rows this slice refuses.
- The warning of a refused card: today's `mcp_identity_card_refused` (with `mcp_blocker`) is
  `mcp_identity_declaration_refused` here (L5G2b-11); what follows it is the same.

**Rows that can take longer than 25 s** (each answers when it is done; they wait for G3's jobs):
`run start` (see below), `run stop` without `cancel_only` (the cancellation and the reset, up to
the longest run deadline), `pause` of an instance (its drain, `drain`, default 300 s), `emu
start|stop|restart` (the Runtime's control; with `wait` up to it), `task stop` and `shutdown` with
`wait`, `frame` and `material` with `export` (the whole read's 60 s budget), `frames` (its count
and interval), `events` with `wait_s`. **`run start` served this way**: without `wait` the call returns at the run's receipt
(`run_contained_task`, after the run, up to its deadline, by default the longest a run may have),
answering `task_run_reported` with the receipt, or the receipt's own outcome, `isError`, when the
run did not complete; with `wait` it returns after at most that long with `command_wait_expired`
and the run's `request_id`, the run going on (its submission keeps the write's connection until
the receipt). No handle is answered.

**Rows without answer shaping that can exceed the budget** (answered in `structuredContent` beside
a summary text, or `output_budget_exceeded`): `targets` (an instance's resource-target view) and
`pack-schedule` (one row per task package of an instance) on a large catalog; `discover` near the
most instances a status holds. `material`'s text is at most 8 KiB and fits.

**Point 10, a line over the budget after its work was done.** Chosen: the call still answers
`output_budget_exceeded` with `actual_bytes` and `limit_bytes`, and beside the outcome the member
`handle`, its job's; the job keeps the line unread, so it counts for the MCP entry; `ac_run_show`
of the handle answers the same refusal with `job_phase` and `summary` (`budget::job_summary`:
`{outcome, members, warnings_total, truncated?}`, the line's own outcome, the names of its other
members, how many warnings it carries and what the serving code cut), and the job is read. Why:
the work was done and must not look undone or be lost: the summary carries the line's own outcome
(whether a write succeeded) and says what the line held; nothing is cut and nothing is sent over
the limit; no code, key or value is added, and the line is written nowhere (the exports stay the
shaping rows').

**At the end of input** (stdin EOF): today's 2 s grace for answers in flight, then the process
ends; jobs are not waited for. A run's job ends with the process, the run going on in the Runtime
as with today's server: its request id, its handle, still reads it (`ac_run_show` of another
server process, `actinglab run show`). Any other job ends with the process and its handle with
it; whether a write it was sending was performed is read from the Runtime before anything is sent
again.

**What an operator and a client see (the second part).** A client calling `ac_lab_observe` or
`ac_do` with `capture` gets the child's line, and the Runtime's ledger holds, after the Lab
request, one `client.action` from (Cli, Cli) on the MCP channel naming the tool, the instance and
the Lab request's id, preceded by the identity card's declaration, as after today's server's
`ac_lab_observe` and `ac_lab_do`; a warning of the line says when the action carries no request id
or was not recorded. A client whose `ac_record_stop`, `ac_lab_observe` or `ac_do` answer is past
the budget gets `{req_id, export, overflowed: true}` with the parts it needs inline (the binding
snippets; the frame's coordinates and files) and `answer_exported` naming the file, which it reads
whole from `%TEMP%\actingcommand-mcp\materials` (the directory today's server writes to); any
other row a child serves exports its success the same way, without parts. An operator sees those
files in that directory, content-addressed, beside today's server's.

**Tests (the second part).** New, apps row "#434 LAB-5G4b, second part", in `tests/serve_calls.rs`
beside the first part's (outside `tests/gate/`), over pipes with this package's made-up `actinglab`
(`src/test_child.rs`), which now answers a request whose `instance` is `<key>` with the envelope a
test wrote as `answer-<key>.json` in its log folder (its line, exit code and request id):
`mcp_lab_overflow_rule` (the server's exports in a temporary folder through `TMP`, `TEMP` and
`TMPDIR`): `ac_record_stop`'s line of some 20 KB is written whole (the file holds the child's
line, its SHA-256 and size as the reference says, in the export directory) and answered
`{req_id: null, export, overflowed: true, lab, warnings, outcome}`, `lab` the four binding parts,
`answer_exported` first naming the file and the child's own warning after it; `ac_lab_observe`'s
keeps `frame_coordinates`, `frame_path` and `after_attachment` in order, its 12 KB `preview` left
out, `req_id` the envelope's; `ac_do`'s keeps the four frame parts in order; a failure line of
some 16 KB is sent whole in `structuredContent` alone beside a summary, no file written; with a
file where the export directory would be, no `export`, `material_export_failed` first, the binding
parts kept. `mcp_capture_records_client_action` (a scripted Runtime): `ac_lab_observe` with
`capture` and a request id, `ac_do` with `capture` and none, `ac_do` whose client action the
Runtime denies, `ac_lab_observe` without `capture`, `ac_do` with `capture` false, and `ac_do` with
`capture` and `dry_run`: four connections, each `health`, `bind_channel`, the identity card and
the client action alone (surface `mcp`, the tool, kind `command`, the instance, the request id as
its value or none), from (Cli, Cli); the lines are the child's, with
`client_action_without_req_id`, and `client_action_not_recorded` caused by the denial (the answer
standing), where they belong; each Lab command reached the child once. No existing test changes.

**Interface (the second part).** None raised: the ledger receives the records today's server
writes after a capture; the files are written where today's server writes its exports; no code,
key, location or vocabulary token is added, and no catalog text changes.

**Where the second part differs from its work order's letter.**

- (g) The client action's `control_id` is the tool called: `ac_lab_observe`, and `ac_do` where
  today's server names `ac_lab_do`, as every write's client action has named this server's tool
  since LAB-5G2b (`runtime::begin_write`).
- (h) The export holds the child's line as it gave it; the answer's warnings, and the measure,
  take the line with the client action's warnings joined (today's export holds the envelope's
  `data` and the job's warnings stay beside it).
- (i) On a failure line the client action's warnings join its `warnings`, as a write's provenance
  warnings join its line since LAB-5G2b, where today's server makes them `note` links of the
  error.
- (j) An envelope whose `line` is no JSON object is no envelope (L5G4b-13), a tightening of the
  first part.

**What LAB-5G4b changes live.** Nothing a person or a client sees: no registration starts the
program until G7. A deployed `actinglab serve --stdio --front mcp` answers the envelope, which
nothing starts.

**LAB-5G4b rollback** (to the release before it). Nothing persisted: the children live in the
server's memory, and each served row writes what the command line would.

**How a read outside a constant fails in CI** (point 1): a debug assertion in the one reader,
`Params::get`/`contains_key`. Not LAB-5B3/5B4's recording: that mechanism holds an own command's
flags (`flag_args::FlagArgs`, in actinglab), which `lab-ops` cannot reach, and a `cfg(test)`
recording in `lab-ops` would be off while actinglab's and actinglab-mcp's tests run this code; the
debug assertion is on in every test build that reaches it. The shape is theirs: one list per row,
used by the code, a read outside it failing with the row and the name. The CI jobs that run these
tests build with debug assertions: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo test` without
`--release` or `--profile` in `host-lab` (lab-ops, actinglab) and `apps` (actinglab-mcp); the
workspace `Cargo.toml` has no `[profile.*]` section and the repository no `.cargo/config.toml`; the
only profile variable set is `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG` (debug information). The test profile
inherits the dev profile, whose debug assertions are on; `lab_ops_a_read_outside_its_constant_fails`
fails in a build without them.

**Exceptions** (point 1; `core_reads::EXCEPTIONS`, `own_flags::DECLARED_EXCEPTIONS`, each with its
reason): `words`, which no row declares, read on every row `core_ops` serves in its process to
refuse it by name; `devices bind`'s `root`, the command line's kept flag, handed on undeclared
after the module's own `--root`; the `--cursor` of `codes`' and `events`' parsers, which the rows
do not declare (the MCP front keeps these cursors, LAB-5C); `session app`'s `--record`, which the
core rows `app launch|restart|stop` do not reach (L5C-7). No declared parameter of these rows is
read elsewhere: every one is read by its row's code (actinglab's global options reach no row
`core_ops` serves, and the MCP front's own members are taken out before it calls).

**Corrections of the table** (point 5): none. On main every planned row `core_ops` serves declares
exactly what its code reads, but the reads of L5B1-3, which the table rightly does not declare (the
parsers refuse them); no row declares a parameter its code does not read; every flag a row's
command line carries is its parser's, and its parser takes nothing more than the row carries but
the exceptions.

**LAB-5C's cases its tests did not cover** (point 4; the review of LAB-5C's pull request), as the
code answers them today, on the command line and in `serve --stdio`:

- both starting points of a read at once: `events`, `runs` and `diagnose` with `since` and
  `since_unix_ms` are refused `actingctl_usage_invalid`, `--since-unix-ms` `repeated`, before any
  connection (`since` goes on as `--since-unix-ms` first);
- a wait outside its range: `events --wait-s 21` is refused `out_of_range`, `range_min` 0,
  `range_max` 20, naming the parameter `wait_s` as MCP names it; `events --wait-s -1` is
  `--wait-s` `wrong_type` (the flag's value is no unsigned integer), where today's MCP server
  answers `out_of_range`: the two look inconsistent and stay as they are (reported to the
  coordinator);
- through the CLI module, not only through `core_ops`: each of `events`' parameters LAB-5C added
  (its twelve filters, `detail`, `wait_s`) reaches the Runtime's connection
  (`runtime_info_unavailable` on a state root without one); `material --out <dir> --offset 5`
  answers the connection's failure, not `conflicting` (LAB-5C fix 1, N1); `packs --role startup`
  reaches `packs`, which refuses no `--role`.

**Where main differs from the survey.** T1 reads 30 rows in this process (the survey's 24 core
rows and four debugging rows, before LAB-5C, R-6 and R-8 added rows and parameters); T2 is the
survey's 16 rows and three offline ones, `frame` in both (served here without `out`); `runs`' list
was its parser's match, not a constant; no core row has `params_more` since LAB-5A (the survey's
differences 1 and 6 are gone).

#### Slice LAB-5G7 (0.12.57): the manual of `actinglab-mcp`, its instructions final, and how a registration is changed

Coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-lab5g7.md` with `rd-1112/brief-lab5g-common.md`, on main
`fdf0fc22` (LAB-5G1 to G6, LAB-5B1, B1b and B1c merged): the last slice of LAB-5G, the row G7 of
the slice table of the coordinator's ruling 6775192250 on board #434 (the manual; at the end the
owner changes the registrations). The standard it is held to is the owner's statement of
2026-11-13 (board #434), in the coordinator's words: the command line and MCP are two shells
around the Lab, and what the Lab has, both must have; today the one registered exception is
`deploy` and `rollback` through MCP, refused until LAB-6. The rule of the slice: nothing a program
does changes but the text of the new server's instructions; today's MCP server
