#### Slice LAB-6S0 (0.12.58): `deploy` and `rollback` through the Lab's MCP server; the detached run carries `Lab-MCP`

Coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-lab6s0.md`, on main `29a65e2d`: the first slice the
coordinator cut from LAB-6 (board #434, 11-13), its row S0 in the read-only survey
`rd-1113/lab6-step0-survey.md` (section D, row S0 and D.5; rows A22 and N6). The standard is the
owner's statement of 2026-11-13 (board #434), in the coordinator's words: the command line and MCP
are two shells around the Lab, and what the Lab has, both must have. The one exception "Slice
LAB-5G7" registered, `deploy` and `rollback` through MCP, ends here. The mechanism is the
coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-13, not the owner's words (the survey's N6 recommends the marker
variable). Untouched: the door (`BindChannel`, the channels, `via`, the origin gates), the runtime
client, the ledger's shapes, every interface declaration, `actingctl`'s commands, the CLI's own
child starts and the MCP server's `serve` children; no operation but these two changes its answer.

**The cause** (the survey's lines, checked on this base). A rescue row that must outlive its
caller runs detached (`crates/lab-rescue/src/rescue.rs`, `detach`): the module starts the program
again through the watchdog's manual-run method (WMI, `install::host::detach_with_wmi`) with the
operation's initiator in `ACTINGCOMMAND_INITIATOR`. A Lab process refuses `Lab-MCP` in that
variable (`lab_ops::initiator`, `of_lab_process`; L2-7), so that no process can call itself the
MCP server. A detached run started from the MCP server would answer "detached" and never run, so
the server refused both rows (`tools::runs_detached`, L5G2b-13), keeping `detach` among the
members it gives (`tools::SUPPLIED`). **One more, found here:** the detached start ran the running
program's own file (`std::env::current_exe()`); in the MCP server, which serves the module in its
own process, that is `actinglab-mcp.exe`, which would have been handed the row's words as its start
options. The start now runs the `actinglab.exe` beside the running program (L6S0-3).

**What `ac_deploy` and `ac_rollback` answer now** (on Windows; the module's `detach`,
`rescue.rs`): at once, `install_command_done` (`operation` `install_deploy` or
`install_rollback_apply`, `installation_changed` false, the detached run's `pid` and `log`),
`isError` false, with the members `detached: true`, `log` (`install\detached-<ms>.log` under the
root, where the run's output goes) and `next` `{status: ["op", "status"]}`. `op status` follows the
operation: its `unfinished` names it while the run works, `last_operations` once it ended (its
`operation_id`, `kind`, result), and `op status` with `op` gives its journal. A refusal before the
start (an unfinished operation, a root whose installation state cannot be read) answers at once and
starts nothing. The answer does not carry the operation's id: the detached run mints it when it
opens its journal (open below).

**The code** (`mcp_operation_unsupported`, the work order's point 4). After this slice no offered
row emits it on any platform: on Windows every offered rescue row is one the module serves (its
33, the three `mcp` rows of slice LAB-5 among them), and elsewhere no rescue row is offered;
`convert` is not offered (its source is not built), so a call of `ac_convert` is an unknown tool
(-32602 `mcp_params_invalid`), not this code. Its two emitters stay as the server's check:
`calls::Service::line` for an offered row `tools::serving` refuses (an offered rescue row of slice
LAB-5 the module would not serve) and `server::answer` for a tool name the catalog does not hold
once `parse_call` admitted the call; neither is reached today. The catalog's way with a code nothing
can emit any more is to retire it with its registry entry (G1; L2-15's `resource_check_release_retired`,
whose command was gone); a code that stays registered with a check no input reaches today stays
active, as `lab_command_option_disabled` does (L5F-5, contract §12). So the entry stays `active`
and `pending`, its `common_causes` say that no row answers it in this build and what the check is
for, and its description and handling are unchanged.

- The manual (`apps/actinglab-mcp/MANUAL.md`): section 1 registers no exception; section 8 names

  ([install-cli.md](install-cli.md), "Operational rule until LAB-7"); section 10 lists the two tools
  among those that change what the installation runs, and its rule of use names deploying and

- The instructions (`tools::INSTRUCTIONS`, 3,371 bytes at a call budget of 25 s, 3,388 before):
  "Only deploy and rollback, which must run detached, answer mcp_operation_unsupported, and nothing
  is sent, run or written for them." → "On Windows deploy and rollback always run detached, as
  Lab-MCP: each answers at once with the detached run's pid and log, and ac_op_status follows the
  operation."; "Starting, stopping or restarting the Runtime and replacing its configuration are the

  configuration, deploying and rolling back a build are the person's to decide: …", the rest of the
  rule unchanged; "This build does not serve deploy and rollback through MCP: use the command line."
  removed.
- [lab-operations.json](lab-operations.json): the notes of `deploy` and `rollback` say that the MCP
  server serves them detached, what the answer is, that the detached run journals `Lab-MCP`, and
  the production rule.

**Tests.** New: apps row "#434 LAB-6S0". In actinglab's unit tests (`gate_434_lab6s0`; pure
functions, no environment changed): `lab_mcp_from_the_variable_only_with_the_marker` (without the

of another value is none; `serve --stdio --front mcp` refuses the variable set to anything, `Lab-MCP`
included). In the rescue module's tests on the installer's fake host and a made-up root
(`install::gate_434_lab6s0`): `detached_start_sets_the_marker_only_for_lab_mcp` (`deploy` and

initiator rule from the recorded variable and marker, runs the row's words, and every journal it
writes says `Lab-MCP`; `op status` lists its operation by its id, and with the id gives its journal,
which says `Lab-MCP`). **Adapted**, as the requirement deliberately changes what they pinned:
`gate_434_lab5g7::mcp_manual_exception_is_the_refused_rows` (rewritten to what is true now: the
server refuses no row it offers on any platform; no heading of the manual is on an exception, and
neither the manual nor the instructions name `mcp_operation_unsupported`; section 9 names the tools
of the rows the front forces detached and `ac_op_status`);
`gate_434_lab5g2b::mcp_served_and_refused_partition` (the class "refused: the front forces its run
detached" is gone; every row the module serves is served, `deploy` and `rollback` among them);
`server_stdio::mcp_calls_refused_unsupported_and_an_unknown_tool` (on Windows `ac_deploy` without
`target` and `ac_rollback` with an undeclared member answer `arguments_invalid`, `required` and
`unknown`, before anything runs, where they answered `mcp_operation_unsupported`; `ac_deploy` too
where `--list` leaves it out); `serve_calls::mcp_detached_rows_refused_and_nothing_started` (with an
unfinished operation's `current.json` the module cannot read in the made-up root, each tool answers

The tests of LAB-5B1, LAB-5B1b and LAB-5B1c that pin what each row reads and hands over are not
changed and still hold: no row's constant, command line or receiver changes. No test leaves the
gate map.

**Interface.** None raised: nothing on the wire, in the ledger, in a journal's shape or in a file a
released peer reads changes (the journal's `initiator` takes `Lab-MCP`, one of the six words, as the
server's in-process rescue rows already write it); no code, key, location or vocabulary token is
added.

**What LAB-6S0 changes live.** Nothing until a client is registered with the MCP entry's second
generation (manual, section 11): no registration names `actinglab-mcp` today. Afterwards an agent of
such a client can call `ac_deploy` and `ac_rollback` of that client's root on Windows, which before
answered `mcp_operation_unsupported`; the manual's and the instructions' rule of use leaves the
decision to the person, and until LAB-7 production keeps deploying through `actingctl install`.

**Rollback** (to the release before it). Nothing persisted but what a detached `deploy` or
`rollback` writes as the command line would; its journal carries `Lab-MCP`, one of the six words,
which the build before reads.

**Where LAB-6S0 differs from its work order's letter.**

- (a) The work order (point 2, citing §5) and the table's note of `detach` say the two tools
  "answer the operation's id at once". The module's detached answer carries no operation id: the
  detached run mints it when it opens its journal, after the answer. This slice keeps the module's
  answer (its command line's too) and says what is true: `detached`, `pid`, `log` and `next` naming
  `op status`, which names the operation by its id. Giving the id at once needs the caller to mint
  it for the detached run, a change of the module beyond this slice: left to the coordinator.
- (b) The program the detached start runs (L6S0-3) is a change the survey did not name; without it
  the server's detached run would start `actinglab-mcp.exe`.
- (c) `mcp_operation_unsupported` stays active (above, "The code").

#### Slice LAB-6S1a (0.12.58): the door also takes `BindChannel{channel: lab, initiator}`; `runtime-client` [3, 8]

Coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-lab6s1a.md`, after the read-only survey
`rd-1113/lab6-step0-survey.md`; the coordinator's rulings of 2026-11-13 on board #434, not the
owner's words; on main `29a65e2d`. The contracts are [lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md)
(the slice table, §2.2, §4.1, §4.3, §10), [runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md)
("Binding" rule 9, "Old Runtimes", "New request kinds") and
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) (`runtime-client` 8, "Planned: Workflow #434").

**The staging, and why.** The contract described LAB-6 as one step: the door takes `lab` with an
initiator and `ui`, and refuses `cli` and `mcp`. The survey showed that, done at once, it breaks
every client of the door on the day of the deploy (actingctl and the kits' installer, the
watchdog and today's MCP server bind `cli` or `mcp`; the installed console cannot decode a
receipt with a member it does not know), and production deploys what is merged. So the
coordinator cut LAB-6 into slices that each leave main deployable: LAB-6S0 (`deploy` and
`rollback` through the Lab's MCP server), LAB-6S1a (this slice), LAB-6S1b (the origin gates of
`RuntimeRequest::validate()` go), LAB-6S2 (every client of this repository binds `lab` with its
word, after LAB-6S1a and LAB-6S1b have been deployed by themselves), LAB-6S3 (the UI list on
`ui`), LAB-6S4a (the five kinds deleted; `install-control` [0, 0]), LAB-6S4b (`cli`, `mcp` and a
`lab` without a word refused; `via` off the wire; `runtime-client` [8, 8]; `actingd-config` 30)
and LAB-6S5 (the initiator in the ledger and the settings rows; `ledger` 9). Each has a way back
but LAB-6S5. The contract's slice table carries the staging; the numbers LAB-0 planned for LAB-6
(`runtime-client` 7, `ledger` 8, `actingd-config` 28) were taken by other slices, and are now 8
(LAB-6S1a), 9 (LAB-6S5) and 30 (LAB-6S4b).

**This slice is additive.** Every connection that binds today binds as today and reads the bytes
it reads today; the only new thing is a connection that declares a word, and no program of this
build declares one (that is LAB-6S2).

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L6S1a-1 | `Initiator` (`UI`, `Lab-CLI`, `Lab-MCP`, `Lab-制包`, `Lab-救急`, `Lab-看门狗`): `ALL`, `as_str`, `is_lab_word`, `from_word`, `Serialize`, `Deserialize` | closed vocabulary of the contract crate | LAB-6S1a | — | the one place the six strings are written; a word outside them does not decode. `crates/lab-ops`' `initiator::Initiator` keeps its methods and converts (`word`), its `as_str` being the contract's, so the recordings and the installation journal write what they wrote. A rename before the release is one line of `as_str` |
| L6S1a-2 | `BindChannel{channel, via?, initiator?}`, `initiator` the word as sent (`DeclaredInitiator`, any string) | wire, request | LAB-6S1a | — | taken only with `channel` `lab`, without `via`, and only as one of the five Lab words (`ChannelBinding::requested`, checked by `validate()`); a word on `ui`, `cli` or `mcp`, a word with `via`, `UI` and a word outside the list are `invalid_bind_channel`, and the connection stays unbound. Absent, the request is revision 7's |
| L6S1a-3 | `ChannelBound{channel, via?, initiator?}` | wire, answer | LAB-6S1a | the host's `bind_channel` | echoes the word of a connection that declared one; absent otherwise, on `ui` included (its `UI` is implied by its channel) |
| L6S1a-4 | the receipt's `initiator`, beside `channel` (`RuntimeReceipt::initiator`) | wire, answer | LAB-6S1a | the door (`with_channel`) | on every receipt of a connection that declared a word; absent otherwise |
| L6S1a-5 | the connection table's `ChannelBinding.initiator` | in memory | LAB-6S1a | — | kept with the channel, gone with its connection, reported by no status read; the gate reads no word and refuses nothing by channel or by word; the binding a connection's first request makes has none |
| L6S1a-6 | `RuntimeClientConfig::with_initiator`; the handshake's echo check | client | LAB-6S1a | — | the one handshake function sends the word and takes the answer only when it echoes channel, `via` and word (another echo is `runtime_result_unexpected`, as another channel is); `connect`, the reconnect in the owner's epoch, the contained-task timeout recovery and the player hold's temporary client carry it as they carry the channel; a word on another channel, with `via`, or `UI` is `runtime_client_config_invalid` at connect. No caller in product code sets it |

**Byte for byte.** A binding without a word (`lab` alone, `lab` with `via`, `cli`, `mcp`, `ui`,
and the binding a connection's first request makes) is answered and receipted exactly as on the
base: each new member is optional and left out when absent, and nothing else of the three shapes
changed. `gate_434_lab6s1a::lab6s1a_a_binding_without_a_word_answers_byte_for_byte_as_before`
holds it: for each such binding the bytes of its `ChannelBound` receipt and of a later `Health`
receipt, read off the connection, equal literal JSON written in the test.

**Nothing persisted changes.** No persisted record embeds a receipt or a `ChannelBound` (read on
the base: the ledger's command records take `channel` and `via` from the binding,
`ObservationDraft::sanitize`; the `host.config_overrides` rows take its `channel`; the
recordings and the installation journal take `crates/lab-ops`' type, whose strings do not
change; the reports that print a receipt, `restart`'s and `request-shutdown --wait`'s, persist
nothing). No ledger payload, override row, recording or journal gains or loses a member, and
`ledger` does not move.

**Interface.** `runtime-client` [3, 8] (component-interfaces.md, revision 8): revision 7 plus the
initiator in `BindChannel`, `ChannelBound` and the receipt; a client of 3 to 7 neither sends nor
receives it. Read before the code: the installer's edges (`crates/lab-rescue/src/install/plan.rs`,
`interface_edges` and `meet`: `installer_meets_previous` and `installer_meets_next` intersect
ranges) pass an update from a [3, 7] build to this one and the rollback from it to that build,
whichever of the two is the installer; `ledger` is unchanged, so no one-way edge. The console of
the UI's release v0.12.16 declares [3, 7]: its installer negotiates the highest common revision
with the Runtime (`crates/acui-setup/src/interfaces.rs`, `negotiate` with `Range::common`; 7
here), the console compares no range, and its pinned client binds `ui` without a word, which is
answered byte for byte as before.

**An earlier Runtime and a client that sends a word.** A Runtime before this slice cannot decode a
`BindChannel` that names `initiator` (`RuntimeOperation` denies unknown members): it drops the
connection without a receipt (`runtime_request_decode_failed`), and the client then reconnects
once, goes on unbound and reports `client_channel_unsupported`, as for an actingd before U-2. So no
client sends a word before this slice is deployed in production; LAB-6S2 waits for it.

**Tests.** New: host row "#434 LAB-6S1a" (`gate_434_lab6s1a` of the host, the first part of the
contract's `gate_two_entries`: `lab` with each Lab word bound, echoed and on its receipts, a
second `BindChannel` `channel_binding_exists`; the byte-for-byte test above; every refused word
`invalid_bind_channel` with the connection left unbound and bound afterwards; and of the runtime
client: the handshake with a word, an echo that differs, the reconnect and the temporary client
keeping the word) and contract row "#434 LAB-6S1a" (`BindChannel`, `ChannelBound` and the receipt
round-trip with and without the member and read revision 7's shape; `crates/lab-ops`' words are
the contract's, in its order). Adapted, each for the new member only: the declaration's pins
(`component_interfaces::V0120`, `gate_429_r0b_pairing`'s two `[3, 7]`); the test fakes and tests
that build or match `BindChannel`, `ChannelBound` or `ChannelBinding` (`initiator: None` or `..`;
the shared scripted Runtime of `runtime-client`'s `test_support` echoes a declared word). The
catalog text of `invalid_bind_channel` names the new refusals; no code is added.

**What LAB-6S1a changes live.** Nothing for any client that exists: no program of this build
declares a word, and every binding answers as before.

**LAB-6S1a rollback** (to the release before it). Two-way: nothing persisted; the earlier build
declares [3, 7], which every client of this build meets, and no client sent a word.

#### Slice LAB-6S1b (0.12.58): the origin gates of `RuntimeRequest::validate()` go

Coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-lab6s1b.md`, after the read-only survey
`rd-1113/lab6-step0-survey.md` (its B.3, B.4, the row S1b of D and E's N9); the coordinator's
rulings of 2026-11-13 on board #434, not the owner's words; built on LAB-6S1a. The contract is
[lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) §2.4 ("LAB-6 deletes the origin gates of
`RuntimeRequest::validate()` ...; the content and shape rules stay"), with the slice table's row.

**Each gate deleted, and what it refused** (all in `RuntimeRequest::validate`, before or after
`self.operation.validate()`):

|---|---|---|---|
| L6S1b-1 | `RequestShutdown` | every envelope but `(User, Ui)`, `(Cli, Cli)` | `invalid_shutdown_origin` |
| L6S1b-2 | `InstallTransition` | the same | `invalid_install_transition_origin` |
| L6S1b-3 | `RecordAuthoringEvent` | every envelope but `(Lab, Lab)` | `invalid_resource_authoring_origin` |

| L6S1b-5 | `RecordDebugEvent`, `ReleaseLabPin`, `RunContainedLabOperation`, `RecognizeArtifact`, `DebugPackage`, `ExportEvidence` | the same | `invalid_runtime_debug_origin` |
| L6S1b-6 | `DeclareGovernanceIdentity` | every envelope but `(User, Ui)`, `(Cli, Cli)` (`valid_governance_declaration_origin`) | `invalid_governance_origin` |
| L6S1b-7 | `RecordApprovalDecision` | every envelope but `(User, Ui)` | `invalid_governance_origin` |
| L6S1b-8 | `ControlEmulatorInstance`, `DiscoverInstances`, `SelfCheckInstance`, `DrillRecoveryLadder` | every envelope but `(User, Ui)`, `(Cli, Cli)` | `invalid_emulator_control_origin` |
| L6S1b-9 | `PauseScheduling`, `ResumeScheduling` | the same | `invalid_scheduling_pause_origin` |
| L6S1b-10 | `AgentWakeTest` | the same | `invalid_agent_wake_test_origin` |
| L6S1b-11 | `PublishFact`, `PublishFacts` by family | every envelope but `(Agent, Adapter)`, and for a family with the origin exception (offsets, remedy choices, the pack schedule) also `(User, Ui)`, `(Cli, Cli)` | `invalid_agent_dispatcher_origin` |
| L6S1b-12 | the agent dispatcher's kinds (the planning session's ten, `ApplyResourceTargets`) | every envelope but `(Agent, Adapter)` | `invalid_agent_dispatcher_origin` |
| L6S1b-13 | `AcquirePlayerHold`, `ReleasePlayerHold` (after the shapes) | every envelope but `(User, Ui)`, `(Cli, Cli)`, `(Lab, Lab)` | `invalid_player_hold_origin` |

**What stays, and why none of it is a gate by origin.** `valid_client_origin`: an envelope
outside the client set (a source other than `Cli`, `Ui`, `Lab`, `Adapter`, or an actor other than
`User`, `Cli`, `Ui`, `Lab`, `Agent`) is still `invalid_client_origin`, a shape rule of the
envelope. Every content and shape rule, `fact_origin_mixed` among them (one request does not mix
key families; `fact_key_family` and `FactKeyFamily::takes_origin_exception` stay, the latter for
the host's choice of the `fact.published` origin). Judged by the envelope outside `validate()`,
unchanged and none of it a refusal by origin of a client request: the frame pin's kind (`Lab` for
a `(Lab, Lab)` request), the C4 intent's record type and origin module
(`c4_client_source_unsupported`), the receipt's default detail.

**The host's own re-checks of an origin stay as they are** (they belong to kinds LAB-6S4a
deletes): `governance.rs`, `declare_governance_identity`, refuses a card from any envelope but
`(User, Ui)`, `(Cli, Cli)` (`valid_governance_declaration_origin`, `invalid_governance_origin`,
nothing recorded); `governance.rs`, `record_approval_decision`, refuses an approval from anything
but `(User, Ui)` on a connection whose card was accepted (`governance_authority_required`);
`installation.rs`, `install_transition`, refuses every action but `Query` on a connection whose
card was not accepted (`install_identity_required`, its lifecycle failure recorded). Since no
card can be accepted from another envelope, each refuses what it refused; only the code of an
approval or a card from a refused envelope changes where validate's came first (an approval from
`(Lab, Lab)` is now `governance_authority_required`; a card keeps `invalid_governance_origin`).
Outside these kinds the host keeps one more check by envelope that `validate()` never held: an
evidence-read confirmation (`RecordClientAction` of `evidence_read_frame` or `evidence_read_run`)
counts only from `(Agent, Adapter)`, `(Cli, Cli)`, `(User, Ui)` (`client_action_invalid`,
`client_events.rs`); and the runtime client still opens an authoring or debug session only on a
Lab envelope (`runtime_authoring_origin_invalid`, `runtime_debug_origin_invalid`). This slice
touches neither.

**Codes.** Retired (`status` `retired`, `retired_in` 0.12.58, no `replaced_by`, the registry
entries removed as G1 asks; the index regenerated): `invalid_shutdown_origin`,
`invalid_install_transition_origin` (released settled in 0.12.0; G9 holds the signature, not the
status), `invalid_resource_authoring_origin`, `invalid_signature_origin`,
`invalid_runtime_debug_origin`, `invalid_emulator_control_origin`,
`invalid_scheduling_pause_origin`, `invalid_agent_wake_test_origin`,
`invalid_agent_dispatcher_origin`, `invalid_player_hold_origin`: no code path emits them once the
gates are gone. No `replaced_by`: the Runtime takes the request; the `channel_request_refused`
the U-6 text planned for some of them (runtime-interface.md, "Retired later") is LAB-6S3's refusal
by channel on `ui`, not a replacement, and that table now says so. Kept: `invalid_governance_origin`
(the host's card check emits it), `invalid_client_origin`, `fact_origin_mixed`. No code is added.
**No interface revision moves**: the Runtime accepts more and no shape changes (no request,
answer, record or document gains or loses a member; [component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md),
"Bump rule").

**What begins to work** (read on the code: `crates/lab-ops`' `front::Front::Actinglab` gives
actinglab's CLI module and `serve` the envelope `(Lab, Lab)`, and `core_ops` serves these rows
through the front's connection). Refused before and served now, from `actinglab` (CLI and

#### Slice LAB-6S2-M (0.12.59): the host records today's channel for a `lab` binding that declares a word

Coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-lab6s2m.md`, after two read-only surveys: the first,
`rd-1113/lab6s2-design.md` (who binds what, and everything outside `validate()` that judges or
records by the envelope or the channel), and the second, `rd-1113/lab6s2-mapping.md` (whether the
host can map a declared word back to today's origin; its variant K, which the coordinator
adopted); the coordinator's rulings of 2026-11-13 on board #434, not the owner's words; based on
main `daac1ed4` (0.12.58). The contracts are [lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) (the slice
table, §2.4, §4.3), [runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) ("Binding" rule 9) and
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) (`runtime-client` 8's row).

**What.** LAB-6S2, every program of this repository on `lab` with its word, is cut into
LAB-6S2-M (this slice, the host's half), LAB-6S2-B1 (the Lab's own programs bind `lab` with their
word and keep the envelope they sent on 0.12.58), LAB-6S2-B2 (`actingctl` and today's MCP server
the same) and LAB-6S2-E (the envelope becomes the channel's; the map and the receipt rule end).
This slice gives the door the map M and the receipt rule R. It is dormant: no program of this
build declares a word.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L6S2M-1 | `ChannelBinding::recorded(source)`, the map M (`crates/actingcommand-contract`, `runtime/interface.rs`) | pure function of the contract crate | LAB-6S2-M | — | the table below; every binding but `lab` with one of the five Lab words is returned as it is (`lab` without a word, with or without `via`, `cli`, `mcp`, `ui`, the binding an unbound connection's first request makes); the result names no initiator and is never `ui` |
| L6S2M-2 | the door applies M once (`runtime-host` `requests.rs`, `process_request_observed`): the validated request carries M's binding | behaviour | LAB-6S2-M | the door | so the C4 `command.received`'s `channel` and `via`, the package debug record's and the `host.config_overrides` row's `channel` (the surveys' places B-3 and B-19) read it; the envelope, and everything judged by it, is untouched. The UI gate reads it too: M leaves `ui` as it is and never yields it, so the gate judges exactly the connections bound to `ui` |
| L6S2M-3 | the receipt rule R (the door, `with_channel`) | wire, answer | LAB-6S2-M | the door | a request whose envelope's source is `Lab`: the connection's binding with its word, LAB-6S1a's receipt; a request with any other client envelope: M's binding, without `initiator`; `BindChannel`: the binding it made or kept, as before |

**The table M**, by the word and the source of the request's envelope:

| Word \ envelope source | `Lab` | `Cli`, `Adapter`, `Ui` |
|---|---|---|
| `Lab-MCP` | `lab`, `via` `mcp` | `mcp` |
| `Lab-CLI`, `Lab-制包`, `Lab-救急`, `Lab-看门狗` | `lab` | `cli` |

**R.** On a `lab` binding that declares a word, the receipt of a request whose envelope's source is
not `Lab` carries M's binding (`channel` `cli`, or `mcp` under `Lab-MCP`), without `via` and
without `initiator`; the receipt of a request from the Lab carries `channel` `lab` and the word, as
from LAB-6S1a. The answer to `BindChannel` is not under R: the client requires its echo. A binding
without a word is receipted as before.

**Why.** The first survey found that moving every program onto `lab` with the Lab's envelope in one
step breaks three things. The evidence-read confirmation counts only from an agent adapter, the CLI
or a person, in the host and in the frame index, so the confirmations of `actingctl` and of both
MCP servers would be refused. The identity card and the host's re-checks take only `(User, Ui)` and
`(Cli, Cli)`, so `actingctl install-transition`, and with it acsetup's close, and both MCP servers'
writes would fail their card. And every receipt on a word binding carries `initiator`, which the
installed console's acsetup (v0.12.16, whose pinned receipt type has no such member and refuses
unknown ones) cannot decode in the receipts that `install-transition` and `request-shutdown` print,
so its close and start would fail. It also changes what a person sees: the console's ledger page
and Lab tab would show the requests of `actingctl` and both MCP servers as the Lab's, its settings
page "via Lab" for the rows they set, the runs they start the origin `lab`, and their frames would
be kept as Lab frames. The second survey found that a word alone cannot name today's origin
(`Lab-CLI` stands for `actingctl`'s `(Cli, Cli)` and `(Agent, Adapter)` and for `actinglab`'s
`(Lab, Lab)` on the same kinds, and one `actinglab` process sends both), and that keyed by the word
and the envelope it can: a client that keeps its 0.12.58 envelope is judged by it as on 0.12.58 (no
branch of `validate()` reads it since LAB-6S1b, and the door checks no envelope against the
binding), so only what the host writes from the channel needs M, and R keeps every byte acsetup
decodes. Of the 33 places outside `validate()` that judge or record by the envelope or the channel,
32 then stay as on 0.12.58; the one left differs only in version skew (a program of LAB-6S2-B1 or
later that meets a Runtime before LAB-6S1a is dropped, goes on unbound and is bound by its
envelope, so an MCP server's connection is bound `cli`). The three owner decisions the first survey
named (kept frames, what the console shows, a console release that reads `initiator`) are not needed
for LAB-6S2-M, LAB-6S2-B1 and LAB-6S2-B2; they come back with LAB-6S2-E.

**The one cell that is not today's.** The rescue rows that `actinglab-mcp` serves send `(Cli, Cli)`
on `cli` today; under `Lab-MCP` M records them `mcp`. Those requests write no channel anywhere (the
rescue module sends no C4 kind, no setting and no debug package, and a pause records no channel),
so only their receipts' `channel` differs (the second survey's V3).

**Nothing else changes.** No request is refused that was taken and none taken that was refused: M
changes no judgement and R only the channel members of a receipt on a word binding. **No interface
revision moves**: `channel`, `via` and `initiator` are optional members of `runtime-client` 8's
receipt, and no record, row or document gains or loses a member (component-interfaces.md's row of
revision 8 now says which receipts carry `initiator`). No outcome code is added. `validate()`, the
UI list, `ui_gate.rs`, the interface revisions file and every client program are untouched.

**Tests.** New: host row "#434 LAB-6S2-M" (`gate_434_lab6s2m`). One test per row of M a program
will use: `cli` against `lab` with `Lab-CLI` and `mcp` against `lab` with `Lab-MCP`, both with
`(Cli, Cli)`; `lab` without a word against `lab` with `Lab-CLI`, and `lab` with `via` `mcp` against
`lab` with `Lab-MCP`, both with `(Lab, Lab)`. Within one host the two connections send a
`ConfigureSettings` of an instance's `stuck_recovery`, a `PublishFacts` of a priority offset, a
`RecordClientAction`, a `StopInstanceRun` (a C4 kind on the fake device, refused after its command
record) and last a `RequestShutdown`; each pair's receipts are equal with the request and
correlation ids, the terminal's event id and position, the fact's event id, the settings' version
token and the channel members left out, the channel members being today's binding and R's; both
write the same records (type, source, module, actor, channel, `via`); and the settings row names
today's channel after either. Then R on each of the five words for `(Cli, Cli)`, `(Agent, Adapter)`
and `(Lab, Lab)`, with the answer to `BindChannel` unchanged; a binding without a word, `cli`,
`mcp`, `ui` and an unbound connection answered and recorded as before; and the UI gate never
judging a mapped connection (M leaves `ui` and yields it for no binding; a priority offset, off the
list, with the console's envelope is served on `lab` with each word and refused on `ui`).
**Adapted**: `gate_434_lab6s1a::lab6s1a_lab_with_each_lab_word_is_bound_echoed_and_carried_by_its_receipts`
sent its Status and Health with the CLI's envelope and pinned the word on their receipts, which R
now answers without it; they are sent with the Lab's envelope, whose receipts still carry it (the
CLI envelope's receipt is pinned in the new gate). No test leaves the gate map.

**At deploy.** Nothing: dormant until a program declares a word (LAB-6S2-B1). A Runtime of this
release answers every program of 0.12.58, and the released console, byte for byte as 0.12.58
does.

**LAB-6S2-M rollback** (to 0.12.58). Two-way: nothing persisted changes shape or value, and no
program of this build declares a word.

**Where LAB-6S2-M differs from its work order's letter.**

- (a) The shutdown the pairs send names another process: an accepted one would stop the host
  before the pair's second connection is answered. It is recorded and refused
  (`runtime_shutdown_denied`) on both, with the request's origin.
- (b) Each connection's priority offset has its own observation time: an observation equal to the
  active one is a replay, which appends nothing.
- (c) On the two `lab` rows the pair's receipts differ in their channel members, as R says (the
  Lab envelope's receipt carries the word, and the MCP children's has no `via`), so the test
  compares those members against today's binding and R's apart from the rest of the receipt.
- (d) runtime-interface.md, "Binding" rule 9, which the work order does not name, said that every
  receipt of a word binding carries `initiator`; it now names M and R, as component-interfaces.md
  does.

### 1.288 Slice SS-2f (0.12.46): the business tier across instances goes to the instance least recently dispatched first (Workflow #428; Alice's answer K2 to question 137 of 2026-11-02 19:4x, recorded on board #428 and in the coordinator's pending list, 「137：K2」, with no reason given; design `rd-1031/design-acm-price-addendum2.1.md` §5.4 and its slice row SS-2f, read on main `eb1e946d`; placed before 116 is lifted by the research channel's `rd-1031/design-c424-redline-1109.md` §4.9, Q13; coordinator work order `rd-1109/brief-ss2f.md`)

[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Net benefit within a tier", "Turns across
instances"; "Dispatch Decision Record" item 1) and [standard-pack-schedule.md](standard-pack-schedule.md)
("Two priority tiers") are the contract. It narrows §1.225 (the ranking across instances) and
§1.235 (3) (the zero tier's order across instances). The number 1.288 is this slice's; SS-2h-a
and #434 LAB-1 may be in flight beside it.

**What.** In a catalog that marks a task `benefit_judged`, two business candidates of different
instances are ordered by their instances' turns (`evaluator/turns.rs`, `InstanceTurns`; one more
key of `allocation_order`), after `promoted`, the tier and the zero tier's place and before every
other key of the tier: the instance whose most recent policy dispatch is the earliest first, an
instance never dispatched before every dispatched one, and at the same instant (two never
dispatched included) the smaller instance id. An instance's most recent policy dispatch is the
latest `last_dispatched_unix_ms` among its task snapshots (`EvaluationFacts.tasks`, the fact
refresh's `_fact_refresh` included). Within an instance the key is equal, so the order of §1.225,
§1.229 and §1.235 stays: unjudged first, then judged by `B ÷ E`, the released zero tier last. The
reserve gate reads the same order (`apply_reserves`), per instance as before.

**Why.** K2, the design's recommendation, which Alice chose; the design's own reasons, not hers:
each game's value unit (its `κ`, `prices.unit_milli`) differs, so `B` of two games is not
comparable, and comparing them by list price is what the 10-30 joint plan warned against; the
turns fit #427's "five instances run like five players" and change one sort key. The shared run
limits (`max_concurrent_runs`, the heavy-scene slots) are where the order across instances
decides, and they are contended on almost every round once scheduling resumes.

**Where the key comes from.** The task snapshots every evaluation already receives: the Runtime
projects them from the policy dispatches it admitted (`policy_host.rs`,
`task_runtime_snapshots_of`), one per task and instance with its latest admission. No new read,
no ledger query (#422), no state file.

**Unchanged.** The maintenance tier and its order, a promotion's place, the zero tier's last place
behind every positive and unjudged candidate of every instance, "one dispatch per instance", the
reserve gate, the shared run limits, the benefit gate, the chain handover, the decision records,
game neutrality. A catalog without `benefit_judged`, or a round with no business candidate,
decides byte for byte as before. **No configuration key, no new code, no ledger record kind, no
interface revision**: the evaluator's order is no anchor of
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) (its "Bump rule": no field, record or document
an older peer reads changes).

**What changes live.** Nothing while ruling 116 holds business dispatch (this slice is placed
before it is lifted). Afterwards, when business candidates of several instances contend for a
shared run slot, it goes to the instance that waited longest, not to the game with the larger
number.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.45). Nothing is persisted: an older build orders the business tier across
instances by `B ÷ E` again.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SS2f-1 | `allocation_order`: business candidates of different instances by their instances' turns (`InstanceTurns::order`) | behaviour (evaluation) | SS-2f | — | only with `benefit_judged` in the catalog and between two business candidates; total: the instance id breaks a tie |

this slice's; §1.288 is SS-2f's.

**What.**
1. **Full price below the cap.** A judged candidate's consumption costs `W·c` whatever the pool's
   fill (`evaluator/benefit.rs`, `judge`; SS-2b's `discount` is removed). A regenerating pool it
   consumes is still read (unknown or expired: `benefit_unknown`, `reading_unknown`) and wakes the
   evaluation at its next step. SS-2d's `ε` reads the whole `C` (its `σ` is gone). The comparison
   `B·E' > B'·E` is signed (`KnownBenefit::order`), the same for two positive `B`.
2. **Two lines.** A V2 pool may write `stop_line` and `hard_line`, both or neither
   (`PoolSpec::stop_line`, `PoolSpec::hard_line`, `PoolLine::Fact` with CF-5's `FactReference` or
   `PoolLine::Constant`): the compiler refuses them in V1 (`unknown_field`), a reference by a
   capacity reference's rules, a constant above 2^53−1 (`limit_exceeded`), and with the new
   diagnostic `pool_lines_invalid` one without the other, a line above the capacity and a stop
   line not above the hard line, wherever it can compare them. Without them `S` is the capacity and
   `H` 0. At each evaluation they are read on each instance (`0 ≤ H < S ≤ cap`, else
   `lines_invalid`), against the reading less the consumption it does not show yet.
3. **Below the cap** a judged candidate that would pass and whose run would leave the pool below
   `H` is held: `pool_line_held` `would_cross_hard_line`. A pool with lines whose cap, reading or a
   line's fact gives no value holds them with `capped_cap_unknown`.
4. **The capped spending order** (`evaluator/capped.rs`): at `r ≥ cap` a capped episode begins on
   the instance (at the start too); each round lists the pool's judged consumers that are
   candidates now by their value without the pool's cost (above that value's rounding bound;
   never by their cost; from the second round not `benefit_limited`), freezes them by `V ÷ C`, then
   task id, and plans from `r` down to `S`, skipping one that would end below `H`; one head at a
   time is dispatched (`capped_spend`), the reading checked again before each dispatch (a head that
   would cross `H` ends the round), the next round starting while `r > S`; the episode ends at
   `r ≤ S < cap`, a round that lists or plans nothing though a consumer is a candidate
   (`capped_round_empty`; with no candidate at all it waits for its next round), a new catalog
   generation or unknown lines.
   The head's block (it and the planned candidates after it that fit above `H`) keeps the head's
   place in the allocation (`capped::assign_leads`, `OrderView` in `allocation_order`; its `B =
   V − W·(c − a)`, `a = min(c, max(0, r − S))`), so a more urgent tier goes first; a block
   candidate a later gate defers yields to the next; the others wait (`capped_not_head`,
   `capped_limited_spent`, `capped_would_cross_hard_line`, `capped_not_dispatchable` with
   `gate_code`).
5. **The memory** `CappedMemory` (episodes, round numbers, frozen orders) is the Runtime's, in
   memory only like SS-4's: the new entry point `evaluate_with_capped_spending` reads and updates
   it, and `runtime-host`'s policy host keeps one and calls it each cycle (taken out for the call
   and put back whatever its result); every other entry point, `evaluate_with_no_progress`
   included, evaluates with an empty one. Which tasks a round ran is read from the task snapshots.
   The idle plan counts a decision held by `pool_line_held` neither due nor as a wake of its own
   (`schedule_explanation.rs`), as one held by the benefit gate.
6. **`benefit_limited`**, a V2 task boolean (requires `benefit_judged`, else
   `missing_required_field`); the composer writes it from the `schedule.json` rule member
   `"limited": true` (`SCHEDULE_RULE_LIMITED_MEMBER`, `BENEFIT_LIMITED_MEMBER`), refuses another
   value, the mark on a maintenance rule and a rule that writes `benefit_limited` itself.
7. **The always-on subsystem `pool_lines`**; the composer refuses a `schedule.json` whose pool
   writes a line while `requires` does not name it (`schedule_invalid` at the member) and copies the
   members as written.

**Why.** Ruling 138 with 172 A and 173 and the two water lines: at its cap a resource is spent by
value per unit, down to a stop line, never below a hard line the scheduler keeps; below the cap
nothing is spent for free. The lines are the model's, a person's or an agent's, never the
program's. Layout 乙 (design §1.6 item 4) keeps one dispatch at a time and every gate.

**Codes, keys, vocabulary** (policy fragment; all pending, `ladder_class` none): `capped_spend`
(info), `pool_line_held` (info) with the new vocabulary `pool_line_hold` (`would_cross_hard_line`,
`capped_not_dispatchable`, `capped_limited_spent`, `capped_would_cross_hard_line`,
`capped_round_empty`, `capped_not_head`, `capped_cap_unknown`, `lines_invalid`), and the catalog
diagnostic `pool_lines_invalid` (error). One domain code with a vocabulary carries the design's
seven holds (§1.6 item 7, provisional names; the outcome-code spec's 10-24 amendment). New keys:
`pool_capacity`, `stop_line`, `hard_line`, `pool_reading`, `capped_episode`, `capped_round`,
`capped_rank` (integers) and `pool_line_hold`; reused: `pool_id`, `amount_after`, `task_id`,
`gate_code`, `fact_key`, `unknown_reason`. New domain prefixes: `capped_` (policy), and policy
added to `pool_`. The descriptions of `policy_benefit_nonpositive`, `benefit_unknown`, the
`benefit_gap` token `reading_unknown`, `benefit_milli` and `tolerance_milli` drop the discount.

**Unchanged.** A catalog without a valuation, lines and `benefit_limited` serializes, hashes and
decides byte for byte as before (no pool takes part without a declared valuation; the neutral
example keeps its V1 and V2 golden hashes); the reserve gate, the zero tier, SS-2f's turns, the
shared run limits, every pause, hold, blackout and budget, SS-4, the one-way rule, game neutrality
and ruling 116's stop. **No configuration key, no persisted ledger shape, no interface revision**:
`component-interfaces.md`'s bump rule keeps a revision for a change older peers tolerate; the
members are gated by their subsystem through `requires` (an older Runtime refuses the file), the
codes are additions to the outcome catalog, and the memory is never persisted.

**What changes live.** Nothing now: no production pool declares a valuation, so no judged
candidate reaches the cost or a line; no `schedule.json` writes a line or `limited`. With
valuations (PRICE-4b) a regenerating pool at its cap is spent down to its stop line, which is why
this slice deploys before the first one (design §4.1, the order).

**Rollback** (to the release before). The ledger and the configuration need nothing. A build
without SS-2h refuses a pool that writes a line, and a task that writes `benefit_limited`, at its
reader (`unknown_field`), and does not name `pool_lines`, so its composer refuses such a
`schedule.json` (`schedule_requires_missing`); it compiles at its start every generation its
dispatches and decision memories name (§1.225's rollback correction), so first let this build
activate a generation without them. Rolling back also brings SS-2b's linear discount back for a
valued regenerating pool.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SS2h-1 | a V2 pool's `stop_line` and `hard_line` (`PoolLine`; schema `v2/pools.schema.json` `poolLine`) | catalog format addition (no ledger shape) | SS-2h | `acmodel bindings apply` (RL-R) | V2 only; both or neither; `pool_lines_invalid`; absent serializes as nothing |
| SS2h-2 | a V2 task's `benefit_limited`; the `schedule.json` rule member `limited` | catalog format addition | SS-2h | `acmodel bindings apply` (PRICE-4b) | requires `benefit_judged`; the composer's |
| SS2h-3 | the cost of a judged candidate's consumption, `W·c`; SS-2b's discount retired; SS-2d's `ε` without `σ` | behaviour (evaluation) | SS-2h | the policy evaluator | a regenerating pool still read |
| SS2h-4 | the hard line below the cap (`would_cross_hard_line`) and the capped spending order (`capped_spend`, `pool_line_held`) | behaviour (evaluation) | SS-2h | the policy evaluator | only valued pools and judged consumers |
| SS2h-5 | `CappedMemory`, `evaluate_with_capped_spending` | memory only (no shape) | SS-2h | runtime-host policy host | a start or a new catalog generation forgets it |
| SS2h-6 | `config.subsystems` row `pool_lines` (always on) | new row value of an existing fact (no shape) | SS-2h | actingd | required of a `schedule.json` whose pool writes a line (`POOL_LINES_SUBSYSTEM`, `POOL_LINE_MEMBERS`) |

Tests: `gate_ss2h` (design §4.1 tests 1 to 17; tests 1 and 2 fail on main and pass here). Adapted,
as the requirement deliberately changes what they pinned: `ss2b_t6` (a full regenerating pool cost
nothing and half way half its weight; now full price, and at its capacity the task is the head of
its capped order with `B` −9000) and `ss2d_t15` (a full regenerating pool cost nothing; now it is
dispatched as the capped head with `B` −9000).

**Fix 1** (coordinator brief `rd-1109/brief-ss2h-fix1.md`, the independent review of PR #1546;
same release, same number). (1) `capped::line_value` returns the named `LinesProblem` instead of a
tuple with a string (the outcome guard's G2); the reason it gives is unchanged. (2) Alice's 17:37
「只加入现在空闲且能被调度/执行的任务进入排序」 for the gates judged after the order: a capped
block's candidate that the reserve gate or the Runtime's admission (a budget, a window, a package
hold, a remedy round) defers is passed for its round (`capped::settle`, after the allocation; the
gate's code kept in `CappedMemory`), the plan, taken again from the round's starting reading,
leaving it out; the block carries fallbacks (what the round would plan once every candidate before
is passed), so the next one is tried in the same evaluation; a passed one is held
`capped_not_dispatchable` with that `gate_code`; a round with nothing left, or whose planned ones
left are no candidates while a consumer is, ends. A whole-instance hold as the cycle starts
(`FactRefreshInputs::instance_holds`, UPD-1's `InstanceHolds`), the random delay
(`successor_wait_codes`) and a chain step pass none: the round waits, as before. (3) A V2 pool with
both lines and no declared valuation compiles with the new warning `pool_lines_unvalued` (catalog
diagnostic, warning, policy fragment) at its `stop_line`; the compiler now returns a catalog's
warnings with it (`CompiledCatalog::warnings`, the accepted dry-run report) and refuses only on an
error. Tests: `ss2h_t18` (fails before: the refused limited member held the pool above its stop
line) and `ss2h_t19`; adapted, as fix 1 deliberately changes what they pinned: `ss2h_t5` (the
blacked-out member is passed, so the next round dispatches K first, where it stayed in its round
and ran next) and, with the busy instance held as the cycle starts as the Runtime gives it,
`ss2h_t5` and `ss2h_t9`. Still no configuration key, ledger shape or interface revision; a catalog
without valuations, lines and `benefit_limited` is unchanged byte for byte.

### 1.290 Slice CW-1 (0.12.47): the composed catalog's compile warnings are recorded and shown (#428; on 11-10 the standard packs of two games went live with pool lines and no valuation, and their `pool_lines_unvalued` (§1.289 fix 1) was nowhere: not in the ledger, `catalog.activated`, `standard_pack_registered`, `ac_overview` or actingd's log, against Fail Loud; the coordinator's ruling, not Alice's words: record and show them; coordinator work order `rd-1110/brief-cw1.md`)

[standard-pack-schedule.md](standard-pack-schedule.md) ("The scheduler workbench", "Compile
warnings"), [scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Pool lines"),
[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("Facts") and [runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md)
(the `ac_overview` row and its output budget) are the contract. The number is the next free one on
main `c76ce040`.

**Why.** The compiler returns its warnings with the compiled catalog (`CompiledCatalog::warnings`),
and only `actinglab scheduling compile` wrote them out. The workbench handed the composition over
through `compiled()` and read none; `StandardPackComposition::warnings()` holds only the
composer's own (unclassified packages, priority tiers).

**What.** (1) The composer places each compile warning in its game's `schedule.json` as it places a
refusal (`Composed::locate`), each place once, in the order game, code, pointer
(`StandardPackComposition::compile_warnings`, `StandardPackCompileWarning`). (2) **Record:** an
activation writes, on the `standard_pack_registered` record it writes today for each changed
`schedule.json`, the new optional value `compile_warnings` (records of `warning_code`, a code, and
`json_pointer`) when that file gave warnings; it writes no other record (fix 1), and a game
without warnings is recorded as before. Chosen over `catalog.activated`
because that record's payload (`CatalogTransitionEventData`, its audit `AuditInput`) is a typed
shape whose members the ledger reader checks, so a member there raises `ledger` (revision 5's
rule), while an outcome's values are what the reader only spells. (3) **Show:** after each
composition the active generation holds, the workbench records the program fact
`config.catalog_warnings` (runtime scope, `config.` re-observed; `ConfigCatalogWarnings`), every
game's warnings: count rows `{warning, game?, count}`, then place rows `{warning, game?, pointer}`
within the fact's 256 rows, a cut said by its last row (fix 1); only when it changes, never while
absent with no warning, and empty once the active generation has none. The overview (`actingctl overview`, `ac_overview`, and actinglab's through
`crates/lab-ops`) reads it from the RuntimeFactSnapshot it already reads and adds
`compile_warnings {count, codes, items}` to the `catalog` block; MCP cuts the `items` just
before the block.

**Interfaces.** None raised. `ledger`: a new outcome key in an existing record's values, and a new
key in the `config.` family of `runtime.fact_recorded` with the existing `RecordList` value; neither
is a member or a word of a closed vocabulary the reader checks (component-interfaces.md, the
`ledger` row of revision 5). `runtime-client`: no request or answer shape changes; the fact travels
in the existing `RuntimeFactSnapshot` answer, and `ConfigCatalog::from_fact_record` ignores members
it does not read. The `catalog` block of the overview's answer is presentation, as §1.243's rows.

**Unchanged.** A composition without warnings records and answers byte for byte as before: no
`compile_warnings`, no `config.catalog_warnings`, the `catalog` block as MCP-9a's. Compiling,
composing, activating and deciding are unchanged.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.46). Records that carry `compile_warnings` stay readable (an outcome's values);
`config.catalog_warnings` is a fact record of an existing shape, which an earlier build reads as
any other and does not load at its start (`config.` is re-observed).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CW1-1 | `standard_pack_registered`'s optional value `compile_warnings` (records `warning_code`, `json_pointer`); keys `compile_warnings`, `warning_code` | outcome values (no ledger shape) | CW-1 | runtime-host workbench | `since` 0.12.47; at most 64 with `compile_warnings_total`; only on the records an activation writes for changed files (fix 1) |
| CW1-2 | the program fact `config.catalog_warnings` | new key of the `config.` family (runtime scope, untagged) | CW-1 | runtime-host workbench | §4 below; the cut row `{counts_omitted, places_omitted}` last when rows were left out (fix 1) |
| CW1-3 | `catalog.compile_warnings {count, codes, items [{warning, game?, pointer}], items_omitted?, counts_omitted?}` | `actingctl overview` / `ac_overview` answer | CW-1 | lab-ops overview | absent without warnings; `items_omitted`, `counts_omitted` only when the fact was cut (fix 1); MCP cuts `items` before `catalog` |

The contracts are [resource-readings.md](resource-readings.md) ("List readings"),
[instance-fact-store.md](instance-fact-store.md) ("List reading facts" and the capacity ledger),
[ocr-fields.md](ocr-fields.md), [selection-policy.md](selection-policy.md) ("Record lists",
"Table maximum over a list", "In-task consumer", "Limits") and
[selection-graph.md](selection-graph.md) ("Select over a scan", "Ending empty", "Judge step",
"Records"); the planned revisions are in [component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md),
"Planned: Workflow #428 168". 1.291 was the next free number on `d06910c6` and still is on
`7910349a`, where LAB-3 added its rows under §1.287; S168-4, S168-5a and S168-5b add their rows
under this section.

**S168-0 itself.** Contracts only: no code, no test, no gate row, no CI file, no configuration
key, no code of the outcome catalog, and no live revision raised. The three pieces carry no game
word: a list of keyed rows read from a page, the largest integer of one table column over listed
keys, and a step that evaluates and records without input. Account data (what an instance holds,
what was judged worth) stays in the instance fact store and the ledger.

  evaluation is `unknown`; never 0.
- `table_list_max_validation`: a `boolean` or `enum_string` `value_column`, an undeclared list or
  table, empty `lists`, a 17th list, a repeated `fact_key`, a substitution, a tie-break key, a
  `fallback_column` and a 33rd distinct reference are validation errors, while 32 distinct
  references that occur more than 32 times are not; `evaluate_collect` and the catalog compile
  refuse a document that uses the source.
- `table_list_max_input_identity`: a changed cell of a contributing row, or a changed row of any
  listed list, moves `input_sha256`; a changed row of an unlisted key does not; a document
  without the source keeps its `policy_sha256` and `input_sha256` byte for byte.
- `table_list_max_union_of_lists`: `inventory.list.example_kind_a` holding {`member.a`,
  `member.b`} and `inventory.list.example_kind_b` holding {`member.b`, `member.d`} read the
  largest of the union {a, b, d}; `member.b`, in both lists, is looked up once and counts once;
  `count` is 3 and `fact_keys` names both lists in the order of `lists`.
- `table_list_max_unusable_list_is_unknown`, in two parts. (1) A direct read of one reference,
  its lists handed in a fake snapshot without the up-front check: with
  `inventory.list.example_kind_b` stale, the reference reads Unknown `fact_stale` whatever
  `inventory.list.example_kind_a` holds; with both lists unusable for different reasons, the
  reason is the first list's in the order of `lists`. (2) A whole evaluation of a document that
  declares the two lists in `facts[]` in the opposite order of `lists`, both unusable for
  different reasons: the up-front check ends the evaluation `unknown` before any candidate and
  before any list maximum is read, with no verdict, no `selection_table_list_max` reason, and the
  reason of the first unusable list in the declared order of `facts[]`.
- `table_list_max_where_skips_rows`: a `where` keeping `state.a` leaves out a row of `state.b`
  whose key the table lacks; that key is not looked up, is no miss and is not counted, and the
  read is the largest of the kept keys.
- `table_list_max_unknown_follows_the_declared_action`: a reference that reads Unknown
  `lookup_miss` (a key of the union without a row in the table; a null cell of the class), read
  by an `integer_compare` gate and by a term: under `drop_candidate` each candidate they assess
  is `unknown_dropped` with `lookup_miss`, and its verdict is no static table drop; under
  `abort_evaluation`, at the evaluator, the evaluation is `unknown` with `lookup_miss` and the
  rule (`gate_unknown_aborted` or `term_unknown_aborted` with the rule's `rule_id`), nothing is
  selected, and no candidate is ranked or scored; under either, no candidate is ranked on the
  value and nothing reads 0.

S168-5b, 7 tests, on fake snapshots whose lists a document reads through `keyed_fact`, tables
loaded with `LoadedTable::load`, and a fake device whose input port fails the test on any call.
Reading the lists through `keyed_fact` concerns the tests' fixtures only, not the order: S168-5b
still goes on main only after S168-4 and S168-5a merged ("Order" below).

- `judge_known_ends_with_outcome_key`: a judge over three slots whose candidates are all known,
  two judged worth and one not, writes one `task.selection_evaluated` with `judge_only`, the
  three verdicts' kinds, `selected` the two worth ones in rank order and `unknown_check`
  `blocking` `none`; the run is Completed on the step's page with the step's `outcome_key`, on
  the mapping with `judge_result` `judged`.
- `judge_unknown_slot_ends_with_unknown_key`: the same judge with one slot out of the dictionary
  writes the record with every verdict it has, `selected` the worth ones and `unknown_check`
  `blocking` `unknown_instances` with count 1; the run is Completed with the step's
  `unknown_outcome_key`, on the mapping with `judge_result` `unknown`.
- `judge_stale_list_ends_with_unknown_key`: with the declared list older than the document's
  `max_age_ms`, the record holds `unknown` with no verdict and reason `fact_stale`; the run is
  Completed with the step's `unknown_outcome_key`, never `selection_not_selected`.
- `judge_unknown_dropped_candidate_ends_with_unknown_key`: a judge whose document reads a table
  under `drop_candidate`, with every slot read: one run with one candidate whose key has no row
  in the table, and one with a candidate whose cell of the class is null and has no fallback,
  each drop that candidate `unknown_dropped`, a static table drop (`unknown_check.blocking`
  `none`, `unknown_instances` 0), and each end the run with the step's `unknown_outcome_key`, on
  the mapping with `judge_result` `unknown`; a run in which a gate decides against a candidate on
  a known value (the class gate's `absent`, an `integer_compare` whose operands are known) and
  nothing is `unknown_dropped` ends with the step's `outcome_key`.
- `judge_performs_no_input`: in the runs above the fake input port receives no call and
  the ledger holds no `task.effect_intent`, input or `task.effect_completed` of the step's
  action; a host handed an effect intent for a judge step's action ends that run
  `contained_task_judge_input_refused` before the device, and a run of another instance
  (`TESTSERIAL0002`) goes on; an architecture guard finds no input type in the kernel's judge
  module.
- `judge_declaration_refusals`: a missing `unknown_outcome_key`, the two keys equal, a `guard`,
  an `expect_after`, a `repeated_anchor` layout, a `scan`, a mode other than `none_allowed`, a
  `required_count` below the slots, a missing mapping for either result, a mapping with the
  wrong key, use as a prerequisite, and each `judge_result` rule (another string, an older
  schema, a task without a judge step, a page that is no judge step's `from` page, together with
  `busy`, a state reachable under both effect conditions) are each refused with the code and
  detail of the declaration tables; two mappings with the same effect condition, page and
  `judge_result` are refused `invalid_scheduling_outcome_declaration`, field `mapping_overlap`,
  while the pair `judged` and `unknown` on one condition and page is admitted.
- `judge_record_reader_rules`: the ledger reader takes `judge_only` with 0 or 2 selected, and an
  `unknown` record whose check counts 2 kept slots with `blocking` `none`; it refuses it with
  `multi_select`, a v2 projection, no `unknown_check`, `outranked_possible`, or a `selected` or
  `empty` record with `blocking` `none` and `unknown_instances` above 0; a reader of `ledger` 7
  refuses the record (`corrupt_ledger_record`).

**Order.** S168-4 and S168-5a go side by side: S168-5a depends on S168-0 only (its tests use
fake snapshots). They ship in one Runtime release, which may ship at any time; the second of the
two to merge declares `package` [3, 8], and until then the first one's merge admits its own
member by code ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md), "Planned: Workflow #428
168"). S168-5b goes on main only after S168-4 and S168-5a merged, that is, after main declares
`package` [3, 8]: its revision 9 is revision 8 plus the judge, and revision 8 holds S168-5a's
value source, so S168-5b never declares [3, 9] on a main without `table_max_over_list`. That its
tests read their lists through `keyed_fact` concerns their fixtures, not this order. It ships
in the Runtime release of LAB-6 and LAB-7. All three come before S168-6, the standard package's
slice; the offline slices S168-1 to S168-3 go on beside them. S168-7, the console's view, needs
a console whose `ledger` range holds 8, which is UI-L1's console.

**What each changes at deploy.**

- S168-4 and S168-5a, one release: the Runtime declares `package` [3, 8]. No pack declares a list
  or reads a list maximum yet, so no run changes. A client's publication under `inventory.list.`
  is refused from it, and so is a mark under that prefix (S168-4's report says that no package on
  the four resource repositories' `main` declares one). A document without the new source
  behaves byte for byte as before. The ledger, the configuration and the capacity are unchanged;
  a rollback below `package` 8 stays open.
- S168-5b, in the release of LAB-6 and LAB-7, on main after S168-4 and S168-5a merged: `package`
  [3, 9] and `ledger` [3, 8], #434's revision 8, shared. One way by the Rp.max rule: once the
  Runtime that declares `ledger` 8 has
  run, going back below it is refused, whether or not a judge step ran; and the Runtime combines
  only with a console whose `ledger` range holds 8, so it is deployed with or after UI-L1's
  console. No configuration key. A package without a judge step and a mapping without
  `judge_result` behave byte for byte as before.

**Where S168-0 differs from the design or the work order.**

- (a) The design reads 256 active fact identities per instance; the store holds 256 for the whole
  host, shared by every instance, and the contracts book lists there.
- (b) A list maximum reads 1 to 16 lists at once, over the union of their keys, each key counted
  once (the coordinator's ruling R1 after the review, work order
  `rd-1110/brief-s168-contracts-fix1.md`; the first work order had one list per reference). The
  holdings split into 8 lists (Q-5) over 9 domains (Q-2) would otherwise take at least 48
  references; a document holds at most 32 distinct list maxima. Any listed list that is not usable makes
  the reference Unknown with its reason; `empty` is read only when every list is usable and no
  key of the union is of the class ([selection-policy.md](selection-policy.md), "Table maximum
  over a list").
- (c) A list reading reads only a `repeated_anchor` layout over a scan: a list that fits one
  viewport declares the scan too, as an `on_empty` select does, so every written list has
  positive evidence of both ends.
- (d) The judge's run ends with one of two keys (the coordinator's ruling R4 after the review,
  made exact by the ruling F3 of fix 3): `outcome_key` only when the evaluation is known, the
  unknown check does not block and no candidate of the layout was dropped because a read was
  Unknown (no candidate `unknown_dropped`, a static table drop included), `unknown_outcome_key`
  otherwise, both Completed and neither with an input, as the design (§9) tells a judgment from
  "could not judge". A candidate a gate decides against on a known value is a judgment and does
  not count. A mapping tells the two
  apart on one page by its member `judge_result`, a closed vocabulary of `judged` and `unknown`
  ([selection-graph.md](selection-graph.md), "Judge step", "Mapping the two keys"): `on_empty`'s
  means, one mapping per page and effect condition, cannot, because both keys end on the same
  page under the same condition. The record tells the rest apart (the decision's own outcome key
  and `unknown_check`).
- (e) The table digests behind a judge's decision are the run's existing
  `standard_pack_table_read` records, not a new member of the record.
- (f) A judge reads one frame of a `fixed_slots` layout: a scan moves the list, which is input.

**Open points** for the coordinator.

1. The `ledger` number, **answered by R3** (the coordinator's ruling after the review): S168-5b
   ships in the same Runtime release as LAB-6 and LAB-7 and shares #434's planned `ledger` 8; it
   does not take 8 ahead of LAB-6 and does not move #434's row to 9. If the releases come in
   another order, the coordinator renumbers at that release
   ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md), "Planned: Workflow #428 168").
2. Fail-closed costs for S168-6, **answered by R2** (the coordinator's ruling after the review):
   a position whose identity the package's dictionary lacks keeps the whole list unwritten, so
   the dictionary covers every identity the list can show (the design's G-3); and what S168-2's
   table owes a list maximum is the rule of [selection-policy.md](selection-policy.md), "Table
   maximum over a list", "What the table owes a list maximum": a missing row of a class says
   the identity is not of the class, so an identity of the class whose value is not known has a
   row of the class with a null cell, and is never placed in another class only to have a row.
3. A run's lists are written at its end: a judge reads lists of earlier runs only, so the
   standard package reads its lists in a task that runs before its judge task.
4. One key per judge run, **answered by R4** (the coordinator's ruling after the review): the
   judge ends with `outcome_key` or `unknown_outcome_key`, mapped by `judge_result`, in S168-5b
   (difference (d)), so a catalog can react to "could not judge" without a later slice.
5. `actinglab replay` reports marks' readings but not a list's rows; an authoring aid for S168-6
   that a later Lab slice may add.

**Rollback.** Nothing to roll back: text only.

**Tests.** New: policy row "#428 S168-5a", the register's nine named tests in
`actingcommand-selection-policy::lib::gate_428_s168_5a` (`table_list_max_reads_largest_of_class`,
`table_list_max_empty_and_out_of_class`, `table_list_max_missing_key_is_unknown`,
`table_list_max_validation`, `table_list_max_input_identity`, `table_list_max_union_of_lists`,
`table_list_max_unusable_list_is_unknown`, `table_list_max_where_skips_rows`,
`table_list_max_unknown_follows_the_declared_action`), on tables loaded with `LoadedTable::load`
and fake snapshots, no clock and no sleep; and the catalog compile's half of test 4,
`actingcommand-policy::lib::source::tests::table_list_max_validation`. No test adapted; no golden
re-recorded (test 5 reads the DB-2 golden of a document without tables).

**Interface.** `package` stays [3, 7] in this build: S168-4 had not merged on `fa8adc67`, so
S168-5a is the first of the two and admits its member by code; S168-4 declares [3, 8]. No
`ledger`, `runtime-client`, `actingd-config` or `runtime-outcomes` raise: the reason is a decision
reason the record reader only spells.

**Outcome codes.** One code added, `selection_table_list_max` (info / none, pending, since
0.12.50, owner `selection-policy`); three keys added, `fact_keys`, `maximum`, `maximum_identity`.
`term_fallback_used` and the vocabulary `unknown_reason` are reused. No persisted structure
change.

**Contract wording this slice changed** (named by fix 1, work order
`rd-1110/brief-s168-5a-fix1.md`). Two sentences of [selection-policy.md](selection-policy.md),
"Table maximum over a list", besides its opening line, which now says that S168-5a built the
section:

- "One read", step 1: a listed list that is malformed now includes, by name, two rows that its
  entry's `where` keeps sharing one key, as the up-front check reads it (reading (a) below).
- "Audit": a pin's `term_fallback_used` now carries `rule_id`, the gate or term that reads the
  reference first, and `table_column`, the pin's column, one per such pin in the order of
  `pins` (reading (b) below).

The independent review before fix 1 found both faithful to the contract's meaning.

**Where S168-5a reads the contract.**

- (a) Step 1's "malformed" includes two rows of one list that its entry's `where` keeps sharing
  one key, as the up-front check reads a reference's list: the up-front check now indexes each
  list a list maximum reads with its `where`, as it does a `keyed_fact` reference's. Written into
  selection-policy.md, step 1.
- (b) A pin's `term_fallback_used` requires a `rule_id`: the gate or term that reads the reference
  first, one reason per pin that used its `otherwise`, in pin order. Written into "Audit".
- (c) "Nor can a `fallback_column` name it": the reference decodes an optional `fallback_column`
  only so that validation refuses it `type_mismatch`, as the contract says, not the decoder.
- (d) What an abort keeps; existing behaviour that this slice does not change (corrected by fix
  1, work order `rd-1110/brief-s168-5a-fix1.md`). Under `abort_evaluation` the evaluator's
  decision keeps the verdicts of the candidates it assessed until then, none given a rank, the
  last of them that of the candidate whose rule ended the evaluation (`unknown_dropped`, with
  `gate_unknown_aborted` or `term_unknown_aborted` and the rule's `rule_id`;
  `evaluate_with_tables` in `crates/selection-policy/src/evaluator.rs`); an evaluation the
  up-front check ends, before any candidate, keeps no verdict. What the record
  `task.selection_evaluated` keeps of an abort depends on the step. A single-frame select's
  record keeps the decision's verdicts as they are, the aborting candidate's included
  (`selection_record`, `record_verdicts(&decision.candidates)` in
  `crates/execution-kernel/src/contained_task/selection.rs`). A select over a scan's record keeps
  none (`scan_selection_record`, in the same file; [selection-graph.md](selection-graph.md),
  "Record per path": "an abort keeps no verdict"). A judge step's record, as its contract plans
  it for S168-5b, keeps none ([selection-graph.md](selection-graph.md), "Execution of a judge
  step", step 4 and the table of results: "`unknown`, no verdict"). Test 9 checks the evaluator
  only: the evaluation is `unknown` with the read's reason and the rule, and no candidate is
  ranked or scored.
- (e) Test 4's catalog half is a test of the same name in `crates/policy`: the selection-policy
  crate does not link the catalog compiler. Test 4 also refuses a list that is no record list, a
  `where` outside its list's values, a gate predicate other than `integer_compare`, a `lookup`
  transform and an `empty` outside the safe integers; test 9 also checks the upper bound.

**What S168-5a changes live.** Nothing runs differently: no package reads a list maximum before
S168-6, and a document without the source keeps its canonical bytes, `policy_sha256`,
`input_sha256` and reasons. Admission takes a document that reads the source; a build before it
refuses one as an unknown value source. The ledger, the configuration and the capacity are
unchanged.

**S168-5a rollback** (to the release before it). Open, as for any release below `package` 8: no
package uses the source until S168-6, which comes after S168-4 and S168-5a.
