### 1.314 Slice R-6b (contracts only): a run the scheduler started can be stopped, and settles as a stop (Workflow #429 A.2 contract point 2 and the slice row R-6, board #429 6535257381; R-6's first slice refused a policy run until `ledger` 8, §1.302 "Left for later slices"; R-8's "close this task" needs it for its second step, §1.308; the coordinator's eight rulings of 11-11, not Alice's words; read on main `385bb500`; coordinator work order `rd-1111/brief-r6b-contract.md`)

[runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) (the row `StopInstanceRun`),
[policy-suspension.md](policy-suspension.md) (the new "A stopped run", and its opening),
[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Settlement Feedback And Eligibility Age", "Runtime
Enforcement", "Clock-slot records", "Capped spending order", "No-progress guard"),
[runtime-fact-store.md](runtime-fact-store.md) (the settlement facts),
[lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) (the `ui` entry's row of `StopInstanceRun`),
[lab-operations.json](lab-operations.json) (the row `task stop`, its `notes`) and
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) (the new "Planned: Workflow #429 R-6b") are the
contract. The number 1.314 is the coordinator's: §1.310 to §1.313 are held for four code slices
open the same day.

**R-6b itself.** Contracts only: no code, no test, no schema file, no gate row, no CI file, no
configuration key, no outcome code and no live revision raised. Every rule it adds is marked
"(R-6b, not built yet)" or written in a section that says so. The outcome catalog's descriptions,
the code's comments, the `help` line of the row `task stop`, `component-interfaces.json` and the
tests are the code slice's. The text names no game.

**Why.** R-6's first slice (0.12.53, §1.302) stops a client's direct run only: a run the scheduler
started is refused (`scheduled_contained_task_not_client_cancellable`, `run_origin` `policy`),
because `policy.execution_recorded` of `ledger` 7 has no legal form for a scheduled run that ends
neither as a success, nor as a counted failure, nor as a condition. On production nearly every run
is the scheduler's, so the console's "close this task" and the Lab's `task stop` stop almost
nothing a person wants stopped; today only a pause of the whole account does. 0.12.55 raises
`ledger` to 8 anyway (S168-LB1a), one way, so the stop of a scheduled run takes the same revision.

**The rulings** (11-11, the coordinator's, not Alice's words), as the contract writes them:
(1) `StopInstanceRun` stops a scheduled run from every counter that sends it today (the Lab's
`task stop`, the console, an agent through the Lab's tool) exactly as a direct run: asked at its
next checkpoint, reset by the Runtime with the run's lease before its terminal, the same wait,
`settled` and `reset`; a run the Runtime started for itself stays refused with `run_origin` `host`;
(2) it settles as an interruption, neither a success nor a failure: no failure count, streak,
backoff, ladder, suspension of a sensitive task, owed rerun or condition, counted under the routine
summary's `interruptions`; (3) what the scheduler does next is the trigger's business, not the
stop's, said per trigger below; (4) the smallest legal form of the record in `ledger` 8, with what
every reader does with it; (5) a restart between the stop and the settlement; (6) a failed reset as
for a direct run; (7) what a person sees, and every text that says a policy run is refused until
`ledger` 8; (8) the interfaces.

**The form, and why it is the smallest** (ruling 4; [policy-suspension.md](policy-suspension.md),
"A stopped run"). Three forms were weighed:

- *A failure with one more optional member* (an interruption flag): every member of a failure
  (the two classes, the streak, the escalation streak, the disposition, the retry, the sensitivity,
  the performance context) would need a value that means nothing for a stop, and every reader that
  takes a `failed` result as a failure (the task snapshot's `failed`, the settlement fold's streak,
  `failures_through`, the ledger's recovery check, the frame retention, `actingd suspended`) would
  go on reading it as one unless taught otherwise, with nothing to say where.
- *A failure read as a stop by its code*, no shape change: the record's check would have to admit
  a failure with no count and a sensitive task's failure without a pause, the same readers would be
  wrong by default, and the tools of the release before would show every stop as a failure.
- *A third result kind*, `{"kind": "stopped", "outcome", "runtime_ms"}` (chosen; the spelling is
  proposed, question 1): two members, each with a meaning for a stop (its cause, the run's time),
  and none of a failure's; every reader that matches on the kind must decide what a stop is, and
  the compiler names each one.

Nothing but the revisions moves: SQLite format 2, `actingcommand.event.v3`, the record types, the
tables, the indexes, every view's type list and the record's other members stay as they are. The
record's stored severity is its outcome's category, as for every result-bearing record. `ledger`
moves because a reader of revision 7 cannot decode the kind; `runtime-client` moves with it,
because every event query page carries the record's result (difference (f)).

**What a stopped run leaves, per trigger** (ruling 3; each "(R-6b, not built yet)"):

| What | After a stop |
|---|---|
| a clock slot's occurrence O | served: O is served by the pair's first admitted dispatch after it ("Clock-slot records"), so the stopped dispatch served O at its admission and the next evaluation does not dispatch the same O; no clock-slot record. The records allow the coordinator's wish as they are: nothing is built for it |
| the stopped task's `dependency_completed` with `since_own_run` (it is the successor) | due again ("its latest run did not succeed"): dispatched again once its cooldown, counted from its dispatch, has passed and its trigger holds |
| a successor's `dependency_completed` on the stopped task (it is the predecessor) | not triggered: the predecessor's terminal state is `cancelled`, which `terminal_states` of `succeeded` or `failed` does not accept; a successor that lists `cancelled`, a word the catalog format already has, is triggered; no chain handover, which needs a success |
| `fact_time_reached` with `once_per_reading` | not served (serving needs a success): true again, dispatched again after its cooldown |
| a pool reading, a `resource_projection` | unchanged: a stopped run publishes no reading, as a failed one, so the pool keeps its last reading until the next reading or its expiry; what the run spent before the stop is real and shows only then |
| the task's cooldown | from the dispatch, as for every run: no end starts a cooldown (difference (a)) |
| the no-progress guard | not held: the guard its admission armed holds only a guarded dispatch that succeeded |
| a capped episode | the stopped consumer was dispatched in its round (`last_dispatched_unix_ms`): the plan counts its whole consumption, the round does not list it again and never passes it; the head after it is checked against the pool's last reading, which the stop did not renew; the episode ends or goes on by its own rule |
| the Runtime's own reruns its dispatch served (an immediate rerun's round, an owed rerun, a remedy retry or request) | end with it (proposed, question 3) |
| a fact refresh read | stopped as any policy run; not one of its failures in a row, no failure backoff; its demand stays, and its `min_interval_ms` counts from its dispatch |

**Where the contract differs from the rulings or completes them**, each reported to the
coordinator:

- (a) Ruling 3, the cooldown: the evaluator counts every cooldown from the pair's last dispatch
  (`last_dispatched_unix_ms`, its admission; "Task Execution Fields"; `evaluator.rs`,
  `cooldown_until`), never from an end, so "the cooldown runs from the stop as from any end" has no
  end to follow. The contract keeps the cooldown from the dispatch (question 5).
- (b) Ruling 3, the guard: every admission arms the pair's guard, the stopped one's too; the guard
  holds only a guarded dispatch that succeeded, so a stopped pair is not held. The effect is the
  ruling's; "not armed" is not.
- (c) Ruling 3, the clock slot: allowed by the records as they are (the table above).
- (d) Ruling 5: the stop's own records do not name the run. `command.received` and
  `command.validated` carry the stop's request, the instance, the action `runtime_action` and an
  empty audit input, and a stop answered from the instance's latest stopped run writes the same
  `command.validated`. With a terminal, the terminal is enough: on a scheduled run only the stop
  asks `ClientRequested` (`CancelContainedTask` refuses a scheduled run), so `contained_task_cancelled`
  on a scheduled run's `task.failed` is a stop's, and the run settles `stopped` from it. Without a
  terminal the ledger cannot tell, and the run settles as interrupted, as today (question 2).
- (e) Ruling 7: `CancelContainedTask` (MCP `ac_stop_run`, actinglab `run stop`) keeps refusing a
  scheduled run with `scheduled_contained_task_not_client_cancellable` (without `run_origin`),
  unchanged, so the code stays for a host run in `StopInstanceRun` and for every scheduled run in a
  client's own cancel. The token `policy` of the vocabulary `run_origin` stays registered, no longer
  produced by the stop.
- (f) Ruling 8: `runtime-client` moves too. An event query page carries the record's
  `policy_result` (codes only in the public projection's `policy_execution_outcome`, whole in a full
  read), which a client of revision 6 cannot decode; R-6b joins the planned 7 of S168-LB1a, whose
  console the release already pairs.
- (g) Ruling 1: a policy run's control enters the run registry only after its package's preparation
  (`run_scheduled_contained_task`: `prepare_scheduled_package`, then `begin_contained_run`), while
  its activity `policy_run` shows from the preparation; a stop sent then is refused
  `contained_task_cancellation_identity_missing` (question 8). A direct run is registered before its
  lease.
- (h) Ruling 1: for a policy run `settled: true` means, as for a direct run, that the run left the
  registry (its terminal and lease end written); its `policy.execution_recorded` follows on the run's
  worker, so a read right after the answer may not hold it yet.
- (i) Ruling 2: a stop takes precedence over two settings that could reach it: a
  `scheduling.rerun.condition_codes` that names `contained_task_cancelled` does not make it a
  condition, and a `recovery_ladder.triggers` that names it starts no ladder (the defaults name it in
  neither). The scheduled cancel branch notes no ladder trigger and computes no failure identity for
  a stopped run.
- (j) Rulings 2 and 4, readers the rulings do not name: the task snapshot (`terminal_state`
  `cancelled`, the evaluator's existing word, which the host never projected before), the
  settlement facts and the snapshot's `last_duration_ms` and `failure_streak` (question 7), the
  failure count of the pair's later runs (`failures_through`), the frame retention's match of a
  settlement with its terminal, `actingd suspended`, `ac_diagnose` and the client's run summary of a
  fixture run.
- (k) Ruling 4, the routine summary: nothing to build. R-12 already counts a scheduled run's failure
  terminal with `contained_task_cancelled` as an interruption (`RunEnd::of_terminal`, §1.264).
- (l) Ruling 6: a policy run's failed lease end may hand its instance to a ladder today (when a
  trigger names its terminal's code); a stopped run's, after a failed reset, never does. The fence holds the instance, its pairs wait with
  `dispatch_resource_fenced`, and a self-check lifts it, as §1.302 says for a direct run.
- (m) A stop that loses the race to the run's deadline or to a pause's drain keeps the run's own
  end (an ordinary failure, `contained_task_deadline_exceeded`, or a condition,
  `contained_task_paused`) and answers `reset: not_needed`, as for a direct run.
- (n) Ruling 7, the texts that say a policy run is refused until `ledger` 8. Rewritten here:
  [runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) (the row `StopInstanceRun`),
  [lab-operations.json](lab-operations.json) (the row `task stop`, its `notes`) and
  [lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) (the `ui` entry's row). Kept as the record of 0.12.53:
  §1.302 (its title, "Why not a policy run", "Left for later slices", "What an operator sees").
  For the code slice: the row `task stop`'s `help` ("a scheduled run ... is refused"), the comments
  of `crates/runtime-host/src/host/stop_instance_run.rs` (the module's description) and of
  `contained_task.rs` (`stop_refused_origin`), and the catalog's descriptions of
  `scheduled_contained_task_not_client_cancellable`, of the key `run_origin` and of its vocabulary.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R6B-1 | `StopInstanceRun` of a policy run, a fact refresh read included | behaviour of an R-0 kind (no shape change) | R-6b | the host (`stop_target`; `stop_refused_origin` refuses a host run only) | asked `ClientRequested` at its next checkpoint, as a direct run; the same wait, `settled` and `reset`; a host run (a startup package, a ladder rung, an idle action's rest) stays refused with `run_origin` `host` |
| R6B-2 | the Runtime's reset of a stopped policy run | behaviour | R-6b | the host (the cancel branch of `execute_contained_task_with_lease`, `reset_stopped_run`) | for a scheduled run too, with the run's lease, before its terminal; a failed reset fences that instance only (#419), its lease ends as a failed run's and hands the instance to no ladder; the fence's failure is the success code's cause |
| R6B-3 | `policy.execution_recorded` result kind `stopped` `{outcome, runtime_ms}` | ledger shape (`ledger` 8, shared); wire shape in the event reads (`runtime-client` 7, shared) | R-6b | actingcommand-contract (`PolicyExecutionOutcome`, planned `Stopped`; its check; the public projection) | proposed spelling; `outcome` the terminal outcome's top node, codes only in the projection; the check asks only that it is a code; its severity its outcome's category |

**Questions for the coordinator, each with the answer the contract proposes.**

1. *The kind's spelling.* Proposed: `stopped` (`PolicyExecutionOutcome::Stopped`,
   `PolicyExecutionInput::Stopped`). `interrupted` is taken in the code by the interrupted
   settlement (`policy_settlement_interrupted`, `settled_as_interrupted`,
   `is_interrupted_settlement`), which is a counted failure. The routine summary's column stays
   `interruptions`.
2. *A restart with no terminal.* Proposed: the interrupted settlement, as today (difference (d)):
   the case is an abrupt end between the stop's request and the run's next checkpoint (a deploy's
   drain lets the stopped run reach its checkpoint first), and the restart lifts the pair's first
   interrupted settlement. Alternative: the stop's `command.validated` names the run (the run's
   `task_id` and `run_id` links) and the recovery settles it `stopped`; the run views and the
   client's run summary would then meet a run-linked record of another request and must learn to
   skip it.
3. *The Runtime's own reruns the stopped run served.* Proposed: they end with it: an immediate
   rerun's round ends as at `policy_retry_round_ended`, an owed rerun is removed, a remedy retry
   closes its round as a failed retry does but without a failure, and a provider's request is used;
   by the record, so replay agrees; the pair then waits for its own trigger and cooldown. Without
   it, a stopped immediate or owed rerun is offered again at the next evaluation, past its
   cooldown and promoted, and the stop is undone within a cycle. Against: the letter of ruling 3.
4. *Counts and runtime.* Proposed: the counts the admission took stay taken (the occurrence was
   served, as ruling 3 wants for a clock slot), the run's runtime counts in the task's and the
   activity's windows as a success's, and it is never re-judged as over its runtime budget.
   Alternative: a refund as a condition gives, which lets a task limited to one run a day run again
   the same day.
5. *The cooldown.* Proposed: from the dispatch, as for every run (difference (a)); a task whose
   stopped run outlasted its cooldown may be dispatched at the next evaluation while its trigger
   holds, which a closing row (R-8) or a pause prevents. Alternative: a cooldown from the stop, for
   stops only, a new input of the evaluator.
6. *The terminal, and what the run views show.* Proposed: the `task.failed` with
   `contained_task_cancelled` that every scheduled cancel writes, so `actingctl runs`, `ac_runs` and
   the console's run list show the run `failed` with that code and its settlement `stopped`.
   Alternative: a `task.cancelled`, as a direct run's, shown `cancelled`; the start's reconciliation
   (`policy_run_terminal_conflict` today), the ledger's recovery, the retention and the run summary
   would then need a third terminal of a scheduled run.
7. *The settlement facts and the snapshot's last duration and streak.* Proposed: a stopped run is
   no settlement for them (they keep the pair's latest success or failure; a cut-short duration is
   no cost), while `terminal_state` shows `cancelled`. Alternative: `last_outcome` `stopped`, a
   third value of a string fact that a catalog may compare.
8. *A stop during the policy run's preparation* (difference (g)). Proposed: the code slice
   registers a policy run's control when its activity begins, before its package's preparation, as
   a direct run's is registered before its lease, and the run ends at its first checkpoint; if that
   is not cheap, the refusal stays and the console sends the stop again.

**The coordinator's answers (2026-11-11, on reading this contract; the coordinator's, not Alice's
words).** The differences (a) to (n) above are accepted as written, and every answer the contract
proposes stands: each "(proposed)" in the texts of this slice reads as settled, and the code slice
drops the mark where it builds the rule. On the questions:

1. As proposed: `stopped`.
2. As proposed: a restart with no terminal settles the run as interrupted, as today. The stop's
   own records do not learn to name the run.
3. As proposed: the Runtime's own reruns the stopped dispatch served end with it, by the record,
   so that replay agrees. A person's stop is not undone by a rerun the Runtime owes itself; the
   pair then waits for its own trigger and cooldown.
4. As proposed: the counts stay taken and the runtime counts; no refund, no runtime-budget
   rewrite.
5. As proposed: the cooldown counts from the dispatch. The code slice says plainly where a person
   reads it (the row `StopInstanceRun` of runtime-interface.md and the `help` of the row
   `task stop`) that a stop ends this run only: a task whose trigger still holds is dispatched
   again once its cooldown has passed, at the next evaluation when the stopped run outlasted it,
   and a closing row (R-8) or a pause keeps it from running. A cooldown from the stop is not
   built; if use shows the need, it is a slice of its own.
6. As proposed: the terminal stays `task.failed` with `contained_task_cancelled`, and this slice
   changes no run view; the console words such a run as stopped, from its code.
7. As proposed.
8. As proposed: the code slice registers a policy run's control before its package's preparation.
   If the code shows that this cannot be done without changing how a failed preparation ends, the
   refusal stays, the register says so, and the console sends the stop again once.

The code slice is built as the two the contract offers, R-6b1 (the form, its check, every reader
and the ledger's recovery rule) and then R-6b2 (the stop and the settlement that write it), in the
same release.

**The code slice.**

| Slice | Repository | Size | What | Depends on | Interfaces |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-6b | Runtime | L (about four work orders: the form and its check; the stop and the live settlement; the decision memory and the projections; the restart, the other readers, the texts and the tests) | R6B-1 to R6B-10 | this contract and the coordinator's answers, questions 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 before it starts (each changes what it builds); main with R-8 (`385bb500`, there); no code of S168-LB1a, LAB-6 or S168-5b (it shares their revisions and `component-interfaces.json` only) | `ledger` [3, 8], `runtime-client` [3, 7]: joined when S168-LB1a (or LAB-6, S168-5b) merged first, raised when R-6b merges first; `package`, `actingd-config` do not move |

It may be split in two of the same release: R-6b1, the form, its check, every reader and the
ledger's recovery rule (nothing writes the form; it takes the revisions), and R-6b2, the stop and
the settlement that write it. No heavy computation is needed.

**Interfaces** ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md), "Planned: Workflow #429
R-6b"). `ledger` 8 and `runtime-client` 7, shared: when S168-LB1a merged first, R-6b joins both and
raises nothing; when R-6b merges first, it raises `ledger` to [3, 8] and `runtime-client` to [3, 7],
and S168-LB1a (and LAB-6, S168-5b, for `ledger`) join them; one raise for the release.
`package` does not move (no pack or bundle member), `actingd-config` does not move (no key; the two
settings a stop takes precedence over keep their shapes and values), and `runtime-outcomes` stays 1
(no code; three descriptions change within it).

**Identity.** A ledger with no stopped record reads, replays, projects and decides byte for byte as
before; a catalog and a pack are untouched.

**Tests that pin today's refusal** (the code slice changes them, the ruling changing what they
pin): `runtime-host`'s `gate_429_r6::r6_a_host_run_and_a_policy_run_are_refused_with_their_origin_and_nothing_is_cancelled`
(its policy half) and `gate_429_r8::r8_closing_a_task_then_stopping_its_run` (its policy half: the
second step now stops the scheduled run); `actinglab-architecture`'s
`the_runtime_declares_each_v0120_interface_revision_once` moves to the ranges it declares. Its work
order names its new tests; the contract proposes one each for: a stopped policy run (its reset on
its lease, its terminal, its `stopped` record, no streak, backoff, pause, ladder, condition or owed
rerun, an interruption in the routine summary); a sensitive task's stopped run, not paused; the
replay of a stopped record at a start; the restart from its terminal; a restart with no terminal;
a failed reset that fences only its instance and starts no ladder; the clock occurrence served; a
stopped capped consumer; the snapshot's `cancelled`; a host run still refused.

**What changes live** (the code slice, 0.12.55). A scheduled run can be stopped from the console's
"close this task" (R-8's second step now acts on it), from actinglab `task stop` and from an agent
through the Lab's tool: it ends at its next checkpoint, the Runtime resets the device with the run's
lease (its record shows one `InputReset` before its lease's release), and the stop answers
`settled` and `reset` as for a direct run. The run's terminal is `task.failed` with
`contained_task_cancelled`, its settlement `stopped`: nothing counts as a failure, nothing retries,
backs off, pauses or enters a ladder, no rerun is owed, and the routine summary counts it under
`interruptions`. A host run, and every scheduled run through `ac_stop_run` and `run stop`, stay
refused. Tools and a console of revision 6 cannot read an event page that holds a stopped record,
so the console of the release is deployed with it.

**Rollback.** Going back below `ledger` 8 is refused by the Rp.max rule once the Runtime of the
release has run, whether or not a stop was recorded (the same for every slice of revision 8). The
way back is a later build or a fresh state root; there is no migration, and the configuration needs
nothing. A console of `runtime-client` 6 cannot read event pages that hold a stopped record.

**Rollback of this slice.** Nothing to roll back: text only.

*Read with §1.316 (R-6b2):* the "no ladder" that (l) and the row R6B-2 say of a failed reset is
said of the stopped run's own terminal and lease end, which start no ladder whatever
`recovery_ladder.triggers` lists, while the fence a failed reset leaves is handed on by the lease
sweep as every fence is (#403, #419), to a `resource_fence` ladder or to a person.

  read the activity as shown from the preparation; the code begins it after the preparation, since
  it names the prepared package's `package_id` (R-0b), and the run's request appears in no record
  before its lifecycle, which also follows the preparation. A stop that names a run read from the
  status or the records therefore always found its control registered; the registration now
  precedes the preparation as answer 8 asks. This slice does not change the activity. The
  coordinator's ruling on reading this (2026-11-11, not Alice's words): the code stands, and the
  activity row of runtime-interface.md is corrected at the merge to say what the code does (the
  activity begins once the package is prepared).
- *A pause's drain during the preparation.* With the control registered, a scheduling pause's
  drain sees a physical policy run during its preparation too (it saw a fixture-simulated one
  already) and, at its drain timeout, asks it to stop; the run then ends at its first check
  `contained_task_paused`, as any run in flight. Before, the drain saw the physical run only from
  its registration after the preparation.
- *Settlement facts.* A stopped record writes none of the four (rather than writing the pair's
  previous settlement again).
- *The policy driver's diagnostic.* As for every scheduled cancel, the driver records the run's
  error as a `runtime.failed` warning (`record_scheduled_policy_failure`); it counts nothing and no
  reader of a stop takes it as a failure. Unchanged.
- *A test seam.* `ContainedTaskCheckpointPoint::ScheduledPreparation` (test builds only), after the
  control's registration and before the package is read.

**What an operator sees after deploy.** A scheduled run can be stopped from the console's "close
this task" (R-8's second step now acts on it), from actinglab `task stop` and from an agent
through the Lab's tool: it ends at its next check, or at its first one when the stop came while it
prepared its package; the Runtime resets the device with the run's lease (one `InputReset` before
the lease's release); the stop answers `settled` and `reset` as for a direct run. `actingctl runs`
and `ac_runs` show the run `failed` with `contained_task_cancelled`; its `policy.execution_recorded`
is `stopped`; nothing counts as a failure, retries, backs off or pauses, the run starts no ladder
of its own (the fence a failed reset leaves is handed on as every fence is, to a `resource_fence`
ladder or to a person), no rerun is owed and a rerun the dispatch served ends; the routine
summary counts it under `interruptions`; the task snapshot shows `cancelled`. A host run, and
every scheduled run through `ac_stop_run` and `run stop`, stay refused. A console of
`runtime-client` 6 cannot read an event page that holds a stopped record, so the console of the
release is deployed with it.

**Tests** (gate rows `#429 R-6b2` in `contracts/test-gates/host.toml` and `policy.toml`; neutral
ids, a manual clock, no sleep): through the host (`gate_429_r6b2`), a stopped policy run end to end
(the reset on its lease before its release, its terminal, its `stopped` record, the later stop's
`settled` and `reset: done`, no streak, failure state, retry round or owed rerun held and replayed
alike, no ladder, the snapshot `cancelled`, an interruption in the routine summary); a sensitive
task's stopped run not paused; the stop over `scheduling.rerun.condition_codes` and a
`recovery_ladder.triggers` item naming `contained_task_cancelled`; the live settlement of a stopped
owed rerun; the restart from the terminal (`stopped`) and with no terminal (interrupted); a failed
reset fencing only its instance, the stop starting no ladder of its own (none of the stage `task`,
of the trigger item or of the run; the fence's `resource_fence` ladder allowed, not required),
while the other instance's run completes; a stop during the preparation; a stopped fact refresh
read. In the decision memory (`policy_control`), the
live input: an immediate rerun's round, an owed rerun and a remedy retry ended; never a condition,
never over its budget, a condition refused. In the evaluator (`policy` crate): the clock
occurrence served, a `once_per_reading` reading not served and the task dispatched after its
cooldown from the dispatch (`gate_405_cf1`); a stopped fact refresh reader neither exhausted nor
backed off (`gate_d2_s4`).
Changed: `gate_429_r6::r6_a_host_run_and_a_policy_run_are_refused_with_their_origin_and_nothing_is_cancelled`,
its policy half (a policy run is asked to stop), renamed
`r6_a_host_run_is_refused_with_its_origin_and_a_policy_run_is_asked_to_stop` with its `[[retired]]`
entry in `ci/retired-gates.toml`; `gate_429_r8::r8_closing_a_task_then_stopping_its_run`, its policy
half (the second step asks the scheduled run to stop), name kept; the test helpers
`begin_uncancellable_run_for_test` and `end_uncancellable_run_for_test` (renamed from
`..._unstoppable_...`). No golden, schema or census reads the `help` of `task stop`; the tests that
read it read the table at run time.

**Rollback.** `ledger` 8 is one way (the Rp.max rule): once the Runtime of the release has run,
going back below it is refused, whether or not a stop was recorded, and after the first stop a
stopped record exists that no build before R-6b1 decodes. A revert of R-6b2's code alone returns to
refusing a policy run's stop (the readers of R-6b1 stay and read nothing new). The configuration
needs nothing.

**The mapping**, one table applied in this order by the slice's script, exact bytes, each count

### 1.318 Slice CLI-COMP (0.12.55): Tab completes `actinglab`'s command lines in PowerShell and bash (Workflow #434; the customer-view audit of 2026-11-11 asked for a command line a person can use without the manual; the coordinator's eight rulings of the same day, not Alice's words; the read-only survey `rd-1111/survey-cli4.md` §2, on main `a62434a4`; coordinator work order `rd-1111/brief-cli-completion.md`, read on main `fed839c2`)

The number is the coordinator's: §1.315 to §1.317 and §1.319 are open at the same time.
[lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) §9.3, "Completion", is the contract. No persisted shape,
wire shape, request kind, configuration key, outcome code, ledger record or interface revision is
new or changed; [lab-operations.json](lab-operations.json) is unchanged.

**Why.** CLI-EV, CLI-IN and CLI-HELP (§1.306, §1.307, §1.313) fixed what the command line's words
mean and what its help prints, but nothing completed them: a person typed every row's words,
options and instance aliases from the help or from memory.

**Turning it on** (ruling 1): two lines per shell, which a person adds; actinglab and the installer
never edit a profile.

- PowerShell (Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7): `actinglab completion powershell |
  Out-String | Invoke-Expression` turns it on in the session; `Add-Content $PROFILE 'actinglab
  completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'` keeps it on in every new session.
- bash: `source <(actinglab completion bash)` turns it on in the shell; `echo 'source <(actinglab
  completion bash)' >> ~/.bashrc` keeps it on in every new shell.

**What** (`apps/actinglab/src/cli_completion.rs`; `main`, `execute`, `OWN_COMMANDS`,
`cli_help::OWN_WITHOUT_ROW`).

- **The two commands** (rulings 1, 2 and 8). `completion powershell|bash` (`run_completion`, its
  read list `COMPLETION_READS`: no flag, the shell) answers `{shell, script}`; without `--json`
  `main` prints the script as it is (`cli_completion::for_people`, `script_text`). Its sentence:
  "Prints the Tab completion script of PowerShell or bash, which a person loads from the shell's
  profile; the script asks actinglab for each word's candidates." `__complete [--json] [--wait-ms
  <ms>] <index> <:word>...` is the scripts' callback (`callback_line`, `callback_text`,
  `run_callback`); its sentence says it is not for people: "Not for people: the completion
  scripts' callback, which prints the candidates of the typed word at the index, one per line; it
  runs and writes nothing."
- **The scripts** (`cli_completion::POWERSHELL`, `BASH`, product constants; ruling 2 and the work
  order's "Build"). Plain ASCII; they need only the shell and the program. Each registers for
  `actinglab` and `actinglab.exe` (`Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName`; `complete -o
  default -F`), takes the words up to the one being completed (PowerShell: the command's elements
  that begin before the cursor, a string constant by its value, and an empty word when the word
  being completed is empty; bash: `COMP_WORDS` up to `COMP_CWORD`), and calls back the program
  the line names, its first word as typed (`actinglab` on the path, or the path the person typed),
  with the index of the last and every word quoted and in the word form. PowerShell quotes a
  candidate that holds a character outside `[\w./\\:=+%-]` in single quotes.
- **The word form** (`WORD_MARK`): `:` and the word with `%` written `%25`, `"` `%22`, a space
  `%20` and a tab `%09`; the callback reads any `%` and two hex digits as that byte
  (`decoded`). Windows PowerShell 5.1 hands a native program an empty word as nothing and a word
  with a quote broken; a word of the form is never empty and holds no space and no quote, and it
  never reads as one of actinglab's global options, `--help` or `--via` (none begins with `-`), so
  it reaches the callback whole in every shell.
- **The callback** (ruling 2). It reads its line itself: `main` answers a line whose first word is
  `__complete` before anything else reads it (no option parse, no `--help`, no installation
  check, no channel reporter), prints the candidates one per line and exits 0; with `--json` it
  prints the own command's line `{candidates, outcome}`. A line that reaches the dispatch another
  way (the word not first) answers the same candidates as data. A line it cannot read (no index,
  a second one, a flag it does not read, a word without the mark, a wait that is no whole number
  or has no value, a word that is no UTF-8), an index beyond the words or the program's own,
  and words that begin no command give no candidate. Nothing on stderr, ever; a stdout that
  refuses the text is left as it is.
- **What completes** (ruling 3; `candidates`, `names`, `position`, `command_candidates`,
  `row_candidates`, `RowLine`, `flags`). The command words are those `actinglab help` lists: each
  offered row (the authoring rows where §8.3 lists them, as help's list does) by its name, by the
  own command that serves it under other words and by each own command it replaces
  (`cli_help::row_names`), and each own command without a row, but `__complete`. At each position,
  the next words of every name the words so far begin, by prefix; actinglab's global options and
  their values are skipped among the words; `help <words>` completes as the words. After a row's
  own name: the row's options and switches, `--name` with `_` as `-`, one already on the line left
  out unless its parameter repeats; after an option of type `enum:…`, or in a positional's place of
  that type, its words; in a positional's place of another type nothing (the shell's own file
  names); the global options the row's line takes: where the row hands actinglab's global options
  to its command as written (`engine::as_written`) those a person gives, else `--json` and
  `--help` (the CLI module refuses the others by name, §9.3); and `--instance` while the row's
  positional instance is not given. After an own command without a row, or a row's other
  spelling: the global options a person gives, nothing else (ruling 5: `own_flags` stays in the
  test build). The global options a person gives are `help`'s (`cli_help::GLOBAL_OPTION_PHRASES`,
  where the retired `--require-session` is not listed) but `--via` and the three no command reads
  (`--instances`, `--profile`, `--quiet`).
- **An instance** (rulings 3, 4 and 7; `instance_aliases`). Wherever a row's parameter is an
  instance: its positional (where its command line takes one: never on the 20 rows actinglab's own
  command serves under the row's name, whose note says "only --instance", register §1.307),
  `--instance` before or after the row's words, and the instance option of `remedy set` and
  `wake-test`. The aliases of the running Runtime, asked with `Status`, the read that resolves
  `<instance>` today (`core_ops::alias_of` and the reads beside it), on one connection of the Lab
  channel made as actinglab's own commands make theirs (`lab_client_config_via`) with one deadline
  (`RuntimeClientConfig::with_deadline`) that ends the connect, the handshake (`Health`,
  `BindChannel`) and the read. When no Runtime answers by then (none is located, none runs, it
  answers no `Status` in time), the aliases of the selected configuration the offline rows read
  (`lab_ops::packs::selected_config` and `packs::read`, as `packs` reads it, from the install root
  this program runs from); none where neither reads. The Runtime is asked only at an instance's
  place. The host answers `Health`, `BindChannel` and `Status` from memory and appends no ledger
  record for any of them (`HostShared::control_plane_status`, `governance.rs` `bind_channel`), so
  ruling 7's condition holds: no new request, no ledger record.
- **The wait** (ruling 4). `--wait-ms <ms>`, a parameter of the callback, default 500
  (`cli_completion::DEFAULT_WAIT_MS`); the scripts pass none. `0` asks no Runtime. No configuration
  key.
- **Not completed** (ruling 6): files, paths, directories, keys, ids, numbers, durations, JSON and
  free text: the callback answers nothing there, and both scripts leave the word to the shell's
  own file name completion (PowerShell's when a native completer returns nothing; bash's by
  `complete -o default`).

**Settled where the rulings left it open** (the implementer's; for the coordinator to confirm).
(a) The callback's word is `__complete`, and it is left out of the command words a person is
offered, though `help` lists it with its sentence. (b) The words reach the callback in the word
form, not bare: PowerShell 5.1's native argument passing drops an empty word and breaks one with
a quote, and a bare word could read as actinglab's own option. (c) The scripts call back the
program the line names, its first word as typed. (d) The callback's index counts the program's
word as 0, as bash's `COMP_CWORD` does, and its words end at the one being completed. (e) The
candidates are sorted and given once; PowerShell quotes one that needs it, bash inserts each as
it is. (f) After a row's own name a word that is no flag gets its positional's candidates (an
instance's aliases, an enumeration's words) and, where no positional is left and nothing is typed,
the row's flags; a flag gets the flags. (g) The global options after a row are those its line takes
(see above), not all of them. (h) A row's other spellings (`session app launch`, `lab watch`)
complete as own commands, by the coordinator's ruling 5. (i) A group's words followed by a flag
(`lab --`) offer `--help`. (j) The wait's default is 500 milliseconds and `0` skips the Runtime;
the subprocess test passes a longer wait so that a slow runner's handshake still fits. (k) A
line that reaches the dispatch with the word not first answers the candidates as data (the
dispatch arm the inventory counts), its global options already parsed. (l) The `completion`
command and the callback are in LAB-5B5's group (a): the first refuses by its read list, the
second reads every word of its line and answers one it cannot read with no candidate, ignoring
none.

**Censuses** (ruling 8; each moved with the two commands).

- The dispatch: two arms in `execute` after `explain`; `OWN_COMMANDS` 32 → 34.
- The command inventory `ratchet/actinglab_commands.json`: `dispatch_arm_count` 45 → 47,
  `command_count` 100 → 102, `completion` and `__complete` after `explain` in both lists; the
  README's count (both READMEs, the English and the Chinese, two places each) with it.
- LAB-5B5's census (`cli_module::own_flags`, test build only): `REFUSING_COMMANDS` 59 → 61.
- CLI-HELP's table of own commands without a row: `cli_help::OWN_WITHOUT_ROW` 35 → 37, each with
  its sentence; its test's count, `gate_434_cli_help::cli_help_the_list_has_every_offered_row_and_own_command_once`,
  34 → 36 (the two commands have no row either), and the CLI-HELP gate row's text with it. The
  help's list holds both with their sentences.

**What a person sees.** `actinglab pa<Tab>` offers the command words that begin so (`pause`,
`packs`, `pack-schedule`, `package` and `paths` among them); `actinglab pause <Tab>` the running
Runtime's aliases; `actinglab events --view <Tab>`
`changes`, `errors`, `events`, `health`, `lab` and `observation`; `actinglab tap --<Tab>` the flags
`tap`'s line takes, `--instance` among them; `actinglab run start <alias> <Tab>` file names. With
the Runtime stopped, an alias comes from the selected configuration. A Tab never prints an error.

**Interface.** None moves: `ledger` 8, `runtime-client` 7, `actingd-config` 28, `package` 9 and
`runtime-outcomes` 1, as the release's other slices leave them, unchanged by this one; no request,
no outcome code, no configuration key.

**Rollback.** Nothing is persisted. A build before this one answers `completion` and `__complete`
as unknown commands (exit 1, nothing on stdout the scripts read), so a loaded script then offers
no candidate and the shell completes file names; removing the profile's line ends it.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLICOMP-1 | `actinglab completion powershell\|bash` | own command, `{shell, script}`; the script as it is without `--json` | CLI-COMP | actinglab | `since` 0.12.55 |
| CLICOMP-2 | `actinglab __complete [--json] [--wait-ms <ms>] <index> <:word>...` | own command not for people: candidates one per line, `{candidates}` with `--json`; exit 0 always, nothing on stderr | CLI-COMP | actinglab, the two scripts | `since` 0.12.55; the word form `:` with `%25`, `%22`, `%20`, `%09` |
| CLICOMP-3 | `cli_completion::POWERSHELL`, `BASH` | product constants, plain ASCII | CLI-COMP | — | `Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native`; `complete -o default -F` |
| CLICOMP-4 | `--wait-ms`, default 500 | a parameter of the callback (no configuration key) | CLI-COMP | — | `0` asks no Runtime |

Tests (apps gate row "#434 CLI-COMP"; the table this build embeds, neutral aliases, a configuration
in a temporary folder and the runtime client's scripted Runtime):
`gate_434_cli_comp::cli_comp_command_words_by_prefix_at_each_position`,
`cli_comp_a_row_s_flags_and_an_enumeration_s_words`,
`cli_comp_instances_from_the_runtime_else_the_configuration`,
`cli_comp_a_row_whose_instance_is_only_the_flag_offers_the_flag`,
`cli_comp_anything_wrong_gives_no_candidate` and
`cli_comp_the_scripts_are_ascii_and_pass_the_words_marked` (the bin's), and the integration test
`completion_callback::completion_callback_prints_on_stdout_only_and_exits_zero` (the program run as
a process: stdout only, exit 0, with an answering Runtime, a silent one, none, and lines it cannot
read). That the embedded operation table does not read is not reachable in a test. The only
existing test that changes is CLI-HELP's count above; the inventory guard
`command_inventory_matches_checked_in_snapshot`, LAB-2's
`consumer_command_lines_take_the_old_path_unchanged`, LAB-2b's `own_results_never_name_outcome`
and LAB-5B5's `the_census_puts_every_inventory_word_in_one_group` read the moved censuses
unchanged. No golden changes.

### 1.319 Slice NAV-L1 (0.12.55): a phased route run as a layer enters at the stage its entry page starts (Workflow #428; a production run of 11-11 failed as a layer where the offline regression of the same package was green; the coordinator's ruling of 11-11, not Alice's words: one rule for every run of a phased route; coordinator work order `rd-1111/brief-nav-l1.md`, read on main `385bb500`)

[README.md](README.md) ("Entry page sets", the sentence on the stage a phased route enters at)
is the contract. 1.319 is the coordinator's number for this slice, appended after 1.309 on main
`385bb500`; the numbers between belong to other slices. No persisted ledger shape, wire shape,
configuration key, outcome code, vocabulary or package member is new or changed.

**What happened.** A navigation package that other packages name as their prerequisite package
was changed from one stage to two: a first stage that receives finished items (three operations,
from three pages; its target the panel page with a free slot) and a second stage that opens a list
(one operation from the panel page with a free slot, one from the panel page with every slot busy).
Its entry page set holds three panel pages. Run as a prerequisite layer on the panel page with
every slot busy, it failed at once with `contained_task_state_invalid`: the dependent package's
entry preflight recorded `entry_recovery_failed` for it and ended `fail_closed`. That page starts
an operation of the second stage only; the first stage has no operation from it and does not list
it as a target. The package's offline regression on the same scene was green, because the offline
simulation runs a package as an ordinary run, which enters at the stage its matched entry page
starts (Workflow #373 NAV-3b), here the second.

**Cause** (confirmed in the code on main `385bb500`). `run_with_collector`
(`crates/execution-kernel/src/contained_task.rs`) took the run's required entry only when the run
was `ContainedTaskEntry::Ordinary` and no declared operation's run, and called
`RunStateMachine::start_at_phase` only with it. A layer (`run_as_prerequisite`,
`run_entry_recovery`, `run_as_host_layer`, each entered as `ContainedTaskEntry::BoundRecovery`;
the host passes nothing else) therefore always started at the first stage, whatever page it first
observed. On a page from which the first stage has no operation, `RunStateMachine::next_directive`
(`crates/execution-kernel/src/run.rs`) found none (`run_decision_invalid`, "no operation can
continue from page"), and `candidate_directive` (`contained_task/candidates.rs`) turned that, on a
page that is no error page, into the bare `contained_task_state_invalid`. What value that code
should carry is another slice's.

**The rule.** When the first page a run of a phased route observes is one of the package's entry
pages, the run enters at the stage that page starts, whether it is an ordinary run or a layer the
host runs for another package's entry: a prerequisite package, a navigation edge, a shared
interrupt's handler, the configured return-home package (`run_as_prerequisite`), a request's own
entry recovery package (`run_entry_recovery`), a step of a navigation recovery chain
(`run_as_host_layer`). A layer whose first page is no entry page of the package starts at the
first stage, as before. Nothing else of a layer changes: it still accepts any page of the package
as its first page, waits for one as long as before (the page wait, not the entry wait of an
ordinary run), and keeps its limits and codes; the host's own entry recognition before and after
it is unchanged. In the code the stage entry reads the package's entry pages and the stage each
starts (`RequiredEntryPages::phase_of`) for every run but a declared operation's, while the entry
wait and the entry end below keep the required entry of an ordinary run (`run_with_collector`). An
ordinary run, a declared operation's run, a route without stages and a phased route with a single
entry page (which starts the first stage) decide byte for byte as before.

**The entry end (#411 B20).** `end_on_entry_page` is still called only with an ordinary run's
required entry. A layer has no gap there: a package whose stage lists `end_pages` is refused as
every kind of layer before it runs (`scheduling_outcome_incompatibility`, reason
`phase_end_pages`, read by `is_prerequisite_compatible` and `is_entry_recovery_compatible`), so no
stage of a layer has an end page. Nothing is built for it.

**What a package author can rely on after deploy.** A phased package run as a layer enters where
its own run, and its offline simulation, enter: on an entry page of a later stage it starts at that
stage, so a stage need not hold a move from every entry page, and an offline regression of the
package from an entry page shows the operations its layer runs from that page. A layer on a page of
the package outside its entry page set still starts at the first stage, which needs a move from
that page.

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)): no record,
member, code, key, vocabulary or package member.

**Rollback** (below 0.12.55). Nothing is persisted: an earlier build starts every layer at the
first stage again, and a package whose first stage has no move from an entry page of a later stage
fails there as a layer with `contained_task_state_invalid`, as in the incident.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NAVL1-1 | the stage a phased layer enters at (`run_with_collector`, `RequiredEntryPages::phase_of`) | rule (no shape; corrects [README.md](README.md), "Entry page sets") | NAV-L1 | — | `since` 0.12.55; a layer off its entry pages starts at the first stage; a declared operation's run is unchanged |

Tests (exec gate row "#428 NAV-L1", `gate_428_nav_l1`; synthetic packages on the kernel's scripted
runtime; every layer case runs through `run_as_prerequisite`, `run_entry_recovery` and
`run_as_host_layer`; a two-stage route whose entry page set holds a panel page that starts the
first stage and one that starts the second):
`nav_l1_t1_a_layer_enters_at_the_stage_its_first_entry_page_starts` (on the second stage's entry
page the layer runs that stage's one operation and ends on its target, with no step of the first
stage; on the first stage's entry page it runs the first stage, then the second);
`nav_l1_t2_an_ordinary_run_and_a_layer_run_the_same_operations_from_each_entry_page` (from each
entry page the ordinary run and each layer run the same operations of the same stages in the same
order, and end on the same page after as many steps); `nav_l1_t3_a_layer_off_the_entry_pages_starts_at_the_first_stage`
(on a page of the package outside the set the layer starts at the first stage, as before); and
`nav_l1_t4_a_route_without_stages_and_a_single_entry_page_run_as_a_layer_as_before`. No existing
test changed: main had no test that ran a phased route as a layer.

### 1.320 Slice DIAG-SI (0.12.55): `contained_task_state_invalid` says what was invalid (Workflow #428; the production run of 11-11 that §1.319 tells ended with the bare code, its cause found only by reading the package's diff; the coordinator's rulings 1 to 6 of 11-11, not Alice's words: one code, with values; coordinator work order `rd-1111/brief-diag-si.md`, read on main `bb5f850d`)

1.320 is the coordinator's number, appended after §1.319 on main `bb5f850d`; §1.316 and §1.318
belong to slices open at the same time. The code stays `contained_task_state_invalid`, with its
category (error), its ladder class (`none`) and every end: each run that ended with it still ends
with it, at the same step and with the same receipt state. Its outcome gains the value
`state_problem`, a closed vocabulary, and the values that locate it where the place that ends the
run knows them: the page (`page_id`), the operation (`pack_operation_id`), the stage (`phase_id`,
new) and, at the host, the package (`package_id`). Where `candidate_directive` already maps a
refused decision to a more specific code (`contained_task_operation_candidates_exhausted`,
`contained_task_error_page_reached`), nothing changes.

**The kinds** (vocabulary `state_problem`, `crates/actingcommand-contract/src/outcome/vocabulary.rs`,
`StateProblem`):

| Token | What is wrong | Whose |
|---|---|---|
| `no_move_from_page` | no operation of the stage the run is in (of the package, for a route without stages) leaves the page the run observes, and the page is no target and no error page | the package author's |
| `transition_refused` | the run's state machine refused a transition the kernel asked of it in its state | the Runtime's |
| `runtime_invariant` | a value that cannot be absent was absent, an arithmetic that cannot fail failed, or an answer that is never given was given | the Runtime's |
| `held_state_unusable` | a state the run's layers or a package registry hold is not one the host can use | the Runtime's |

The state machine's error (`crates/execution-kernel/src/run.rs`, `RunDecisionError`) now carries
its kind, `RunDecisionKind` (`Invalid`, `NoOperationFromPage`, `TransitionRefused`,
`CandidatesExhausted`), beside the code it had (`run_decision_invalid`, `run_transition_invalid`,
`contained_task_operation_candidates_exhausted`); the kernel names the token by that kind
(`decision_problem`, `machine_refusal` in `contained_task.rs`), never by the message.

by kind (22, 23); `held_state_unusable` 9 places.

**Where the values are read** (ruling 4). The run's terminal and receipt carry them as every
kernel failure's values (`host/contained_task.rs`, the terminal's `has_values` branch, unchanged).
A layer's failure: a prerequisite layer's gate (`host/prerequisite.rs`, `close_open`,
`record_closed`, `fail_gate`) records the outcome of a `contained_task_state_invalid` with its
values (`layer_failure_outcome`) in each `EntryRecoveryFailed` and in its fail-closed
`EntryTargetDisposition`, and carries the code with its values out (`layer_task_failure`); every
other code stays its code alone there, as before. The home entry's recovery layer
(`host/contained_task.rs`, the task-failure arm after `run_entry_recovery` and a configured
return-home package's run; the one edit there) does the same. Navigation layers, recovery chain
steps and interrupt handlers already record and carry the layer's whole outcome
(`run_navigation_layer`, `run_interrupt_layer`, `close_navigation`). The codes-only projection keeps
`state_problem` (a `vocab` value); the ids are `id` values, which codes mode withholds
([runtime-outcomes.md](runtime-outcomes.md), "Codes mode"). The offline replay adapter's error
(`OfflineSimulationError::outcome`) carries the token; `actinglab replay` prints its code as before.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSI-1 | `state_problem` (`vocab:state_problem`), `phase_id` (`id`) | outcome keys, `runtime-outcomes` 1 | DIAG-SI | the kernel, the host | `since` 0.12.55 |
| DSI-2 | `state_problem`: `no_move_from_page`, `transition_refused`, `runtime_invariant`, `held_state_unusable` | vocabulary, `runtime-outcomes` 1 | DIAG-SI | the kernel, the host | closed; kept in codes mode |
| DSI-3 | `contained_task_state_invalid`: optional values `state_problem`, `page_id`, `pack_operation_id`, `phase_id`, `package_id`; description, causes and handling written | catalog entry (contract fragment) | DIAG-SI | — | category, ladder class and every end unchanged |
| DSI-4 | `RunDecisionKind`, `RunDecisionError::kind` | kernel API | DIAG-SI | — | the code of each refusal unchanged |

**Settled here** (the rulings left them open; each the slice's, the coordinator may change them):

- The operation's key is the existing `pack_operation_id` (the catalog has no `operation_id`;
  `operation` is a location key). The stage's key is `phase_id`, the stage's declared id (the key
  `stage` is a location and the guard G3 refuses it, and a phased route's stages are its
  `phases`, as the Lab's declared operation names its `phase_id`).
- `state_problem` is optional in the code's values: a relayed spelling carries no value, and a
  build before 0.12.55 wrote none.
- A layer's failure keeps its values only for this code; widening that to every code would change
  other codes' records, which no ruling asked.
- The two places of the offline replay adapter (43, 44) end the replay as before
  (`OfflineReplayError::Invariant`), now with an outcome that names the token.

**What an operator and a package author see after deploy.** A run that ended
`contained_task_state_invalid` still ends so, but its terminal, its receipt and, for a layer, its
`task.entry_preflight` records say what was invalid. The incident's kind, a phased prerequisite
package on a page outside its entry page set that its first stage has no operation from, reads in
full detail:

```json
{"code":"contained_task_state_invalid","category":"error",
 "values":{"operation":"run_contained_task","state_problem":"no_move_from_page",
           "page_id":"neutral/busy","phase_id":"first"}}
```

and in codes mode `{"code":"contained_task_state_invalid","category":"error","values":
{"operation":"run_contained_task","state_problem":"no_move_from_page"}}`. The package author
gives the stage `phase_id` an operation from the page `page_id`, makes that page a target of the
stage, or, for a layer, lists the page in the entry page set with the stage it starts. The three
other tokens are the Runtime's own: report the run's records with the outcome.

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)):
`runtime-outcomes` stays 1, with two keys and one vocabulary added within it and the code's
values widened; `ledger` does not move (the records gain values in an outcome they already
carry, a map their reader takes as written); `package`, `runtime-client` and `actingd-config`
are untouched.

**Rollback** (below 0.12.55). Nothing is persisted that a build before needs undone: it emits the
bare code again, and it reads the records this build wrote, whose new values it only spells.

Tests (exec gate row "#428 DIAG-SI", `crates/execution-kernel/src/contained_task/gate_428_diag_si.rs`,
synthetic packages on the kernel's scripted runtime; host gate row "#428 DIAG-SI",
`crates/runtime-host/src/tests/gate_428_diag_si.rs`, a synthetic game root on the fake device):
`diag_si_t1_a_stage_without_a_move_from_the_observed_page_names_the_page_and_the_stage` (a phased
route run as each kind of layer on a page outside its entry page set and outside the first
stage's moves ends before any step with the token, the page and the stage; an ordinary run of a
route without stages, brought by its one operation to a page no operation leaves, ends after that
step with the token and the page; category error, ladder class `none`);
`diag_si_t2_the_state_machine_names_the_kind_of_a_refused_decision` (no operation from the page, a
refused transition and a page matching two targets, each with its code of before and its token);
`diag_si_t3_a_pacing_factor_below_the_minimum_is_a_runtime_invariant`;
`diag_si_t4_the_codes_only_projection_keeps_the_token`; and the host's
`diag_si_a_prerequisite_layer_without_a_move_names_the_page_and_the_stage_in_its_records` (the
incident's shape through the prerequisite gate: receipt failed with the code, no input, and
`EntryRecoveryFailed`, the fail-closed `EntryTargetDisposition` and the terminal with the token,
the page and the stage). An ordinary phased run cannot be brought to such a page by its own
operations: admission's static walk refuses that route (`task_phases_unreachable`), so T1's
ordinary run is a route without stages. No test reaches `transition_refused` or
`held_state_unusable` through a run: the kernel alone drives its machine (T2 pins the kind and the
token), and each host place is guarded by the state it reads (`navigates()` before
`navigate_to_entry`, an admission just before the lookup, the bundle check of a registry). No
existing test changed: none compared an outcome of this code (the kernel's and the host's
`gate_411_a45` name it only as absent, `gate_419_iso1` as an instance fault's code), and none
pinned a run's end with it, so the end's step, category and receipt state are asserted beside the
new values.

### 1.321 Slice CODES-IX (0.12.56): a generated index of the outcome code catalog, kept current by CI (Workflow #439; Alice, 11-12: 「错误码可以分批做，并且可以搞个索引」; the coordinator's eight rulings of 11-12, not Alice's words; coordinator work order `rd-1111/brief-codes-index.md`, read on main `2e3062ec`)

[runtime-outcomes.md](runtime-outcomes.md), "The index", is the contract. 1.321 is the
coordinator's number for this slice, appended after 1.319 on main `2e3062ec`; the numbers between
belong to other slices. No persisted shape, wire shape, request kind, configuration key, outcome
code, ledger record, vocabulary or interface revision is new or changed, and no catalog entry is
edited: the index only reads the catalog.

**Why.** The catalog is 29 owner fragments under `contracts/outcome-codes/` with 3912 codes: a
person could not see at a glance what exists, which codes have their text written and which still
hold placeholders. The index answers that for people who read the repository; `actingledger
codes`, `actingctl codes` and `ac_outcome_code` stay the lookups of one code.

**What the index holds** (`contracts/outcome-codes/index/`; rulings 2 to 4).

- `README.md`: the codes by status (active, retired); the active codes by category; the active
  codes by text (`common_causes` and `handling` both written, one of the two written, neither; a
  text is written unless it is missing, empty or `TBD`, as G10 reads it) and by review
  (`settled`, `pending`); one table of the owners (the owner with a link to its file, codes,
  active, text written, settled; text written and settled count active codes) with a total row;
  and one paragraph saying what each column means and how to regenerate.
- `<owner>.md`, one per owner fragment: one table sorted by code, with the code, category, ladder
  class, `since`, status (`active`, or `retired, replaced by <code>` where the entry names one),
  review, text (`written` when both texts are written, else `TBD`) and the description's first
  sentence.
- The first sentence: white space, newlines included, reads as one space; the sentence ends at the
  first `.`, `!` or `?` followed by a space or the end; longer than 160 characters it is cut at
  the last space within the 160 (at 160 when it has none) and ends in `…`. In a cell every `|` is
  written `\|`, and a `<` outside a code span `\<`.
- Nothing that changes without the catalog: no time, no commit id. Owners and codes sorted by
  name, LF line ends, UTF-8 without BOM; the same text on Windows and Linux.

**How it is generated** (rulings 1 and 6). `ci/outcome_codes_index.py [--check] [<workspace
root>]`, standard library only. It reads the catalog with `ci/outcome_release.py`'s new
`owner_fragments(root)`: the release script's loop over the header's `fragments` (an owner without
a file skipped, a name registered twice failing), moved into a function that `catalog_signatures`
now calls too, so both scripts read the same entries; on main `2e3062ec`'s catalog the release
script's signatures and rendered release file are the same as before the move. The index script
loads `outcome_release.py` by its path, so it runs under `py -3 -I -B` as well as `python3`. An
entry the index cannot count (a status, review or category outside the guard's sets, a text
member that is no text) fails the run; other inconsistencies it sees (a fragment's or an entry's
`owner` other than the fragment's, a `replaced_by` that names no code, a settled code without its
text) are printed as `NOTE outcome_codes_index:` lines on stderr. On `2e3062ec` it printed none.
Without `--check` it writes the index and deletes nothing: a file under `index/` that it does not
generate fails the run, naming the file.

**How CI keeps it** (ruling 5). The `gate` job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (check name `rust`,
a required check), where `ci/gate_check.py check` and its logic tests run, checks out
`contracts/outcome-codes/` too and runs `python3 ci/outcome_codes_index.py --check`, then `python3
ci/test_outcome_codes_index.py -v`, after a red job too (`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`). A stale index
exits 1 naming the first file in name order that is missing, differs, or is no file of the index:

    ERROR outcome_codes_index: contracts/outcome-codes/index/<file> differs from what the script generates from the catalog (and N other files): the committed index is stale; run py -3 -I -B ci/outcome_codes_index.py from the workspace root and commit contracts/outcome-codes/index/

A pull request that changes a fragment therefore regenerates the index. Two such pull requests
meet in `README.md`: `main` merges only a branch that is up to date with it, so the later one
merges `main`, regenerates and commits the index.

**The counts at the time of writing** (main `2e3062ec`): 3912 codes, 3894 active and 18 retired;
the active ones by category: success 126, info 205, warning 146, error 3403, fatal 14; of the
active codes 624 have both texts written, 9 one of the two, 3261 neither; 171 are settled and 3723
pending. 29 of the header's 39 owners have a fragment file; the catalog's 1750 locations are not
indexed. 30 files, 687,208 bytes; the largest are `runtime-host.md` (192,838 bytes, 1145 codes)
and `contract.md` (164,200 bytes, 915 codes), every file under the 400 KB the work order allows.

**Settled where the rulings left it open** (the implementer's; for the coordinator to confirm).
(a) The index lists codes only; the README's paragraph counts the locations it leaves out. (b) The
text and review counts, per owner too, count active codes, as the coordinator's count of 11-11
did; an owner's *codes* counts active and retired ones, and an *active* column stands beside it.
(c) The README splits the active codes whose text is not written into one of the two written and
neither. (d) The cut falls at a space and splits no word: a word cut in two can read as another
word, and the neutral-word guards (C2, NEUT-1, NEUT-2) read every word under `contracts/`. (e) A
`<` outside a code span is escaped as well, so that a renderer shows `<root>` instead of dropping
it as a tag. (f) The tests are `ci/test_outcome_codes_index.py`, in the place and style of
`ci/test_gate_check.py`, run by the same job.

**Interface.** None moves: `ledger` 8, `runtime-client` 7, `actingd-config` 28, `package` 9 and
`runtime-outcomes` 1, as main `2e3062ec` declares them; no request, no outcome code, no
configuration key.

**At deploy.** Nothing changes at run time: no program reads the index.

**Rollback.** Delete `contracts/outcome-codes/index/` and, in the `gate` job of `ci.yml`, the two
steps and the sparse checkout's line `contracts/outcome-codes/` (`ci/outcome_codes_index.py` and
its test may go with them). `owner_fragments` may stay: the release script reads the catalog as
before.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CODESIX-1 | `contracts/outcome-codes/index/README.md` and `<owner>.md` | generated Markdown, no interface | CODES-IX | `ci/outcome_codes_index.py` | `since` 0.12.56; `--check` in the `rust` check |
| CODESIX-2 | `ci/outcome_release.py` `owner_fragments(root)` | the shared reader of the header and the fragments | CODES-IX | — | `catalog_signatures` reads with it; release output unchanged |

Tests (`ci/test_outcome_codes_index.py`, run by the `gate` job; a synthetic catalog of three
neutral owners, one without a fragment file, in a temporary folder):
`test_the_summary_counts_by_status_category_text_review_and_owner`,
`test_owners_and_codes_are_sorted_and_a_retired_code_names_its_replacement`,
`test_a_pipe_a_newline_and_a_tag_are_safe_in_a_table_cell`,
`test_a_description_is_cut_at_a_space_within_160_characters` and
`test_check_fails_on_a_stale_index_and_passes_on_a_fresh_one` (missing, fresh, one file changed by
hand, a file the index does not hold; no BOM, no CR). No Rust test, gate map entry or golden
changes.

1.322 is the coordinator's number, appended after §1.320 on main `e2b5590f`. Main `6e4119c7`,

`task_held` and its `codes`), the two key rows and the paragraph "Held records" of

**What happened** (production, 11-11, in neutral words). The head of a chain of tasks on one
instance was held by the no-progress guard for about 50 minutes, while the tasks that could change
the reading it waited for waited on the head. Nothing failed. The not-run explanation said why
each task did not run (`policy_no_progress` on the head, `trigger_unknown` on the followers), in
memory and at info only: the ledger held no warning and no error for that instance in those 50
minutes, the diagnosis listed nothing, and no wake rule could match. A person found it by looking.
From 0.12.55 that deadlock no longer forms (SS-4b, §1.310); the record is for the next one,
whatever its cause.

**The census** (ruling 2; every `why` code a candidate row can carry on `e2b5590f`, from the
evaluator `crates/policy/src/evaluator.rs` and its modules, the host's eligibility closure in

which the evaluator sets before the code: `false` with a false trigger or a true stop

unknown trigger or stop, `true` once the stop is false (`:1990-1996`), kept by every later

**Where the contract differs from the rulings or completes them.**

- *Ruling 1.* The record has one side effect, the one every planning signal has: it invalidates
  each active fact whose `invalidate_on` lists `policy.planning_signal_observed`, on every instance
  (`crates/runtime-host/src/fact_store.rs:401-427` at replay and `:1245-1271` live, by event type;
  `:120-138` a record without an instance link matches every instance). Having none takes a `ledger`
  revision either way: another record type (`EventType` has no catch-all), or an exception in both
  derivations that a reader of 0.12.55 does not make, which then derives an invalidation the newer
  build never wrote, so the first persisted invalidation of the same fact snapshot fails its replay
  (`fact_invalidation_source_mismatch`, `:393-398`). No fact the Runtime or a run writes lists the
  type (`invalidate_on` is empty in every reading of `host/contained_task.rs:351`, `:475`, `:528`
  and every host fact of `host/facts.rs:302`, `:890`, `:964`); only a client's `PublishFacts` can.
  The contract keeps the effect and says so (settled 4). No other path acts on it: the old agent
  dispatcher takes only `timeline_reached` and `drift_predicted` (`host/planning.rs:131-139`), the
  remedy state only its prefix (`:114-121`), the detection quota only the detection kinds
  (`runtime-state/src/store/planning.rs:188-200`).
- *Ruling 2.* A fourth class, *not due* (`trigger_false`, `feedback_stop_true`): ruling 3 keeps a
  false trigger out ("not due"), and neither fits "said no" or "its own time". Two codes are
  decided by a value (`benefit_gap`, `pool_line_hold`). The held set is closed: a code outside it,
  one a later slice adds included, is never held until the census names it. The fact refresh read
  and a pair with a dispatch in flight are never held (the clock-slot rule,
  `policy_host/clock_slot.rs:530`, `:587`, `:621`); the latter keeps a run of a pair due during its
  own run (a cooldown shorter than the run) from being reported for that run.
- *Ruling 3.* One code is the better form: one record, one wake rule, one catalog entry for one
  state; two codes would double what reads them for one meaning (#420 S4: one domain code with
  values). The value `held_state` is the row's eligibility,
  not its code: `true` is `due`, `unknown` is `undecidable` (the fact refresh codes come with
  either).
- *Ruling 5.* No one rhythm of the pair exists for every trigger, so the threshold is the floor
  alone. The task's `cooldown_ms` is a lower bound between two dispatches, not a rhythm, and a held
  pair is past it (the cooldown comes first, `evaluator.rs:2051-2058`). A clock's period exists only
  for a trigger with a counted clock; a `fact`, `resource_projection`, `fact_time_reached`,
  `dependency_completed` or `outcome` trigger has none, an `any` of a clock and a fact has two
  causes, and 11-11's head was due by a fact. The expected duration E exists for every pair but
  says how long a run takes, not how often it should run; a wait behind another run would be
  measured by the other run's E. The default floor is the coordinator's 30 minutes: the guard holds
  until a reading changes, the fact refresh's interval (5 minutes) and failure backoff (10 minutes)
  are shorter, so a transient wait clears first, and 11-11's hold would have been reported about
  20 minutes before a person found it. The range, one minute to one day, is the idle gap keys'.
  The coordinator's proposal of 11-12, a default by the task's own rhythm, was dropped for these
  reasons, and the coordinator agreed to the floor alone on 11-12.
- *Ruling 6.* The reason's values go in a `caused_by` link, whole, not beside the record's own:
  they collide (`task_id` names another task in `pool_line_held`, `gate_code` is a fact refresh
  wait's own gate, `instance_id` is beside `alias`). The link adds nothing that needs another
  observation. `gate_code` is reused with its description widened. A `trigger_unknown` reason has no
  values (`evaluator.rs:1878-1881`), so an undecidable hold names no fact key: a stated limit of
  HELD-1 (settled 8).
- *Ruling 7.* "Left the table" for a trigger turned false or a package closed is a `why` change:
  the row stays with `trigger_false` or `pack_schedule_closed`. "Dispatched" is `selected`: the
  explanation sees the selection, the dispatch records the admission. The restart end is written by
  the start, before it records its settlement anchor, not at the first evaluation (settled 1), and
  carries no `held_for_ms`: the last evaluation of the run before is not known to the start.
- *Ruling 4 and 8.* With the table's clock, a pair that changes held codes faster than the
  threshold is never reported. The three waits for one fact's refresh change codes that fast, so
  from HELD-1 they share one clock per `fact_key` and are reported (settled 2).
- *Ruling 9.* `ac_diagnose` with an instance shows no held record today: its errors page filters by
  the instance link (`crates/lab-ops/src/diagnose.rs:439-446`), which a planning signal does not
  have (`host/planning.rs:90`, the system links).
- *Ruling 10.* The second `next_reads` entry names no instance, for the same reason.

30 minutes leaves one warning in the ledger, in the errors view (`ac_events`, an `ac_diagnose`
without an instance) and, with HELD-1's readers, in `actingd suspended` and the instance's
`ac_diagnose`; its end leaves one info record; a start ends the holds the runs before it left open.
No decision, intent, eligibility age, guard, pause, ladder or streak changes, and nothing reaches
a person's channel until HELD-2 and a rule exist. The configuration manifest lists the two keys
(and each instance's two). A console edits them only once its `actingd-config` range reaches the
revision.

**Rollback** (below 0.12.56). A build before reads both records and ignores them (the walk). Its
configuration must not name `scheduling.task_held` (refused as an unknown member): remove the
member before going back. A hold open when the build changes keeps no end record: the older build's
start does not end it, and records its own anchor, after which a newer start reads; a reader takes
the next start record after a held record without an end as its end. After HELD-2, an open wake row
of kind `task_held` fails loudly on the older build (`kind_unknown`).

### 1.323 Slice MAPP-C (contracts only): several applications on one device, one queue, one application in front (Workflow #437; Alice's direction of 2026-11-11 in the body of board #437, of which one sentence is quoted below; the coordinator's fourteen rulings of 11-11 and its answers of 11-12 to the fourteen questions this section held, `rd-1112/answers-437-mapp-c.md`, not Alice's words; the read-only survey `rd-1111/agent-report-multiapp-survey.txt`, made on `bb5f850d`, every line used here read again on main `e2b5590f`, and no Rust file changed from there to main `6e4119c7`; coordinator work orders `rd-1111/brief-mapp-contract.md` and `rd-1112/brief-437-mapp-c-fix.md`)

The contract is in these files:

- [device-group.md](device-group.md) (new): the whole contract;
- [application-lifecycle.md](application-lifecycle.md): the paragraph after the opening, and the
  startup package hook;
- [runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md): the new "Device groups";
- [scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md): "Per-Instance Lanes" and "Why A Candidate Does Not
  Run";
- [device-binding.md](device-binding.md): "Identity, label and fingerprint";
- [emulator-control.md](emulator-control.md): "Operation and origin gate";
- [player-hold.md](player-hold.md): the opening;
- [actingd-check-config.md](actingd-check-config.md): "Discovery-bound instances";
- [component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md): the new "Planned: Workflow #437 MAPP";
- [README.md](README.md): the index line.

The number 1.323 is the coordinator's. Sections stand in merge order: §1.321, §1.324 and §1.322
were merged first (main `fbb457a4`, merged into this slice), so this section follows them.

**MAPP-C itself.** Contracts only: no code, no test, no schema file, no catalog entry, no gate row,
no CI file, no configuration key in the defaults, and no live revision raised. Every rule is
marked "(MAPP, not built yet)", and device-group.md is so as a whole. Every code, value key,
vocabulary word and the one configuration key it names is proposed. The text names no game and no
store. Alice's one sentence it quotes is 「切换到另一个应用时，原先的应用直接杀掉就行」.

**Why.** Today one device runs one application:

- one entry has one `application_id`, one `nemu_app_index`, one policy identity and one startup
  package;
- the scheduler has one queue, one worker and one lease per instance;
- the evaluator selects one task per instance per round.

Alice wants one device to hold several applications that the scheduler serves in turn (her rules
in neutral words open [device-group.md](device-group.md)). The model is the survey's model B:
today's instance entry stays one application on one device, and several entries declare one
device as a device group.

**What the code slices build**

| Kind | What | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| configuration | the entry member `device_group`, check-config's report member, the manifest row `instance.<id>.device_group` | MAPP-1 | `actingd-config` 29 (planned row) |
| check | the group's rules at assembly, the instruction rule by `section_check`, and undeclared sharing at assembly and after discovery | MAPP-1 | `device_group_config_invalid` and the vocabulary `device_group_problem` (proposed) |
| check | every group of several refused at load after the group's rules, until the slice "order within one device" removes it | MAPP-1 | `device_group_config_invalid`, `several_members_unsupported` (proposed) |

**Device-level actions** (ruling 8; the full table with files and lines is
