**Where the contract differs from the rulings or completes them**

1. *Ruling 3, completed.* "The queue" is three things keyed by instance: the scheduler state
   (lib.rs:892-908), the worker (host_claims.rs:107-143) and the in-flight registration
   (policy_dispatch.rs:101-134). Two more places read the instance as the device: the admission
   guard (lease.rs:3230-3240) and the owner journal's active instances (lease.rs:3242-3247,
   lib.rs:2585-2593). All of them are keyed by the device key, the token keeps the member's id, and
   a pause's wait reads the member's lease, not the device's (policy_dispatch.rs:3164-3170).
2. *Ruling 4, completed.* The group cannot go into the evaluator's input: `InstanceSnapshot` denies
   unknown members (evaluator.rs:181-191), and the input feeds the snapshot and decision
   identities. It is a separate in-memory argument, as `InstanceHolds` is.
3. *Ruling 4, completed.* "Today's scores as they are" includes the business tier's turns across
   instances. These put the members of one device in alternation, so slice 1 may switch at every
   dispatch there.
4. *Ruling 6, completed.* "Starts the member's application by its package" is the startup
   package's own first step (`application` `restart`, provider.rs:902-929): there is no separate
   launch.
   - When the front is unknown or no member's, every other member's application is stopped.
   - The switch also runs before every other start of a member's application.
   - The startup run's end hands the key back to the run.
5. *Ruling 6, completed (the member's ladder).* A failed switch starts no ladder. The run is
   refused before its request lifecycle, so it has no `task.failed` terminal at the task stage, and
   startup runs never start one.
6. *Ruling 8, completed.*
   - Idle `close_app` is device-level too: its wake runs a member's startup package ahead of the
     device's pick.
   - The defaults make every emulator climb a ladder with `emulator_restart` and take `idle.action`
     `close_app`, so every member of a group of several must name `idle.action` `none` and a profile
     without that rung (the neutrally named profile MAPP-1 adds, or the defaults file's `handset`).
   - Operator emulator control and keyless observation are added to the list.
7. *Ruling 9, decided.* A fence of one member holds the whole group, because slice 1 cannot tell a
   device's cause of a fence from an application's.
8. *Rulings 2 and 11.* Two entries on one device can be proven at assembly only when they name it
   by the same key and value. An index beside a name, or `HOST:PORT` beside a discovery binding, is
   seen only after the start's discovery, which check-config never runs. So the check runs in two
   places. Handsets are covered already by the binding file. The refusal of undeclared sharing is
   the one thing a configuration without groups can see, so ruling 2 holds with that one
   exception.
9. *The coordinator's claim of 11-11, corrected.* The claim that putting the switch time into the
   expected duration makes the scheduler finish one application's due work before switching does
   not hold, because the order across members is decided by the business tier's turns across
   instances before any duration is compared (scheduling/README.md, "Turns across instances"),
   which is why the slice "order within one device" exists.
10. *Rulings 1 and 7.* Handsets cannot be members in slice 1 (the binding file binds one serial to
    one alias). So a clone "perhaps on a phone" needs the binding made group-aware as well as the
    Android user.
11. *Ruling 10, completed.* A second hold on another member of the same group is refused, and a
    hold's release runs the member's startup package through the switch.
12. *Ruling 13, confirmed.* Neither `ledger` nor `runtime-client` moves (the walk below).

**Settled by the coordinator on 11-12** (its answers to the fourteen questions this section held,
`rd-1112/answers-437-mapp-c.md`). Questions 4, 5 and 6 were meant for Alice; the coordinator
answered them and informs her, so no line below is her words. Each stands as settled text in the
section of [device-group.md](device-group.md) it names.

1. The form is the entry member `device_group`, not a top-level list ("The configuration form").
2. The device key is the smallest instance id of the group's members, in memory only ("Derived, never stored").
3. A member's conflicting device-level setting is refused, never overridden; MAPP-1 adds a neutrally named profile without `emulator_restart` to the defaults file's `recovery_ladder.profiles` ("The configuration form").
4. On a device with several members, slice 1 does not start, stop or restart the emulator, does not close the application or the emulator when idle and does not restart the emulator after a major failure; the slice "device-level actions by device" lifts this, before the first real use ("Device-level actions", "Later slices").
5. While a person uses one member by hand, the whole device waits ("Pause and hold").
6. The first two slices may switch application after every task; the first release that accepts a group of several also carries the slice "order within one device", and until then such a group is refused at load with `several_members_unsupported` ("One pick per device per round", "The configuration form", "Later slices").
7. A failed switch starts no ladder, and the member then does not compete for the device for `scheduling.device_group.switch_failure_cooldown_ms`, default five minutes ("The switch before a run").
8. With the front unknown or no member's, every other member's application is stopped ("The switch before a run").
9. A fence of one member holds the whole group until it is lifted ("A failure stays where it belongs").
10. Before MAPP-1 ships, the production configuration files are read, read only, for two entries on one device ("The configuration form", "Undeclared sharing").
11. In slice 1 a keyless observation of a member is refused while another member holds the device ("Device-level actions", row 15).
12. A refused device-level action has the one new code `device_group_action_refused` with `operation` ("Device-level actions", row 5).
13. A discovered index a group shares names the group's first member by alias as its `bound_alias`, in the discovery answer and the startup record ("Device-level actions", row 6).
14. The release that first accepts a group of several carries MAPP-1b, MAPP-2 and the order within one device together; MAPP-1a shipped in 0.12.56 with every group of several refused at load ("Later slices", "Release"; corrected by the coordinator on 11-12, §1.330: this answer said that MAPP-1 and MAPP-2 ship in one release).

**Release** (settled points 6 and 14):

- MAPP-1a shipped in Runtime 0.12.56 with every group of several refused at load (corrected by
  the coordinator on 11-12, §1.330: this point said that MAPP-1 and MAPP-2 ship in one release).
- The release that first accepts a device group of more than one member carries the host's rows
  (MAPP-1b), the switch before a run (MAPP-2) and the slice "order within one device"
  (device-group.md, "Later slices") together. Until then every build refuses such a group at load
  (`device_group_config_invalid`, `several_members_unsupported`), and no release ships the switch
  after every task. MAPP-2's key comes with MAPP-2 and takes the next free revision of
  `actingd-config`.
- The slice "device-level actions by device" comes before the first real use of a group of
  several.

Until the order slice the load refuses a group of several. So the tests of a running group of
several hand the member → device map to the scheduler, the host and the evaluator as the assembly
builds it, and the tests of the instruction rule build the configuration in effect directly; the
load itself is tested with a group of one, with each refusal, and with the refusal of a group of
several that passes every rule.

MAPP-1's tests:

- a group of one writes what today writes: the same file with and without a lone `device_group`
  gives the same decisions, outcomes, records, owner journal ids and thread names, compared within
  one host;
- the entry still denies unknown members and the Runtime declares `actingd-config` [5, 29], which is
  what makes an older revision's build refuse the new form;
- two members never hold the device at once (lease, queue, admission);
- one pick per device, the other member waits with `device_group_waiting` `selected` with `alias`
  and `task_id`, as a candidate behind its own instance's winner waits;
- a due task of one member waits (`held`) while the other member's package runs, and runs after it;
- each group rule refused with its `device_group_problem`;
- a group of several that breaks no rule refused at load with `several_members_unsupported`, and a
  group of one accepted;
- undeclared sharing refused, at assembly and after a fake discovery;
- the instruction refused by `section_check`;
- a fence or a hold of one member holds the others, and its end frees them;
- a second hold refused;
- a pause of one member leaves the others scheduled and does not wait for their runs;
- emulator control and keyless observation refused;
- a member's session closed at its lease end;
- a restart rebuilds the member → device map from the configuration in effect, and the takeover
  cooldown covers the group.

MAPP-2's tests:

- a switch kills the first application, starts the second and reaches its home before the task,
  under one causation id, the key never granted to another claim in between;
- no switch when the member is in front;
- the front unknown stops every other member;
- a failed switch fails that task only: each step, the run settled failed with
  `application_switch_failed`, its step and cause, the other member's pairs untouched, no ladder;
- a failed switch starts the member's switch cooldown, on a fake clock: every other candidate of
  the member, an owed rerun included, deferred with `dispatch_instance_cooldown` (`failure_code`
  `application_switch_failed`, `next_eligible_unix_ms` and the wake at its end) for the key's value,
  the other member dispatched meanwhile, no ladder, and the member a candidate again at its end;
  the key's default `300000` and its range `1..=3600000`;
- a direct run (the Lab) goes through the same switch;
- `ApplicationLifecycle` `launch`, the application restart rung and a hold's release stop the
  member in front first;
- at most one member's application is alive after any sequence of these on the fake device.

**Later slices**, named and not written here (device-group.md, "Later slices"): the order within
one device (with the switch's time as a cost), the normalized weight (board #437 comment
6799803829), the device-level actions by device, the console and the command line, and clones.

**What changes live.** This slice changes no build. MAPP-1a shipped in 0.12.56 with every group
of several refused at load; MAPP-1b, MAPP-2 and the order within one device reach a root together
in the release that first accepts a group of several (corrected by the coordinator on 11-12,
§1.330). As they ship:

- a root without `device_group` runs as today, except that a file naming one device from two entries
  is refused at its start (settled point 10) and, from MAPP-2 on, the `scheduling` section has one
  more key, the switch cooldown's, with its default, in the next free revision of
  `actingd-config`;
- the five production roots stay groups of one, and no data is migrated;
- a file with a group of several is refused at its start until the release that carries the order
  within one device. From that release on, a person who puts two applications on one device
  writes, for each member, `device_group`, the same device key, its own `application_id`, a
  `startup_package`, `idle.action` `none`, a ladder profile without `emulator_restart`, and no
  `start_emulator`.

**Rollback.** Going back to a build before MAPP-1 needs a file of revision 28 or lower: every
`device_group` removed, and at most one entry kept per device, because an older build accepts two
entries on one device and drives it from two workers. The ledger written by MAPP builds is
readable by the older build (no ledger revision moved), and the owner journal's ids are instance
ids it reads as before. Going back from the release that accepts a group of several to one that
carries MAPP-1a alone means refusing every group of several again (settled point 14, as corrected
on 11-12).

**Not verified** (the repository does not say; device-group.md, "Not verified"):

- what `am force-stop` does to a package that is not running;
- whether two members' sessions can be open on one emulator;
- whether an emulator's ADB port survives its restart;
- how a clone is addressed;
- whether the report's readers deny unknown members.

### 1.326 Slice REM-1 (0.12.56): in composer mode the remedy table is built from the composed manifest at start, and every build says what it found (Workflow #442; a production run of 11-12 on v0.12.52 whose outcome key declares a remedy opened no round and recorded nothing; the read-only investigation of that run at `b44eea2d`; coordinator work order `rd-1112/brief-442-rem-1.md`, read on main `6e4119c7`)

[remedies.md](remedies.md) section 7.1 is the contract. 1.326 is the coordinator's number,
written after §1.324 on main `6e4119c7`. Sections stand in merge order: §1.322 and §1.323 were
merged first (main `c7dc14ec`, merged into this slice), so this section follows them; §1.325 was
not used. No persisted ledger shape, wire shape, request kind, configuration key, outcome code,
vocabulary or interface revision is new or changed. On main `6e4119c7` the start order,
`table_due` and `build_table` are the ones the investigation read at `b44eea2d`; since then only
Workflow #429 R-8 added the task packages to the table, which the pack schedule view reads.

**What happened.** On production (v0.12.52, composer mode) a scheduled run ended on an outcome key
whose package mapping declares a remedy. No remedy round opened, and nothing said so: no reason
code, no planning signal, no ledger record, no log line.

**Cause** (confirmed in the code).

1. The start builds the remedy table (`recover_remedy_state`) from the host's procedure manifest;
   in composer mode the configuration gives none.
2. The composed manifest was put in place only by the scheduler workbench's first check, in the
   first policy cycle, after that recovery: the table was built empty, carrying the active
   catalog's hash.
3. `table_due` rebuilt it only without a table, for another catalog, or at its interval while a
   round, a stop or a client wait is open; an unchanged composition is not activated again, so the
   empty table lasted until the next activation, and every restart built an empty one again.
4. With no entry for the task the settlement does not read the terminal's key, and the next
   cycle's remedy plan is empty; an empty table wrote no line.
5. `actingd check-config` builds its table from the composed manifest, so the offline check passed
   while the running table was empty.

**What changed.**

- **The start** (`host.rs`, before `recover_remedy_state`): in composer mode the workbench adopts
  the active generation the policy host loaded (`adopt_standard_pack_generation_on_start`; the
  adoption step of its check is now `adopt_active_generation`, which both call): the procedure
  bindings of its composition record are the host's procedure manifest, so the table the start
  builds reads the composed packages and the start reads the keys of the runs before it. The first
  check finds the generation adopted and does not adopt it again; it still reads the games in use
  and composes as before. A generation that is no composed one, or whose record cannot be used,
  gives the manifest that binds no procedure, as the check gives it; no failure path is added.
- **A table follows its manifest:** the table keeps the digest of the manifest it was built from
  (`ProcedureManifest::digest`: SHA-256 over each binding's alias, binding digest and location, in
  alias order; none without a manifest), and `table_due` is also true when the evaluation's
  manifest has another digest. This covers any other order in which a manifest arrives after a
  table.
- **Every build says what it found:** each table taken into effect (`RemedyState::set_table`)
  writes `actingd remedy_table built catalog_hash=<hash> manifest=<sha256:…|none> tasks=<n>
  located=<n> remedy_tasks=<n> providers=<n> unbound=<n>` and, when some catalog task has no
  package location, `actingd remedy_table unbound tasks=<first ten ids> more=<n>`. The `finding`
  and `unreadable` lines are unchanged.

**What an operator sees after a restart.** Among the start's lines, before `actingd
startup_recovery`, one `actingd remedy_table built` line for the active catalog: in composer mode
with `manifest=sha256:…` and `located` equal to `tasks` when every composed task is bound, and the
number of tasks that declare a remedy and of providers the packages declare. A line with
`manifest=none`, or an `unbound` line, says the table read no package for those tasks. One more
such line follows each activation, a change of the manifest, and each rebuild while a round is
open. A first start with no composed generation yet writes its first line at the first cycle.
Nothing is configured.

**Older builds** keep the defect: in composer mode their start builds the table from no manifest,
and a blocked result opens no round until the next activation. Nothing in the ledger changes shape
and this build writes no new record, so an older build reads every record as before.

**Seen, not changed.** `actingd check-config` builds its offline table as before and writes no
summary line. The pack schedule view (`host/pack_schedule.rs`) reads the same table and so lists the
composed packages after a restart; no test of the view pins an empty table after a start (its tests
run in configured mode). The ten names of the `unbound` line are a constant: the bound of one log
line, not a scheduling value, and the work order adds no configuration key.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REM1-1 | the remedy table built at start from the active composed generation's bindings, and rebuilt when the manifest's digest changes | rule (no shape; corrects [remedies.md](remedies.md) section 7.1) | REM-1 | — | `since` 0.12.56; configured mode unchanged |
| REM1-2 | the developer lines `actingd remedy_table built` and `actingd remedy_table unbound` | log lines, no record and no interface | REM-1 | `RemedyState::set_table` | `since` 0.12.56 |

Tests (host gate row "#442 REM-1", `gate_442_rem1`; composer mode over one neutral game root on a
manual clock and a fake device; the rule, pool and profile builders of `gate_rl1b` are shared with
it, no assertion of `gate_rl1b` changes): `composer_restart_table_declares_remedies` (a second
start on the same files declares the blocked task's remedy and lists the provider before and after
its first cycle, and its summary line says so); `composer_restart_blocked_run_opens_round` (after a
restart the blocked task succeeds with the remedy key; the next cycle, inside the instance's
activity interval, holds it with `policy_remedy_waiting` naming its round; once the instance may
run again the provider's intent carries `policy_remedy_requested`, `remedy_source` `package`,
`irreversible` true; the provider takes the instance in that cycle, so the blocked task is settled
`instance_already_selected` there, as `gate_411_b15h` pins, and its hold is asserted in the cycle
before); `composer_restart_keeps_round_opened_before` (a blocking run from before the restart
opens its round after it); `remedy_table_names_unbound_tasks` (the tasks without a package
location in catalog order, their number in the summary, ten named and the rest counted, a located
package that cannot be read unreadable and not unbound, and `manifest=none` without a manifest). No
existing test changes.

**The interface.** `actingd-config` goes to 29: the row 29 of
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) holds HELD-1's member `task_held` of the
section and of an entry's `scheduling` member; `distribution/windows/component-interfaces.json`
and `tools/actinglab-architecture/tests/component_interfaces.rs` declare [5, 29]. HELD-2's word
and MAPP-1's members join that row when they ship in 0.12.56. `ledger`, `runtime-client`,
`runtime-outcomes` and every other interface stay (§1.322, "The interface walk").

**Where the code reads the contract, and why** (no point the contract's text leaves open is
guessed; each is a reading of its own words):

- *An end by the row's start.* A reported hold ends `why_changed` when the pair's row carries
  another start than the hold's: the table's `since_unix_ms` changes exactly when the `why` code
  does, or when a fact refresh wait names another `fact_key`. So `fact_refresh_pending` of one key
  followed by `fact_refresh_pending` of another restarts the row, which before HELD-1 kept its
  start ("another `fact_key` … starts another run").
- *The not-running row too.* The one clock of the three fact refresh waits applies to the
  not-running row's `since_unix_ms` as to the candidate rows' ("count as one `why` code for
  `since_unix_ms`").
- *Reported means in the projection.* A held record is written when the projection does not hold
  its id, also again at the next cycle when its append failed (the cycle failed loudly); an end is
  written only when the projection holds the held record ("a hold that was never reported leaves
  nothing"). A held record the projection holds for the row's start is taken as open.
- *A capped pair stopped by a gate.* `pool_line_held` with `capped_not_dispatchable` is held when
  its `gate_code` is one of the codes held whatever their values (`HELD_CODES`); a gate code a
  value decides cannot be decided from the code alone and is not held.
- *An instance the context does not name* (it is not in the snapshot) writes no new held record.
- *A held record the start cannot read back* stops no start (settled by the coordinator on 11-12
  at the slice's review; not the owner's words). The start reads a held record back by its own
  values: its outcome is `task_held`, its task and alias are the record's own, its `gate_code` is
  a code the catalog this build embeds registers (whether this build's held set holds it is not
  asked: the set is closed per build, a later slice may change it, and a hold another build
  reported is ended all the same), and its id is the digest of its task, alias and start. A
  record that fails one of these (a spelling this build does not register, a missing value,
  another digest) is left as it is, without an end, and the start goes on; the pass names such
  records on one developer line, `actingd task_held unreadable sequences=<s1,s2,…> more=<n>`
  (their ledger sequences, the first eight in ledger order, and the number of the rest; Fail
  Loud), and `actingd suspended` keeps listing each of them open. The reason: no decision reads
  these records, the ledger keeps what an earlier or a later build wrote, and a start that failed
  here would leave the settlement anchor where it was, so every later start would fail the same
  way until another build was installed. The slice's first form failed the start with
  `policy_planning_signal_identity_conflict`; that form was not merged. The pass runs over the
  range the settlement of direct runs reads, when it holds a record.
- *`ac_diagnose`'s cut.* Its `held` rows are cut after the clock slots and before `not_run`; the
  whole list stays in `actingd suspended`, and the records in `ac_events`' errors view.

**Tests** (`crates/runtime-host/src/tests/gate_438_held.rs`; host gate row "Workflow #438
HELD-1"). Logic tests on the policy host's own table and memory with a fake projection and a
manual clock: `held_t1`, `held_t2` (a pause, a cooldown, a false trigger, a blackout, an
exhausted budget, the benefit gaps that wait for a value, a hard line and a capped pair a budget
stops, beside a row that is reported), `held_t4`, `held_t5`, `held_t7`, `held_t10`. Through the
host on a manual Runtime clock: `held_t3` (a client lease holds the instance; the restart's end;
counting again), `held_t6` (two hosts, the record on and off, the same decisions, intents and
other records at every cycle; only decisions, reason codes and records are compared), `held_t8`,

**What an operator sees after deploy.** A pair that should run and is held by a held code for

**Also built.** The defaults file's `recovery_ladder.profiles` gains `without_emulator_restart`
(`return_home`, `application_restart`), the profile a member names. `actingd-config` rises to
[5, 29] (`distribution/windows/component-interfaces.json`, the architecture test,
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) row 29); MAPP-2's key comes with MAPP-2 and
takes the next free revision of `actingd-config` (0.12.56 ships revision 29 without it; corrected
by MAPP-1b, §1.330). A discovered index several entries resolve to names the first by alias as its
`bound_alias` (`provider_startup.rs`), as "Device-level actions" row 6 settles.

**MAPP-1b** (the next slice; its rows, listed here and nowhere else):

1. one worker per device: `InstanceWorkers` keyed by the device key, thread
   `actingd-device-<device_group>` for a group of several;
2. a member's occupancy read across the group (`instance_occupancy`, `dispatch_held_error`), with
   `device_group_waiting` `held`;
3. the admission guard keyed by the device key (`instance_guard`);
4. a scheduling pause of one member that waits only for that member's own work
   (`release_paused_instance`, which the scheduler's `member_refusing_count` is for);
5. the gates of the group: a fence of one member holds every member (`fenced`), a player hold of
   one member holds the device (`player_hold`), and a second hold on another member of the group
   is refused (`player_hold_already_held`);
6. no session kept across lease ends for a member of a group of several (`keeps_device_session`
   false);
7. the refusals of operator emulator control and of a keyless observation while another member
   holds the device (`device_group_action_refused`, registered by MAPP-1b);
8. a chain handover's successor before the candidates of the device's other members too (point 8
   below);

and the tests of these rows in §1.323's list. None of them can be reached by a configuration of
MAPP-1a: the load refuses every group of several.

**Where the build differs from the contract or completes it.** The coordinator accepted points 1,
5 and 6 as built and the manifest row as built (a row of the key table, not settable, read at
assembly, tier `hidden`), and settled points 4, 8 and 9 and the defaults profile ("A group of one
is today", below) on 11-12.

1. *The order of the table's rules.* The rules are checked per group by name, the kind rules
   first (`handset_member`, `fixture_member`), then `device_mismatch`, `application_shared`,
   `startup_package_missing`, `device_action_unsupported`; then undeclared sharing over every two
   entries, in configuration order; then `several_members_unsupported`. With the kinds first a
   fixture or a handset, which names no device key, is refused for what it is rather than as a
   mismatch.
2. *`aliases` and `config_key`.* `aliases` is the entries concerned: both entries of a mismatch,
   of a shared application or of undeclared sharing; the one member for the kind rules, a missing
   startup package and a device-level action; every member for `several_members_unsupported`.
   `config_key` is the entry's member: `host`, `port` or `serial` (the first that differs), or the
   key the differing member uses, for a mismatch; `port` for one host and port shared undeclared,
   `instance_index` for a discovered index shared after discovery.
3. *The keys an instruction's refusal names.* The member's own key (`start_emulator`,
   `idle.action`, `recovery_ladder_profile`), the section's `idle.action` when the member takes
   it, `recovery_ladder.kind_profiles` when the member climbs its kind's profile and
   `recovery_ladder.rungs` when it climbs the section's rungs; a change of `recovery_ladder.profiles`
   that puts `emulator_restart` into a profile a member names is refused on that member's
   `recovery_ladder_profile`.
4. *A malformed name* (settled by the coordinator on 11-12). The bound of 64 bytes stays. An empty
   name, one longer than 64 bytes or one the alias rules refuse is `device_group_config_invalid`
   with `aliases` the entry, `config_key` `device_group` and the word `name_invalid`, added to
   `device_group_problem` for it, not `invalid_instance_alias`: the alias is right, and the
   person must be told which member is wrong. It is the first of the group checks, on every entry
   that names a group (a group of one too), before the kind rules.
5. *`device_group_assembled`'s `device_label`* is the `HOST:PORT` the first member is bound to
   once the registry is built, and is optional: a discovery-bound member of a stopped emulator has
   no port yet.
6. *The manifest row's console tier* is `hidden`: `advanced` holds its eight keys, and how the
   console shows a device with its applications is the console slice's.
7. *The scheduler's gate per member.* A scheduling pause stays per instance, so the scheduler
   judges each queued entry by the gate of the member it serves (`MemberGates`: a `ClaimGate` is
   every member's, as every caller passes today; a closure gives each member its own).
8. *A chain handover's successor* (settled by the coordinator on 11-12). It goes before the
   candidates of the device's other members too: the contract's "Never interrupted" says the
   device's other members wait behind it, and a handover has its value only while its application
   stays in front. It is MAPP-1b's, not built in MAPP-1a: here the successor goes before the
   candidates of its own instance that outranked it, as today, and a candidate of another member
   that outranked it takes the device first, the successor waiting `device_group_waiting`.
9. *The state of a member that waits* (settled by the coordinator on 11-12). A candidate that
   waits for its device (`selected`) has exactly the state, the eligibility and the wake of a
   candidate behind its own instance's winner (`instance_already_selected`); only the code and its
   values differ. Neither is deferred by a later pass keyed by the instance: both keep the state
   the placement found, and the policy tests compare the one with the other.
10. *A serial names its device* (settled by the coordinator at the slice's review, 11-12). An
    explicit entry that names a `serial` is addressed by it (ADB's `-s`), and its `host` and `port`
    are the daemon's defaults when it names none; the default port is the first emulator's. So
    undeclared sharing reads two explicit entries as one device when both name the same serial
    (`config_key` `serial`), or when neither names a serial and their `host` and `port` are equal
    (`config_key` `port`). Two different serials, or a serial beside an endpoint, prove no
    sharing at assembly, and the check after the discovery compares a discovered endpoint only
    with the explicit entries that name no serial. The first form compared `host` and `port`
    alone, defaults included: a file that named two devices by their serials and no endpoint, or
    one such device beside the first emulator, accepted today, would have been refused; that form
    was not merged. A group's own rule is unchanged: its members name the same `host`, `port` and
    `serial`. Test `mapp1_two_serials_are_two_devices_whatever_their_host_and_port`.
11. *The held set* (settled by the coordinator on 11-12; done here after §1.327, HELD-1, was
    merged into this slice). The held set is closed, and a slice that adds a deferral code classes
    it ([scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md), "Held records", "The held set"; §1.322's
    census). `device_group_waiting` is held, due, whatever its `device_group_wait`: a member that
    waits hours for its device behind another member is the starvation a held record exists for,
    and it is the device's form of `instance_already_selected` and `dispatch_instance_held`,
    which are held. So `HELD_CODES` (`crates/runtime-host/src/policy_host/held.rs`) has 18 codes,
    12 of them due; the census gains its row and the contract's list names it. MAPP-1a writes the
    code only with `selected`, and no configuration of MAPP-1a reaches it (the load refuses every
    group of several): test `held_t12_a_member_that_waits_for_its_device_is_held` gives the
    detector such a row.

**A group of one is today.** With no entry naming one device twice, every decision, record, key
and byte the Runtime persists is as before, but for the contract's three exceptions
([device-group.md](device-group.md), "A group of one is today"): the refusal of undeclared
sharing; MAPP-2's key; and the defaults file's profile `without_emulator_restart`, which the
coordinator kept in the defaults file on 11-12 and wrote in as the third exception. It is a member
of the default of `recovery_ladder.profiles`, so on a root whose file and instructions leave that
key at its default three things change, and only these: the value of the manifest's row
`recovery_ladder.profiles`, the program fact `config.parameters.recovery_ladder` that carries the
row, and the ladder's configuration digest (`recovery_ladder_started` `config_digest`, the SHA-256
of the section's values in effect: `LadderConfig::digest`, `crates/runtime-config/src/recovery_ladder.rs`, which reads `profiles` with
every other key of the section). A profile set the file names replaces the default whole, so such
a root sees none of them; a root whose instruction set the key keeps the instruction's value and
its start notes `config_override_base_changed` on the key. Nothing climbs by the profile unless an
entry names it (`recovery_ladder_profile`): the defaults' `kind_profiles` name only `handset`, so
every ladder climbs the rungs it climbs today, and the profile's two rungs, those of `handset`,
add no refusal under `rules.start_beyond_profile` `refuse`.

**What an operator sees after deploy.** A root without `device_group` runs as before; a file whose
`device_group` is not a name of 1 to 64 bytes under the alias rules is refused at its start,
`device_group_config_invalid`, `name_invalid`; a file that
names one device from two entries outside one group is refused at its start (at assembly, or
after the discovery as a Provider startup failure), `device_group_config_invalid`,
`undeclared_shared_device`; a file with a group of several is refused at its start,
`several_members_unsupported` (or the broken rule's problem), until the release that carries the
order within one device. check-config reports the same. A console whose `actingd-config` range
ends at 28 does not pair with this build's [5, 29] until the UI repository raises its range.

**Rollback** (below 0.12.56). Remove every `device_group` (an older build refuses the member,
`config_decode_failed`). Nothing is persisted by MAPP-1: no record type, payload member, fact,
tag or state file; the owner journal's ids are member ids an older build reads as before.

### 1.330 Slice MAPP-1b (0.12.57): device groups in the host: one worker per device, the group's occupancy, gates, session rule and refusals, and a chain handover's successor before the device's other members (Workflow #437; the contract of §1.323 and the list of §1.328, "MAPP-1b", with its points 7 to 10; the coordinator's rulings it records, not the owner's words; coordinator work order `rd-1112/brief-437-mapp-1b.md`, read on main `dffd6263`)

1.330 is the coordinator's number, appended after §1.329. The contract is
[device-group.md](device-group.md), the passages §1.323 lists and §1.328's list "MAPP-1b". A
build still refuses every group of several at load (`several_members_unsupported`, unchanged), so
no configuration reaches this slice's code: its tests hand the host the member → device key map
and the group's name as the assembly builds them.

| §1.328 "MAPP-1b" row | Built | Where |

| 1 one worker per device | yes | `crates/runtime-host/src/host/host_claims.rs`, `spawn_instance_workers` (one worker per device key: `actingd-instance-<alias>` for an instance alone on its device, a group of one included, `actingd-device-<device_group>` for a group of several), `post_host_claim` and `post_policy_run` (the device's worker); the name comes from `RuntimeHostConfig::with_device_group_names` (`crates/runtime-host/src/host.rs`), which actingd fills from `DeviceGroups::names` beside `with_device_keys` (`apps/actingd/src/config.rs`) |

| 5 the gates of the group | the gates yes; the refusal of a second hold no | `device_group_hold`: another member's player hold (`player_hold`, the control gates' player-hold dimension, `SchedulingPauseTable::player_holds`), then another member's fence (`fenced`). | 6 no session kept across lease ends | yes | `crates/runtime-host/src/host/resource_close.rs`, `keeps_device_session` (false for a member of a group of several) |
