**The code.** `device_group_action_refused` (`runtime-host`, error, ladder class `none`, `since`
0.12.57, values `alias` and `operation` required; its description, common causes and handling
written). `runtime-outcomes` stays 1; no key, no record type, payload member, fact, tag or state
file is added.

**Where the build differs from the contract or completes it.**

1. *The order of a member's waits.* The member's own control gates come first, then its own
   holder (each with its own code); then another member's player hold, another member's fence
   (the one order of the control gates; the other members in alias order) and another member's
   holder; then the device's takeover cooldown (`dispatch_instance_cooldown`, as before). These
   are the eligibility's waits. A candidate behind the round's winner of its device waits
   `selected` before any of them is asked, as one behind its own instance's winner waits
   `instance_already_selected` (§1.328, point 9): so a paused member's candidate waits `selected`
   in a round another member wins, and with its own pause's code in a round no member wins (test
   `mapp1b_a_pause_of_one_member_waits_only_for_its_own_work_and_leaves_the_other_scheduled`,
   corrected in fix round 1: it expected the pause's code in both).
2. *The admission's refusal* is `device_group_waiting` with the waiting member's alias as
   `instance_id` (as the policy's reasons name it, where `dispatch_instance_held` names the opaque
   identifier), the hold's values and `operation` `admit_policy_dispatch`, at info, as the catalog
   entry of MAPP-1a declares its receipt values.
3. *`task_id` with `held`* is the catalog task of a registered run (a run handed to the device's
   worker); a policy dispatch's lease on the driver's own thread (`scheduling.parallel.enabled`
   off) is held with no `task_id`.
4. *The player hold is not built* (Workflow #429 R-7b: `AcquirePlayerHold` and
   `ReleasePlayerHold` answer `not_implemented`; only tests set the hold's dimension). Row 5's
   gate is built: another member's hold holds the device for every member (`player_hold`), on that
   dimension. The refusal of a second hold on another member (`player_hold_already_held`) is not
   built, and no build refuses one: there is no acquire to refuse it in. Accepted by the
   coordinator on 11-12: the drain at acquisition, that refusal and the release are not
   MAPP-1b's; they come with the slice that builds player holds (R-7b), which reads the group.
5. *A fence of one member* holds the other members' dispatches (evaluation and admission). Its
   own routine claims stay held as before; the other members' claims and direct requests are not.
6. *A keyless observation's refusal* is written as the capacity refusal of an observation is
   (`scheduler.denied`, then the failure's record), with `operation` `observe_readonly` for every
   keyless observation (an observe, a capture sequence, a Lab observation). "Another member holds
   the device" is another member's lease (lapsed or not) or the device held for the member by
   another member's run or waiting claim, as its occupancy reads it. A member that holds the
   device itself, and a free device, are not refused.
7. *Emulator control* of a member is refused first in its request, before its intent and before
   the fixture check, with no record (a fixture is never a member in a configuration).
8. *Two handovers on one device.* A device has at most one handover in a round, the first in rank
   order; a later successor of another member of the device is an ordinary candidate. The
   candidates that wait under `policy_chain_handover_waiting` stay those of the successor's own
   instance; the device's other members wait `device_group_waiting` `selected`.
9. *A group of several the host was not given a name for* stops the start with
   `instance_worker_spawn_failed` (its worker cannot be named as the contract says).
10. *Not changed:* the pump and the transfers still judge a device's queue by the routine gate of
    the instance they are called for (as MAPP-1a left them); only the occupancy reads each
    member's gate.
11. *A keyless observation served on a free device* (the coordinator's ruling of 11-12: the
    contract's rule that two sessions of one device are never open at once wins). Its capture
    runs under the device's admission guard (row 3), so for its duration no other member's run
    starts: a dispatch admission meets the guard (`dispatch_instance_contended`) and a lease
    grant waits for it. Before the guard frees the device, the member's session is closed
    (`close_keyless_session_of_group`, after each frame, so between two frames of a sequence
    the device is free and holds no session): through a dedicated close lease, as a lease end
    closes it (row 6), and the lease ends as the other closes of a session a lease-free path
    retained end theirs (`close_device_link_session`, `close_lapsed_run_session_guarded`:
    `LeaseReleaseReason::BackendFailure`, which hands the key to a claim queued meanwhile, else
    releases it). A close that fails fails the observation, its records written by the close
    path. A device a lease of the member holds (a ladder's settle probe) leaves the session to
    that lease's end. An instance alone on its device keeps its session as before. Test
    `mapp1b_a_keyless_observation_of_a_member_keeps_no_session_and_no_other_member_runs_under_it`.
    *Fix round 1 (CI of pull request #1635):* the first build ended the close lease as an
    explicit release (`LeaseReleaseReason::Explicit`), which the scheduler takes only from a
    client's release request (`release_owned` refuses it); the lease end was refused with the
    lease still held (`scheduler_cleanup_state_mismatch`, `cleanup_runtime_lease`), and the member
    was fenced (`instance_resources_fenced`). *Open, for the slice "order within one device":* a
    close lease that a waiting claim refuses (`lease_transfer_not_safe`: the member's own claim,
    or a claim of any member queued while the capture ran, which meets the device's guard and
    waits) leaves the session to the member's next lease end, recorded once; when that claim is
    another member's, the member's session stays open while the claim's lease runs, so two
    members' sessions are open on the device for that time. In the device's takeover cooldown the
    close lease is refused (`lease_cooldown`) and the observation fails with it after its capture,
    the session left open likewise. Closing either needs a close lease that a queued claim or a
    cooldown does not refuse, or the capture held under a lease of its own; neither is this
    slice's.

**The held set.** `device_group_waiting` is held, due, whatever its `device_group_wait` (§1.328,
point 11). The waits `held`, `player_hold` and `fenced` carry it, so a member that waits past
`scheduling.task_held.after_ms` leaves one held record (`gate_code` `device_group_waiting`), counted
from the first round in which it waited for its device under any of the four words; test
`mapp1b_one_worker_per_device_and_a_member_held_behind_the_others_registered_run`.

**A group of one is today.** Every map keyed by the device key has today's keys for an instance
alone on its device (its own id), its worker keeps `actingd-instance-<alias>`, its occupancy,
admission, pause release, guard, session rule and requests take the paths they took, and the
evaluator's handovers are keyed by the instance (`DeviceGroups::default()`). The existing tests of
those paths are unchanged.

**MAPP-2's key** (the coordinator's correction of 11-12, text only). 0.12.56 ships `actingd-config`
revision 29 with HELD-1's `task_held` and MAPP-1a's `device_group` and without MAPP-2's
`scheduling.device_group.switch_failure_cooldown_ms`. As row 29 of
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) says, that key comes with MAPP-2 and takes the
next free revision. [device-group.md](device-group.md) ("The key", "Interfaces", "Release"),
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) ("Planned: Workflow #437 MAPP" and its row),
[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("Device groups", the switch cooldown), §1.323 (its
table, its interface walk, settled point 14, "Release", "What changes live", "Rollback") and
§1.328's "Also built" say so now, and that MAPP-1a shipped in 0.12.56 with every group of several
refused at load, while the release that first accepts a group of several carries MAPP-1b, MAPP-2
and the order within one device together (the coordinator's correction of 11-12).

**Tests.** `crates/runtime-host/src/tests/gate_mapp1b.rs` (gate map `host.toml`) and
`crates/policy/src/tests/gate_mapp1b.rs` (`policy.toml`).

**What an operator sees after deploy.** Nothing: the load refuses every group of several, so no
root runs this slice's code until the release that carries the order within one device. A root
without `device_group` runs as before.

**Rollback** (below 0.12.57). Nothing is persisted by MAPP-1b; the build before it reads every
record this one writes.

### 1.331 Slice LAB-OCR-DL (0.12.57): an offline evaluation of a saved scene can raise the OCR inference deadline to the contract's maximum (Workflow #428; after VIS-LOAD-1, §1.298, a resource repository's CI frame regression on a hosted runner, on the CPU, still failed 1 check of 2260 in 1 of 3 runs on Tools v0.12.54 with `candidate_feature_failed` … `Timeout: fatal vision FFI error in ppocr_ctc_engine: PPOCR recognizer could not start before the configured timeout`; the coordinator's rulings of 11-12 on board #428, not the owner's words; coordinator work order `rd-1112/brief-lab-ocr-deadline.md`, read on main `dffd6263`)

1.331 is the next free number: main `dffd6263` holds 1.329, CODES-T2, and 1.330 is MAPP-1b's, in
flight. [vision-model-folders.md](vision-model-folders.md), "Startup and first use", is the
contract and gains one sentence; [package-reference.md](package-reference.md) defines no
`timeout_ms` and does not change; the operation table
([lab-operations.json](lab-operations.json)) declares the switch. No persisted ledger shape, wire
shape, configuration key, outcome code, closed vocabulary or interface revision changes, no
package's `timeout_ms` or its bounds (1 to 60 000), and no file of today's MCP server
(`apps/actingctl/src/mcp/**`).

**The rulings** (the coordinator's, 11-12, board #428). A package's `timeout_ms` is not changed for
CI, and production keeps every deadline it has. An offline regression asks whether a saved scene is
recognised correctly, not whether it is recognised fast enough, and a cold CPU process on a shared
runner says nothing about production's speed: so an offline evaluation of a saved scene may, on an
explicit switch, raise each OCR target's inference deadline to the contract's maximum, 60 000 ms.
Raised, not removed: a hung inference still ends. The switch is refused wherever the frame does not
come from a saved scene.

**The rows.** The rows that declare `scene` (an offline PNG frame) and whose saved-scene path
evaluates it with the Lab's OCR provider, so that it can reach an OCR target (page detection
evaluates every target of every page; a target reaches the members of a composite and the sides of
a value test). Each loads its package through `contained_resources::load_with_ocr_deadline`, whose
bundle evaluator holds the provider every evaluation of the line uses.

| Row | The path that takes the switch |
|---|---|
| `observe` | `--scene` (not `--capture`): page detection, `--targets`, the actions' targets, the candidate layouts |
| `do` | `--scene` with `--dry-run`: the page, the guard and the target |
| `ensure` | `--scene` with `--dry-run`: the page |
| `wait` | `--scene`: the page or the stable target, each poll |
| `recognize`, `is-visible` | `--scene` (their `--capture` is retired and refused): the target |
| `detect-page`, `current-page` | `--scene`: page detection |
| `tap-target`, `navigate` | `--scene` with `--dry-run`, their only path (`--capture` is retired): the target, the page |

Not given the switch: `recover`, whose planned recovery builds its evaluator without a vision
provider (`RecognitionEvaluator::new`), so that an OCR target is never inferred there
(`recognition_pack_provider_missing`); `locate`, template matching only; `recognize-artifact`,
whose request (`RecognizeArtifact`) the resident Runtime evaluates. The rows that evaluate saved
frames that are no `scene` are not the rulings' rows and do not take it: `regression` (a run's
frames, read from a state root's ledger, through the same load and with no time bound of its own),
`replay` and the dry runs of a package over a directory of frames, and the authoring rows'
recordings. **Open for the coordinator:** `replay` runs the kernel's contained task, whose sampling
deadline (`with_sample_deadline`, sized from the declared `timeout_ms`) a raised deadline would
outgrow; giving it the switch would change the kernel's recognition outside the Lab's own entry, so
it is not done here.

**Where a target's `timeout_ms` becomes the engine's deadline on these paths.** The recognition
pack's evaluator builds each OCR request with the target's `timeout_ms` (a candidate layout's shared
read with its own, `shared_ocr.timeout_ms`) as `OcrProviderRequest.timeout_ms` (`evaluate_ocr`, the
OCR observation, `read_shared_text`, the text locate) and hands it to the provider the package load
gave it: the kernel's `VisionFfiProvider` over the `ppocr-ctc` engine on the CPU
(`LabOcr::from_vision_root`, `crates/lab/src/ocr.rs`). Its `call_ocr` takes it as the request's
deadline (the wait for the model's lock and, in `load_ocr`, for another request's runtime
initialisation) and gives the engine what remains, which the engine's `read_request` takes as its
inference deadline (§1.298). With the switch actinglab gives the package load
`with_ocr_deadline_max(provider)` instead (`crates/lab/src/ocr.rs`), which hands every OCR request
on with `timeout_ms` 60 000 (`OCR_DEADLINE_MAX_MS`) and changes nothing else: model admission, NN
requests and the provider's reports pass through. The kernel's provider then bounds the request and
the engine its inference by 60 000. No file of the kernel, the recognition pack or the engine
changes, and no path the resident Runtime runs builds the wrapper.

**The other wall-clock bounds of these paths, with the switch.**

- The recognition pack's sample deadline (an OCR target whose `timeout_ms` exceeds what is left is
  not started, `recognition sample budget insufficient`; `recognition_sample_deadline_exceeded`
  after an evaluation): only the kernel's contained task sets one (`with_sample_deadline`); the
  scene contexts of these rows (`scene_context`, `scene_context_with_samples`) carry none. Nothing
  to change.
- The saved artifact's OCR request deadline (`evaluate_saved_artifact_ocr`, 120 s): the Runtime's
  `RecognizeArtifact`, on no path of these rows. Unchanged.
- The package admission deadline (`ContainedTaskRequest::DEFAULT_RESPONSE_DEADLINE_MS`, in
  `contained_resources::load_with_ocr_deadline`): it bounds the reading of the package, before
  anything is evaluated. Unchanged.
- `wait`'s `--timeout-ms` (default 5 000) and `--poll-ms`: the wait compares the time spent only
  after a whole evaluation and answers `arrived` when the page or the target is what it waits for,
  whatever the time; it never refuses or cuts an evaluation. Unchanged.
- `do`'s `--after-timeout-ms`, `ensure`'s and `navigate`'s `--step-timeout-ms` and `--poll-ms`:
  online or pressing only, refused or not read on these paths. Unchanged.
- The text-read budget and a candidate projection's provider budget count calls and area, not time;
  the 5 s limit of a unique template search is a template's. Unchanged.

So the offline path is consistent without any further change, and no code the production path
shares changes.

**The switch.** `--ocr-deadline-max`, the proposed name, which the table's naming rule gives the
parameter `ocr_deadline_max` (form `switch`, type `boolean`, not required, the last parameter of
each of the ten rows, its `note` saying the above). The command lines read it through their lists:
`lab2_cli::LAB2_SWITCHES` and the reads of the four `--scene` paths (`OBSERVE_SCENE`, `DO_SCENE`,
`ENSURE_SCENE`, `WAIT_SCENE`; no `--capture` path reads it), and the switches of
`readonly_cli::READONLY_INPUT_READS`, a part of the six readers' read lists. `serve --stdio` hands
it on as any switch of a row; `help` and the completion read it from the table. No row's `help`
changes: a row's sentence says what the row does and nothing its parameters say (LAB-5E,
[lab-two-entries.md](lab-two-entries.md) §9.1), and the parameter's note says this.

**Refused off a saved scene.** Given beside `--capture`, or on a line with no `--scene`, the switch
is refused before any package is loaded or any frame read: `validation_failed`, its details
`{argument: "--ocr-deadline-max", argument_problem: "conflicting"}`, the message
"--ocr-deadline-max raises the OCR inference deadline of an offline evaluation of saved scenes
only: give --scene, without --capture". `detect-page`, `tap-target` and `navigate` carry those
details in their trace's `details`, as every refusal of theirs.

**The answer.** With the switch every answer of these rows that stands carries the member
`ocr_deadline_raised_to_ms`, `60000`, beside its others (on actinglab's line flat beside `outcome`,
LAB-2b); `observe`, `do`, `ensure` and `wait` keep it in Min (`lab2_projection_request`'s kept
members). Without the switch every line is as before, byte for byte. A failure's line is the
failure's, unchanged.

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)): no declared
interface covers the Lab's lines, and the one member appears only when the switch is given.

**At deploy.** Nothing changes in production, nor for any command line without the switch. A
resource repository's regression script may pass `--ocr-deadline-max` to `observe --scene` and
`recognize --scene` once its Tools pin has it; a build without it refuses the switch as a flag it
does not read. **Rollback** (below 0.12.57): the switch is refused again as unknown.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OCRDL-1 | `ocr_deadline_max` (`--ocr-deadline-max`) on `observe`, `do`, `ensure`, `wait`, `recognize`, `detect-page`, `current-page`, `is-visible`, `tap-target`, `navigate` | operation table parameter, a switch | LAB-OCR-DL | actinglab | `since` 0.12.57; a saved scene only |
| OCRDL-2 | `ocr_deadline_raised_to_ms` | member of those rows' answers | LAB-OCR-DL | actinglab | `since` 0.12.57; only with the switch; 60000 |
| OCRDL-3 | `with_ocr_deadline_max`, `OCR_DEADLINE_MAX_MS` (`crates/lab`) | Lab-internal | LAB-OCR-DL | — | the wrapper of the Lab's provider; the contract's bound, no tunable |
| OCRDL-4 | what a target's `timeout_ms` bounds offline ([vision-model-folders.md](vision-model-folders.md)) | contract sentence | LAB-OCR-DL | — | the switch; production never |

Tests (apps gate row "#428 LAB-OCR-DL"):
`gate_428_lab_ocr_dl::lab_ocr_dl_an_inference_longer_than_the_timeout_fails_without_the_switch_and_passes_with_it`
(`crates/lab`: the readers' evaluation, `ReadonlyRecognitionEngine`, over a fake provider whose
inference takes 3 000 ms of an OCR target that declares 1 000: without the switch it fails with
the engine's Timeout of today, its request's deadline 1 000; through `with_ocr_deadline_max` it
passes, its request's deadline 60 000; no clock, no sleep, no model), and
`gate_428_lab_ocr_dl::lab_ocr_dl_the_answer_names_the_raised_deadline_only_with_the_switch` and
`lab_ocr_dl_the_switch_off_a_saved_scene_is_refused` (actinglab's bin, a neutral package and frame:
the member on each of the ten rows only with the switch, `recognize`'s answer otherwise the same;
the refusal beside `--capture` and without `--scene`). The lists extended are the code's:
`lab2_cli::LAB2_SWITCHES` (8 to 9), the reads of `OBSERVE_SCENE`, `DO_SCENE`, `ENSURE_SCENE` and
`WAIT_SCENE`, and the switches of `readonly_cli::READONLY_INPUT_READS`, which LAB-5B2's
`strict_rows_match_their_commands` and LAB-5B3's `lenient_rows_match_their_reads` hold equal to the
ten rows. No golden and no list of CLI-HELP or CLI-COMP changes (both read the table), and no
existing test changes.

### 1.332 Slice IDLE-3 (0.12.57): an idle action is taken only on a plan that counts the end of the instance's last run (Workflow #447; a production defect of v0.12.54; the coordinator's rulings of 11-12 on board #447, not the owner's words)

1.332 is the coordinator's number. [runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md), "The `idle` section", is
the contract and says when the action runs in the terms below. No persisted ledger shape, wire
shape, configuration key, outcome code, record shape, closed vocabulary or interface revision
changes.

**The defect** (production, v0.12.54; the idle code was the same on main). A chain of two
scheduled tasks on one instance: the second becomes due once the first has ended (it reads the
first's end). Within one second the ledger holds, in this order: `task.completed` (the first task
ends), `lease.released` (its lease), `lease.requested` (the idle action asks for the instance's key,
granted at once), `policy.execution_recorded` and `policy.dispatch_completed` (the policy records
the first task's execution), `command.received` to `application.completed` (the application is
stopped), `instance_idle_action` `run_idle_action` `close_app` (its next occurrence about an hour
later), `instance_idle_action` `queue_idle_wake` (a wake queued at once), `policy.dispatch_intent`
(the second task), and 0.13 s later `policy.dispatch_rejected` `dispatch_instance_held` behind the
startup package. The cold start took about 50 s and ended at the home page; the second task's
package starts from the page the first one ends on, so it failed at its first step, and the work of
that cycle was not done.

**The cause.**

1. The idle action waited for a plan evaluated after the last idle check that found the instance in
   use (`in_use_at_unix_ms`): a sample of the lease, taken at each policy cycle and once a second.
2. A run's lease is released before its settlement, which appends `policy.execution_recorded` and
   `policy.dispatch_completed` in one hold of the policy's guard.
3. The next task of a chain is due only from the completion: its predecessor's terminal state
   (`task_runtime_snapshots`) and outcome (`outcome_key_snapshot`) come from completed dispatches.
4. An evaluation that read its inputs before that completion, but was evaluated after the last check
   that saw the lease, passed the sample: its plan had the next task's trigger unknown and the next
   work an hour away.
5. The first check after the release that read it, the evaluation's own check or a lease sweep's
   (the ledger does not say which, and the rule does not depend on it), closed the application;
   the evaluation that counted the completion came a fraction of a second later.

**The rule.** An idle action step (`IdleStep::Act` and `IdleStep::Rest`: return home, close the
application, stop the emulator) is decided only on a plan from an evaluation that already counted
the end of every run the policy dispatched on the instance: at the time that evaluation read its
inputs, the policy held no dispatch of the instance that was still open (from its intent to the
record of its execution), and none has been opened since. A dispatch is open from its intent until
its completion (`policy.dispatch_completed`) or its refusal: the settlement appends the completion
with the record of the execution, in the same hold of the policy's guard, and the completion is what
makes the next task of a chain due (3 above), so it is the anchor. A dispatch the start could not
settle (`quarantine_dispatch`) is not counted, as it is not among the pending settlements: no end of
it comes in that start. How the host knows it: the evaluation reads, under the guard it projects
its inputs under, the instances with an open dispatch and the ledger position of its inputs
(`PolicyHost::idle_dispatches_read`), kept with its not-run explanation; at a check,
`PolicyHost::idle_runs_counted` holds that a dispatch opened since has its intent after that
position, and the dispatch journal keeps every open dispatch and each pair's latest intent. The
check reads the plan and this answer under one guard (`IdleView::run_uncounted`), the cycle's check
and the sweep's alike. The sampled rule stays beside it for work the policy does not dispatch
(manual, direct, Lab, ladder and host runs). A wake reads every plan as before: an owed wake, the
switch, `none` and the kept state across a start are unchanged.

**On the key.** The action's claim checked a pause and a request queued meanwhile; it now also reads
the latest plan again by the same rule (`idle_action::stands_on_key`): a plan that does not count
the end of every run the policy dispatched on the instance, or that shows a task or a reading due,
or its next work closer than the gap the step is taken from (`idle_action::action_min_gap_ms`:
`idle.min_gap_ms`, under `auto` `stop_emulator`'s `idle.stop_emulator_min_gap_ms`; a rest's
`idle.return_home_min_gap_ms`), leaves the instance alone as for a pause: the planner's `abandoned`,
nothing sent, no record of an action. A skipped step needs no record: it is decided again at the
next check, on a plan that counts the run's end, normally within the same second.

**What an operator sees.** Nothing new: no record, code or key. The action comes at the first idle
check after the evaluation that counts the run's end, and a chain's next task is no longer met by a
closed application. **Older builds** (below 0.12.57) keep the defect; a rollback brings it back and
changes nothing else, since nothing is persisted.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IDLE3-1 | when an idle action or rest is decided ([runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md), "The `idle` section") | rule (no shape change) | IDLE-3 | — | a plan that counts the end of the instance's last run; `IdleView::run_uncounted`, `RunsRead` |
| IDLE3-2 | the check on the action's key | rule (no shape change) | IDLE-3 | — | the latest plan read again (`stands_on_key`); abandoned as for a pause |
| IDLE3-3 | `PolicyHost::idle_dispatches_read`, `PolicyHost::idle_runs_counted` | memory only | IDLE-3 | — | read with the evaluation's inputs; replaced with its not-run explanation; a start begins with none |

Tests (host gate row "IDLE-3", the idle planner on a manual clock, in the defect's order with the
ledger positions of the dispatches): `gate_idle3::idle_action_waits_for_plan_after_run_end` (no step
after the release on the plan that read the first dispatch open, though the sampled rule passes it;
none on the next plan with the second task due; the second task's claim and run meet an instance
never closed), `idle_action_waits_for_plan_after_run_end_under_auto` (the same with `auto`, the
next work in a rest's gap and in `close_app`'s), `idle_action_runs_after_fresh_plan` (the next plan
counts the end and shows the next task an hour away: one `close_app`, its wake at next due minus the
lead) and `idle_action_abandoned_on_key_for_newer_plan` (`close_app` and a rest under `auto` do not
stand on their key against a task due, work closer than the gap, a reading due or a dispatch opened
after the read; the planner is active again and decides once more). On a real policy host, through
the mapped chain of two tasks on one neutral instance (the second due once the first has completed)
and evaluated cycles at fixed times on the manual Runtime clock:
`gate_idle3_host::idle_runs_counted_follows_the_policys_dispatches` (`PolicyHost::idle_runs_counted`
is true before any evaluated cycle and after a cycle evaluated with nothing open; false once that
cycle's dispatch is admitted, after a cycle evaluated while it is admitted and after its execution
and completion with no new evaluation; true after the cycle evaluated after the completion, whose
plan shows the second task due; false once the second task's dispatch is admitted). Not reached
there: an intent apart from its admission (the live admission records both under one guard) and a
dispatch a start could not settle (it needs a start that refuses the run's settlement). No existing
test changes.

### 1.333 Slice SBUD-1 (0.12.57): admission refuses a step whose declared sampling need cannot fit its deadline (Workflow #448; a released package whose select step failed at every run in production on v0.12.54, though `standard-pack check` and the Runtime's admission had passed it; the coordinator's rulings of 11-13 on board #448, not the owner's words; coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-448-sbud-1.md`, read on main `a01fac44`)

1.333 is the coordinator's number: 1.332 belongs to a pull request not merged yet.
[business-identity-consensus.md](business-identity-consensus.md) (the select step's budget),
[selection-graph.md](selection-graph.md) ("Select step", the admission checks),
[resource-readings.md](resource-readings.md) ("List readings", "Declaration") and
[policy-suspension.md](policy-suspension.md) ("What is suspended") gain sentences. No outcome code,
value key, configuration key, persisted shape, wire shape or closed vocabulary is added, and no
interface revision moves. The catalog's text of `recognition_sample_budget_invalid` speaks of
declared sampling in general (its causes name "consensus or candidate sampling declarations" and
"a package written for an older kernel whose budget rule was looser"), not of consensus only, so it
does not change and the index is not regenerated.

**The defect.** A released package changed the candidate layout of a select step: it gained OCR
features that read an integer, four rows read at a time, each target declaring `timeout_ms` 5 000,
with no consensus. The package declares no step timeout, so the step's deadline is the default
5 000 ms. `standard-pack check` passed it and the Runtime admitted it; at that step every run failed
after one frame with `candidate_sample_budget_insufficient`, `{required_ms: 20000, remaining_ms:
4997}`, and nothing said so before a run.

**The cause** (main `a01fac44`, `crates/execution-kernel/src/`):

1. At a select step's start (`contained_task/selection.rs`, `select_attempt`) the run compares
   `sampling_budget_ms` with what is left of the step's deadline; that function answers only when
   the pack declares target consensus or the layout consensus.
2. The projection (`project_transaction_placed`) samples a layout that has consensus or a feature
   with an identity or an integer, and compares its declared worst provider time plus waits
   (`CandidateLayout::maximum_provider_and_wait_ms`, less the waits between its frames) with what is
   left. The production failure came from here: 4 × 5 000 = 20 000.
3. Load (`contained_task.rs`, `prepare_bundle`) compared only `sampling_budget_ms` with each
   operation's limit (the smaller of the step and task timeouts; a scan's `max_ms`), so a layout
   without consensus was never compared.
4. The same projection runs on each viewport of a select over a scan (`scan/online.rs`) and of a
   list reading, whose `sampling_budget_ms` reads only `operation.select`.
5. `standard-pack check`, `package check` and `package preflight` admit through the same load, so
   they passed what the Runtime admitted.

**The one function and its two users.** `selection::candidate_provider_need_ms(layout, evaluator)`
answers, for a layout that has consensus or a feature that reads an identity or an integer, its
declared worst provider time plus waits less the waits between its frames, and `None` for any other
layout, which is projected on the step's frame alone. The run's check (`project_transaction_placed`)
takes from it both whether the layout is sampled and checked and the need it compares, at the same
point as before: the same refusal, `candidate_sample_budget_insufficient` with the same
`required_ms`. Admission takes it through `selection::step_provider_need_ms(operation, evaluator)`,
on the layout of a prepared select step (single-frame or over a scan) or of a prepared list reading,
and compares it in `prepare_bundle`'s loop with the operation's limit as the loop computes it: the
smaller of the step and task timeouts, or a scan's `max_ms` capped by the task's `timeout_ms`. A
larger need is `recognition_sample_budget_invalid` with `required_ms`, `limit_ms` and
`pack_operation_id`, as the loop's existing refusal carries them, and the developer detail
`operation=<id> requires <n>ms across candidate provider calls and waits; limit=<m>ms`; a need equal
to the limit is admitted. `sampling_budget_ms` does not change: its answer decides the run at its
other two callers.

**Item 4 of the investigation, verified real.** Every capture of a list reading's scan takes the
step's timing, whose deadline is the scan's `max_ms`; in a pack with target consensus each one
samples its page and first checks that what is left holds
`selection::page_recognition_budget_ms(…, None)` (`capture_frame_gated`,
`recognition_sample_budget_insufficient`). Load compared that need with the step and task timeouts
only, and the list reading's `sampling_budget_ms` counts its guard alone. Admission now compares it
with the list reading's limit too (detail `… across page calls and waits`), before the projection's
need, the order a run meets them in. A select over a scan needs no such change: its
`sampling_budget_ms` holds the page term whenever the pack declares consensus and was compared with
its `max_ms` already.

**What it leaves as it was.** For a layout with consensus the existing comparison of
`sampling_budget_ms` (twice the layout's provider time and waits, and more) is at least this need,
so the new comparison refuses nothing more there. A `linear_steps` task declares no select step and
no list reading.

**What an author sees.** `standard-pack check` (and `package check`, `package preflight`) of such a
package refuses it before any run: `package_invalid`, caused by `recognition_sample_budget_invalid`
naming the operation (`pack_operation_id`), the need (`required_ms`) and the limit (`limit_ms`),
instead of a package that passes and a run that fails at the step. The remedy is the package's: a
step timeout (for a scan, a `max_ms`) above the need, or fewer or shorter provider reads. The
bound is necessary, not sufficient: a run compares the same need with what is left of the step
once its first frame is taken and its page recognized, so a limit exactly at the need is admitted
and is still refused in a run (the production case had 4 997 ms left of 5 000). An author leaves
room for that first capture; how much depends on the device, so admission does not fix a margin.

**What older builds do.** A build before 0.12.57 admits such a package and ends every run at the
step with `candidate_sample_budget_insufficient` (`required_ms`, `remaining_ms`), which the default
`scheduling.rerun.condition_codes` reruns, to fail the same way. A package whose step timeout covers
its need runs on every build.

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md), "Bump rule"): no
member of a pack or a bundle is added, removed, renamed or given another meaning, and no record or
document an older reader refuses is written. Admission refuses more of an already admitted shape,
as LOAD-4 (§1.262) and LOAD-4b (§1.265) did with `package` staying. Unlike theirs, the refused shape
is in a released package, which already failed at every run; from this build on it is refused, and
suspended under the default `scheduling.pack_admission.suspend_codes`, until its content changes.
`actingd-config`, `ledger`, `runtime-client`, `runtime-outcomes`, `install-*`, `player-hold` and
`tools-layout`: untouched.

**At deploy.** Packages that declare a need over their deadline are refused at admission and by the
offline checks, and the Runtime suspends them instead of failing their step at every run. Before a
deploy every installed package root is checked with the new build's Lab (`standard-pack check`).
**Rollback** (below 0.12.57): such a package is admitted again and fails at its step as before.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SB1-1 | `recognition_sample_budget_invalid` (`required_ms`, `limit_ms`, `pack_operation_id`): a select step's, single-frame or over a scan, or a list reading's candidate provider need over the step's limit | stricter admission rule (existing code and values) | SBUD-1 | execution-kernel | `since` 0.12.57; the need of `selection::candidate_provider_need_ms`, the run's own; a need at the limit is admitted |
| SB1-2 | the same refusal for a list reading's page recognition over its scan's `max_ms`, in a pack with target consensus | stricter admission rule (existing code and values) | SBUD-1 | execution-kernel | `since` 0.12.57; compared before SB1-1 |
| SB1-3 | the run's provider check of a candidate projection | behaviour unchanged, its rule shared | SBUD-1 | — | the same layouts, need, refusal and point |
| SB1-4 | the sampling budget at admission in four contracts | contract sentences | SBUD-1 | — | the files named above |

Tests (exec gate row "#448 SBUD-1"), in `crates/execution-kernel/src/contained_task/gate_448_sbud1.rs`
over synthetic `neutral` packages: `admission_refuses_integer_layout_over_step_deadline` (a
single-frame select over four slots that each read an integer by OCR, 2 000 ms each, no consensus,
need 8 000 ms: refused with no step timeout, limit 5 000, and with 7 999, each with the need, the
limit and `pick`; admitted with 8 000, and the run's check at the start of a fresh step of 8 000 ms
on the scripted clock lets the projection go on), `admission_refuses_scan_select_over_max_ms` (a
select over a scan of a card list, need 32 000 ms: refused within `max_ms` 31 999, admitted within
32 000 though the step timeout is 10 000), `admission_refuses_list_reading_over_limit` (a list
reading of the same list likewise; with target consensus on its list page, three frames 1 000 ms
apart, its page recognition of 2 000 ms refused within 1 999 and fitting within 2 000, where the
projection's 32 000 is refused), `admission_and_run_time_share_one_need` (the need admission refuses
with is the `required_ms` of the run's `candidate_sample_budget_insufficient` at a fresh step of
5 000 ms, `remaining_ms` 5 000, and the function's answer for the layout); and
`package_cli::gate_448_sbud1::package_check_refuses_integer_layout_over_step_deadline` (actinglab's
bin: `package check` of the integer package as an assembled ZIP answers `package_invalid`, exit 2,
`details.code` `recognition_sample_budget_invalid`, the need, the limit and the operation). One
existing fixture newly refused gets the step timeout its need asks for, no assertion changed: the
package of `gate_308_l4b_admission.rs` (10 000 ms to 32 000 ms), whose
`l4b_admission_refuses_on_empty_where_the_step_cannot_end_the_run_normally` admits a single-frame
select over the card list (32 000 ms) without `on_empty`.

### 1.334 Slice NOTICES-1 (0.12.58): the rules of a bundle's notices directory, in the contract crate (Workflow #444; the design note `rd-1113/design-notices-in-archive.md`, read on main `29a65e2d`, adopted as design (a) with every recommended answer of its section 8 by the coordinator's rulings of 11-13 on board #444, not the owner's words, the three slices one after another; coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-444-notices-1.md`, read on main `29a65e2d`)

1.334 is the coordinator's number. [package-reference.md](package-reference.md), "Notices" (in
"Standard package root"), is the contract. One module of the contract crate, seven words of the
vocabulary `standard_pack_problem` and four optional values of `standard_pack_root_invalid` are
added. No outcome code, value key, configuration key, persisted shape, wire shape or record is
added, no program calls the module, and **no program's behaviour changes**. The outcome code index
is regenerated and comes out unchanged: it lists codes, not vocabularies, and the first sentence of
`standard_pack_root_invalid` stays.

**What the directory is for.** A package may come with texts its author must ship with it. A
standard-package bundle zip will carry them in one directory `notices/` at its root, beside
`packs/`, not listed in `bundle.json`; the installer will place it in the game root as it is, as
one item, and no reader of the Runtime opens it. So no pack's `file_count`, `byte_count`, listing or
content hash, no catalog version and no composed generation moves with a text (design §2, §3.4).

**The rules** (`crates/actingcommand-contract/src/standard_pack_notices.rs`, exported as the other
standard-pack readers are; pure functions and constants, no file system, no zip):

- the directory `notices` (`STANDARD_PACK_NOTICES_DIRECTORY`), in exact lower case;
  `notice_relative_path` takes a zip member's or root-relative name apart (`Notices/…` is not of
  it);
- the path rule (`check_notice_path`): at most 2 segments below the directory (`notice_depth`);
  each segment 1 to 64 bytes of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, its first byte a letter or a digit, and a segment
  `safe_source_path` accepts (no trailing dot, no device name) (`notice_name`); a file name with no
  dot, or ending after its last dot in `md`, `txt`, `tsv` or `csv` in any ASCII case (`notice_name`);
- the size rule (`check_notice_size`): a file of 1 to 2,097,152 bytes (`notice_bytes`);
- the set rule (`check_notice_listing`), over a listing of `NoticeEntry {path, bytes}`: at most 64
  files (`notice_count`), each path by the path rule and each size by the size rule, at most
  8,388,608 bytes together (`notice_total_bytes`), no two paths equal under ASCII case folding and no
  file whose path, in any ASCII case, is another path's directory (`notice_name`); judged in the
  byte order of the paths, so a zip's member order and a directory walk's give the same answer;
- the pack rule (`check_notice_pack_ids`): a bundle that carries the directory lists no pack whose
  `package_id` is `notices` in any ASCII case (`notice_name`); `reserved_package_id` is unchanged
  (design Q4), since reserving the name would narrow what a reader of `package` revisions 3 to 9
  accepts;
- the text rule (`check_notice_text`): strict UTF-8, none of U+0000 to U+0008, U+000B, U+000E to
  U+001F and U+007F (`notice_not_text`); TAB, LF, FF, CR and any line ending allowed; the bytes
  judged, never changed;
- the bounds as constants (`MAX_NOTICE_DEPTH`, `MAX_NOTICE_SEGMENT_BYTES`, `NOTICE_FILE_SUFFIXES`,
  `MAX_NOTICE_FILES`, `MAX_NOTICE_FILE_BYTES`, `MAX_NOTICE_TOTAL_BYTES`): format bounds a writer and
  every reader share, as `MAX_BUNDLE_TABLES` is, not configuration keys (design Q5).

**The answer.** Each rule answers the first thing it finds broken as
`NoticeIssue {problem, subject, bound}`: `problem` the `notice_*` word; `subject` the directory as a
whole (`Directory`, for the count and the total), a path below it (`Path`), or a pack (`Package`,
its id); `bound` `Count {limit, found}` or `Bytes {limit, found}`, the bound broken (the least or
the most) and the value found, which `standard_pack_root_invalid` carries as `limit_count` and
`count` or `limit_bytes` and `actual_bytes`. `NoticeIssue::member` names the path relative to the
root that holds the directory (`notices/<path>`, `notices`, or `bundle.json` for a pack, whose id
`NoticeIssue::package_id` gives). The shape serves the three later callers without one of them
restating a rule: each lists the files it found (a zip's member table with its declared sizes for
`place`; a directory on disk for `package bundle --notices`; a placed game root for `standard-pack
check` and `place`'s `post_check`), reads each file through the size and text rules, and prefixes
its own root (`<zip>\`, the game root) to `member()` to name the member in its outcome, with
`json_pointer` empty. One issue, the first, as the root-file checks answer: a bundle is refused
for one cause.

**Two cases the work order asked to decide.** `a.tar.md` is accepted: a file name's suffix is what
follows its last dot, `md` (and `a.md.html`, of the suffix `html`, is refused). A trailing dot
(`NOTICE.`, `NOTICE.md.`) is refused, by `safe_source_path` (and its suffix would be empty). A
byte-order mark at the start is accepted, and a U+FEFF after it is an ordinary character: the text
rule's refused set is closed and does not hold it.

**Why one place.** Three programs will judge the directory in three forms: the installer in a zip
before it places it, `package bundle` in a source directory before it lays it, `standard-pack
check` in a placed root. A rule each states itself drifts, and one root accepted by one tool and
refused by another is what the shared root-file checks exist to prevent ("One check, three readers"
in [package-reference.md](package-reference.md)).

**The three slices**, one after another (the coordinator's order of 11-13):

| Slice | What it turns on |
|---|---|
| NOTICES-1 (this) | the rules, the seven words, the optional values, the contract text; nothing reads the directory |
| NOTICES-2 | the installer's `place` (crate `lab-rescue`): the `package` edge checked before the layout, the directory as one item of kind `notices` placed first and set aside when a later bundle carries none, `notice_undeclared`, reads through each file's bound; the raise of `package` to revision 10, the Runtime declaring [3, 10] |
| NOTICES-3 | `package bundle --notices`, `standard-pack check` (the directory checked and counted when the root holds one) and `resource verify`'s bundle step |

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md), "Bump rule"): no
program writes or reads anything new. The seven words and the four optional values are added
within `runtime-outcomes` 1, values a reader only spells, as `argument_problem`'s `not_absolute`
(L5G2b-10) and the optional `count` of S168C-3 were; `standard_pack_root_invalid` is `review:
pending`, so it may gain optional values (the outcome-code writing spec v2.2, §11; §2 rule 5 forbids
only a required key on a settled entry). `package` stays at 9: NOTICES-2 raises it with its first
reader. `BundleIndex`, `reserved_package_id`, `actingd-config`, `ledger`, `runtime-client`,
`install-*`, `player-hold` and `tools-layout`: untouched.

**At deploy.** Nothing changes: no program calls the module. **Rollback:** nothing to undo.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NT1-1 | the module `standard_pack_notices`: the directory's name, the bounds, the path, size, set, pack and text rules, `NoticeIssue`, `NoticeSubject`, `NoticeBound`, `NoticeEntry` | contract rules (no shape) | NOTICES-1 | — | first callers NOTICES-2 and NOTICES-3; no file system, no zip |
| NT1-2 | `standard_pack_problem` + `notice_count`, `notice_bytes`, `notice_total_bytes`, `notice_depth`, `notice_name`, `notice_not_text`, `notice_undeclared` | outcome vocabulary | NOTICES-1 | NOTICES-2, NOTICES-3 | in `StandardPackProblem` and the catalog's vocabulary; `notice_undeclared` (a bundle that carries the directory and declares a `package` maximum below 10) is registered now so that the vocabulary moves once, NOTICES-2 its first user |
| NT1-3 | `standard_pack_root_invalid` + optional `limit_count`, `count`, `limit_bytes`, `actual_bytes` (existing keys) | optional values of a pending entry (no shape) | NOTICES-1 | NOTICES-2, NOTICES-3 | its description names the notices refusal's `path`, `json_pointer`, `package_id` and bound |
| NT1-4 | [package-reference.md](package-reference.md), "Notices" | contract text | NOTICES-1 | — | the layout lines of `package bundle` and of the standard package root, the `package` row of [component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md), [install-cli.md](install-cli.md), `lab-operations.json` and [resource-verify.md](resource-verify.md) come with NOTICES-2 and NOTICES-3 |

Tests (contract gate row "#444 NOTICES-1", the module's own tests, placeholder names, a notice file
`NOTICE.md`): `standard_pack_notices::tests::notices_path_rule_holds_each_bound_at_its_edge`
(`notices/` in exact lower case; depth 2 kept and 3 refused with the bound; segments of 64 bytes
kept and 65 refused, a file name and a directory's name, and an empty segment, with the bound
broken; a first byte that is a dot, a dash or an underscore; a byte outside the alphabet; a device
name in any case and a trailing dot; every accepted suffix in lower and upper case and none; other
suffixes refused; `a.tar.md` kept and `a.md.html` refused; a dot in a directory's name),
`notices_set_rule_holds_each_bound_at_its_edge` (64 files kept and 65 refused; a file of 0 bytes,
1 byte, the bound and the bound plus one, through the listing and the size rule; the total at the
bound and one byte past it; two paths equal under ASCII case folding and a file and a directory of
one name, in any case, each refused at its path; the first path in byte order decides whatever the
listing's order), `notices_pack_rule_refuses_a_pack_named_like_the_directory_only_beside_it`
(`notices`, `Notices` and `NOTICES` refused beside the directory and free without it; other ids
free) and `notices_text_rule_accepts_text_and_refuses_the_control_characters` (ASCII, UTF-8 with
and without a byte-order mark and one after the start, CRLF, CR and mixed line ends, TAB and FF
kept; each of the 29 refused characters refused at the start, the middle and the end, every other
ASCII byte kept there; six invalid UTF-8 sequences refused). No existing test changes.

### 1.335 Slice NOTICES-2 (0.12.58): the installer's `place` takes a bundle's notices directory; `package` revision 10 (Workflow #444; the design note `rd-1113/design-notices-in-archive.md`, read on main `29a65e2d`, design (a) with every recommended answer of its section 8 adopted by the coordinator's rulings of 11-13 on board #444, not the owner's words; coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-444-notices-2.md`, read on main `734dd786`)

1.335 is the coordinator's number. [install-cli.md](install-cli.md), "The Lab's rescue module"
(`place`) and "Interface checks" (`pack place`), [package-reference.md](package-reference.md),
"Notices" and "Standard package root", and the `package` row 10 of
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) are the contract. Added: one value of the
`pack_item` intent's `kind` (`notices`), one rule of the notices set rule, and the `package` raise.
No outcome code, value key, vocabulary word, configuration key, step kind, intent member, wire
shape or record is added. **A bundle without the directory on a root without it plans, journals
and places exactly as before.**

**What `place` does with the directory** (crate `lab-rescue`, `src/install/place.rs`; design
§3.2, §3.3, §3.6):

- **The edge first.** The `package` edge (the maximum the bundle's `interfaces.json` declares lies
  in this installer's `package` range) is checked right after `bundle.json` and before the layout,
  so that a bundle of a later revision is refused through `package` and not through a member this
  installer does not know. The one refusal that changes: a bundle that fails both the edge and the
  layout is refused `interface_edge` where it was `pack_invalid` (design Q2, accepted; no released
  bundle is in that class). Every other refusal and its order are as before.
- **The layout** takes the members `notices/<path>` (exact lower case: a member `Notices/…` stays
  unknown, `pack_invalid` naming it). When the zip carries one or more, in this order: a declared
  `package` maximum below 10 is `notice_undeclared`; the listing (each file's path below the
  directory with the size the zip declares) goes through `check_notice_listing`; the bundle's
  listed packs through `check_notice_pack_ids`; each file is read through 2,097,153 bytes (its
  bound plus one) and what was read goes through `check_notice_size` and `check_notice_text`, so a
  member that holds more than the zip declares is still refused at its bound. All of it in the
  plan, before the hold and before any write, as a root file's problem is refused: `pack_invalid`
  (`path` the zip) caused by `standard_pack_root_invalid` with `game`, `standard_pack_problem` the
  rule's word, `path` the member below the zip (`<zip>\notices\…`; `<zip>\notices` for the count
  or the total; `<zip>\bundle.json` with `package_id` for a pack named like the directory;
  `<zip>\interfaces.json` for `notice_undeclared`), `json_pointer` empty, and the bound with the
  value found on `limit_count` / `count` or `limit_bytes` / `actual_bytes`. The rules are the
  contract crate's (§1.334); `place` states none of them.
- **The item.** One folder item of kind `notices` (`ItemKind::Notices`), `item` `notices`, `dst`
  `<game root>\notices`, its members `<path>` → `notices/<path>`, digested as a pack's folder is
  (the listing digest of each file's SHA-256), and **placed first** among the items, before the
  tables, the packs and the root files, so the texts are in place before the material they
  accompany. States `new`, `replace`, `unchanged`, and `retire` when the game root holds
  `notices\` and the zip carries none (design Q3): set aside as `notices.old-<ms>` and kept, as a
  reader's root file is; not when a pack of the bundle is named `notices` in any ASCII case (that
  folder is the pack's, and two items would share one place). Its step is one more `pack_item`,
  its part `notices.new-<ms>.part` in the game root, where the leftover check already looks; no
  new step kind and no new intent member. The item's files are read through their bound also
  when it is digested and when its part is written.
- **`post_check`** covers the item through its rerun (its listing digest, or its absence after
  `retire`). This release's `standard-pack check` ignores the directory (NOTICES-3 teaches it); a
  change of the notices alone leaves `schedule_changes` false, so the composition row expects the
  catalog unchanged. **`undo`** reverses the item by kind and digest: the placed directory set
  aside as `notices.rolledback-<ms2>` and the kept one renamed back; a retired one renamed back.
  Nothing is deleted.
- **Fixed point 4.** A zip without `notices/` on a root without it gets no item: the same canonical
  plan document and plan id, the same steps and the same journal.

**The added set rule** (`crates/actingcommand-contract/src/standard_pack_notices.rs`,
`check_notice_listing`, after its two collisions; the coordinator found it reading NOTICES-1):
two paths whose directories' names are equal under ASCII case folding and not byte for byte
(`A/x.md` beside `a/y.md`) are refused `notice_name` at the later path in byte order. Their whole
paths differ, so the two earlier collisions passed them; on a file system that folds case they land
in one directory, and the placed directory no longer lists as the zip does (the item's digest after
the swap would not match). One directory spelled alike by several paths is kept; a file `A` beside
a directory `a/…` stays the earlier rule's. The catalog's description of `notice_name` and the
"uniqueness" row of package-reference.md say so; the vocabulary does not move.

**The raise.** `package` [3, 9] → [3, 10]: `distribution/windows/component-interfaces.json`, the
architecture pin (`tools/actinglab-architecture/tests/component_interfaces.rs`) and the row 10 of
component-interfaces.md, which says that once an installation's register records a root's declared
range, a rollback below 10 is refused by the `package` edge for a root placed from a notices bundle,
and that placing a bundle without the directory first is the way (design Q6). A bundle declares
[10, 10] only when it carries the directory; a bundle without it keeps its revision, so its zip,
`SHA256SUMS`, plan and journal stay what they are. The packer writes the revision (the resource
repositories' script and `resource verify`'s mirror, NOTICES-3 and later); `package bundle` writes
no `interfaces.json`. **Every reader of the `package` range, checked before the raise:** the
update's and the rollback's `package` edge (`plan.rs`, `interface_edges`: each registered bundle's
maximum in R\*'s range) compares the register's range, which is unknown for every root
(`adopt.rs`, `package_range: None`), so it is the warning `pack_declaration_unknown` for [3, 9] →
[3, 10] and for [3, 10] → [3, 9] alike, and a register holding [3, 3] would pass both; `undo` of an
update judges the same edges (`rollback_edges`); the update's other edges do not read `package`;
`place` reads I's range, which now takes [3, 3] to [10, 10]; the Runtime reads no `interfaces.json`
and no range (its root reader, the composer, check-config); `resource verify` writes [3, 3] and
compares it with nothing of the Runtime's; `standard-pack check` reads no range; the exact-SHA build
checks the declaration's form only, and the release reader that both halves declare alike. None of
them refuses a bundle or a root that is accepted today.

**What programs of an earlier release do** (design §3.2):

| Program | A zip that carries `notices/` | A game root that holds `notices/` |
|---|---|---|
| rescue `place` before 0.12.58 | `pack_invalid` naming the first `notices/` member in name order (its layout check, which runs before its `package` edge), before the hold: nothing paused, nothing written | a bundle without the directory is placed and `notices\` is left as it is; a notices bundle is refused as on the left |
| the coordinator's placement kit, until it learns the directory (design §5) | refused at its layout check, and its release facts check refuses `package` 10 | lists `notices` as an unlisted directory; nothing refused |
| `standard-pack check` | reads no zip | ignores the directory; the root checks as before |

`actingctl install` has no pack placement of its own (`actingctl install pack plan|place`, INST-4,
is not built; the word `pack` is `actingctl_usage_invalid`, `unknown`), so it never opens such a
zip.

**At deploy.** The Runtime declares `package` [3, 10]; nothing changes for a bundle without the
directory. A bundle that carries it is placed only by this release's `place`. The coordinator's
placement kit and the resource repository's packer do not know the directory yet, so no bundle
that carries it is released before they are changed (design §4, §5; slices 4 and 5). **Rollback**
to a build before 0.12.58: the update's `package` edge stays the warning
`pack_declaration_unknown`, and the earlier Runtime reads a root that holds `notices\` as one
without it; an earlier installer cannot undo a `pack_place` that placed or retired the directory.

### 1.336 Slice NOTICES-3 (0.12.58): the Tools lay and check a bundle's notices directory (`package bundle --notices`, `standard-pack check`, `resource verify`) (Workflow #444; the design note `rd-1113/design-notices-in-archive.md`, read on main `29a65e2d`, design (a) with every recommended answer of its section 8 adopted by the coordinator's rulings of 11-13 on board #444, not the owner's words; coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-444-notices-3.md`, read on the head `6df7d87d` of NOTICES-2's branch)

1.336 is the coordinator's number. [package-reference.md](package-reference.md), "Notices" (the
readers), the layout of `package bundle` and the answer of `standard-pack check`,
[resource-verify.md](resource-verify.md) (the `bundle` step, its index checks and its counts) and
the rows `package bundle` and `standard-pack check` of `lab-operations.json` are the contract. Added:
one flag (`package bundle --notices <directory>`), one member of `standard-pack check`'s answer
(`notices`), one parameter of the operation table's row `package bundle`, and one public constant of
the contract crate. No outcome code, value key, vocabulary word, configuration key, interface
revision, persisted shape, wire shape or record is added. After this slice nothing of the design's
Runtime side is left: the coordinator's placement kit and the resource repositories' packer (the
design's slices 4 and 5) are what remains.

**The rules are the contract crate's** (§1.334): the Tools call `check_notice_listing`,
`check_notice_pack_ids`, `check_notice_size` and `check_notice_text` as `place` does (§1.335) and
state none of them. One module of the Tools crate, `crates/resource-tooling/src/notices_directory.rs`,
reads a directory on disk for both commands: it lists every file below it with its `/`-separated
path and its length on disk; a link below it (a symbolic link, a junction or any other reparse
point), or an entry that is neither a file nor a directory, is refused as the pack loader refuses
one in a pack directory (`package_invalid`, the loader's `content_directory_link_or_type`, naming
the entry; a link at the directory itself is followed, as the loader resolves a locator). Then the
listing goes through the set rule, the bundle's packs through the pack rule, and each file, read
through its bound plus one byte (2,097,153), through the size and text rules. A broken rule is
answered as a root file's problem is (`standard_pack_check::root_invalid`):
`standard_pack_root_invalid` itself, with `game`, `standard_pack_problem` the rule's word, `path` the
file on disk (the directory itself for the count and the total), `json_pointer` empty, and the bound
with the value found on `limit_count` / `count` or `limit_bytes` / `actual_bytes`.

**`package bundle --notices <directory>`** (`crates/resource-tooling/src/package_directory.rs`; the
request's `StandardPackRootFiles.notices`; the CLI's read list `package_build::BUNDLE_READS`):

- Before anything is created, after the root files and the loading copies are checked: a path that
  names no directory, and a directory that holds no file, are refused as a `--loading` that names no
  file is (`validation_failed`, naming the path); then the directory is held to the rules, its pack
  rule over the `package_id`s the packs' `control.json` declare (`package_loading::named_packs`, the
  reading `stale_copies` uses before anything is written). A pack named like the directory, in any
  ASCII case, is `notice_name` with its `package_id`, `path` the pack's source directory (the
  bundle's `bundle.json` is not written yet). A refusal leaves neither `--out` nor `<out>.part`.
- Then, after the other root files and `loading/`, every file is laid byte for byte into
  `<out>/notices/<path>`: no line end, byte-order mark or case of a name is changed. `bundle.json`
  lists nothing of it and no `interfaces.json` is written.
- Without the flag the output is byte for byte what it was: the module is not called.

**`standard-pack check --root <game root>`** (`crates/resource-tooling/src/standard_pack_check.rs`):
right after the root files and the registry are read, and before the loading copies and the
cross-check, a directory `notices` in the game root is held to the same rules, unless the root's
`bundle.json` lists a package named `notices` in any ASCII case (such a folder is that pack's, as
`place` treats it, and is admitted as the pack it is). A broken rule fails the check with `path` the
file below the game root. The answer gains `notices` `{files, bytes}` (the count of the files and
the sum of their lengths; an empty directory counts `{0, 0}`) when it checked a directory, and has no
such member otherwise; `notices` never joins `root_files`, and no name of a file and nothing of a text
is echoed. A root without the directory answers byte for byte what it answered. Entries beside it
that `place` leaves (`notices.old-<ms>`, `notices.rolledback-<ms>`, `notices.new-<ms>.part`) are not
looked at. `place`'s `post_check` runs this check on the placed root, so from this release it checks
a placed directory by the rules (§1.335 said the check ignored it).

**`resource verify`, the `bundle` step** (`apps/actinglab/src/resource_verify/bundle.rs`): when the
repository root holds a directory `notices` (found as the root files are, by `symlink_metadata`), the
step passes it to `package bundle` as `--notices`, so it is laid by the code above; expects `notices`
among the bundle root's entries (`root_file_differs` otherwise); writes `interfaces.json` declaring
`package` [10, 10] and counts `package_revision` 10; zips the directory with the rest; lays its files
into `installed/<game>/notices/`; and requires `standard-pack check` of that copy to answer `notices`
with the count and the bytes of the zip's `notices/` entries (`root_files_unread` otherwise). Without
the directory every byte it writes is what it wrote: [3, 3], `package_revision` 3, no `notices/`
entry, and the check's member absent on both sides.

**The constant.** `NOTICES_PACKAGE_REVISION` (10), which NOTICES-2 left private in
`crates/lab-rescue/src/install/place.rs`, is now the contract crate's public constant
(`standard_pack_notices.rs`); `place` (`notice_undeclared`) and `resource verify` (the revision it
declares) read it from there. That is this slice's one change in `crates/lab-rescue`; no rule of the
module changes.

**Both entries** (board #434: what the Lab does is reachable through the CLI and through the MCP
server alike). The row `package bundle` gains `{"name": "notices", "form": "option", "type": "dir",
"required": false}`; the row `standard-pack check`'s `output` names the notices directory's count and
bytes. The CLI reads `--notices` from its read list; the MCP server's tool is generated from the row
(one input property per parameter) and its call goes to a `serve` child, which writes the row's
options as flags (`engine::arguments`), so `notices` reaches `--notices` with no change to the MCP
server. The pin `gate_434_lab5b3::lenient_rows_match_their_reads` holds the row and the read list
equal in both directions with the new parameter.

**Interfaces.** None raised. `package` stays [3, 10] (NOTICES-2): the Tools' packer mirror writes 10
only for a bundle that carries the directory. `standard-pack check`'s answer gains an optional member
only for a root that holds the directory (`place`'s `post_check` reads the check's exit code alone).

**At deploy.** The Tools gain `package bundle --notices` and the `notices` member of `standard-pack
check`; nothing changes for a root or a repository without the directory. No bundle that carries it
is released before the coordinator's placement kit and the resource repositories' packer are changed
(design §4, §5; slices 4 and 5). **Rollback** to Tools before 0.12.58: `package bundle` refuses the
unknown flag, and `standard-pack check` ignores a placed directory again.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NT3-1 | `package bundle --notices <directory>`; `StandardPackRootFiles.notices` | Tools flag, request member | NOTICES-3 | — | checked before anything is written; laid byte for byte into `notices/`; no `interfaces.json` |
| NT3-2 | `standard-pack check`'s answer + optional `notices` `{files, bytes}` (`StandardPackNotices`) | Tools answer member | NOTICES-3 | — | absent without the directory and beside a pack named like it; never in `root_files` |
| NT3-3 | `resource verify` `bundle` step: `--notices`, `package` [10, 10], the installed `notices/`, the check's member | Tools behaviour | NOTICES-3 | — | without the directory every byte as before |
| NT3-4 | `NOTICES_PACKAGE_REVISION` in `actingcommand_contract` | contract constant (no shape) | NOTICES-3 | — | read by `place` and `resource verify` |
| NT3-5 | `lab-operations.json`: `package bundle` + `notices`; `standard-pack check`'s `output` | operation table | NOTICES-3 | — | CLI and MCP serve the row as it is |

Tests (exec gate row "#444 NOTICES-3", placeholder names, a notice file `NOTICE.md`):

`notices3_package_bundle_lays_the_directory_byte_for_byte` (three files, one with a byte-order mark

`apps/actinglab/src/tests/gate_rv1.rs`: `notices3_the_bundle_step_carries_a_notices_directory` (a

### 1.337 Slice RG-STOP (0.12.58): a planned stop is not a failure of the run-recovery grouping (Workflow #429; a real run of 11-13 stopped on request; the coordinator's ruling of 11-13 on board #429, not the owner's words; coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-429-rg-stop.md`, read on main `ea8ef8ea`)

1.337 is the coordinator's number; another slice of this release appends 1.336.
[global-ledger-query.md](global-ledger-query.md), the paragraph on `run_recovery`, is the
contract. No persisted shape, wire shape, page or group shape, outcome code, category, vocabulary
word, configuration key or interface revision changes, and no outcome code fragment, so the index
is not regenerated.

**What was seen.** A scheduled run was stopped on request (`StopInstanceRun`). In the ledger view
of that run, the run-recovery group listed the stop's own records as failures without a recovery:
three positions, each "failed, no recovery seen", with the gap `missing_relation` and the state
`unknown`. A stop on request is neither a success nor a failure of the run
([policy-suspension.md](policy-suspension.md), "A stopped run"), and the routine summary counts
such a run as an interruption, not a failure.

**The cause.** `run_recovery` (`crates/ledger/src/global/projection/views.rs`) took as a failure
every record of the run's context of severity `warning` or above, or of a failure kind
(`failure_kind`). A stopped scheduled run writes, linked to the run: the Runtime's reset of the
device (`input.intent` and `input.committed` of `input.reset`), its terminal `task.failed` with
`contained_task_cancelled`, the policy driver's `runtime.failed` with the same code
(`record_scheduled_policy_failure`) and its settlement, `policy.execution_recorded` of the kind
`stopped`, with the same code. The code's category is `error` and a record's severity is its
outcome's category, so the last three are errors; none of them has a recovery relation. Those are
the three positions.

**The rule.** In the grouping, a record whose outcome code is of the ladder class `planned_stop` is
no failure unless a failure kind knows it: it is not listed and causes no gap. The class is the one
the outcome catalog this build embeds gives the record's code (`planned_stop` and `ladder_class` in
`views.rs`, over `outcome::catalog_json` and `parse_ladder_class`), read as the recovery ladder's
trigger matching reads it (`ladder_class_of`); a code the catalog does not list has no class. The
rule names no code: today the class holds eighteen codes (the release notes of 0.12.58 list
them), among them `contained_task_cancelled` and `contained_task_paused` (a pause's drain, a
player hold's drain); this entry first named these two as if they were the whole class.

**What stays.** A record a failure kind knows (`input.failed`, `recognition.failed`, a failed entry
recovery) is a failure whatever its code; any other record of severity `warning` or above stays a
failure. A run whose context then holds no failure, read completely and within the context bound,
has no group, as a run without failures had none; a context cut by the bound or the read's budget,
or an incomplete source, still has its group with its gap. A stop whose reset failed keeps the
reset's `input.failed` and the fence's records, of their own codes, in the group, and a cleanup
refusal recorded beside a stop keeps its own code: those are failures a person must see. The
records' severity, the codes' categories, `failure_kind`, `success_kind`, the page's rows, their
views, the cursor, the read scope and the shapes of the page and of the group do not change.

**The paths.** `run_recovery` has one caller, `project_selected`, the one projection of a view
page, which every reader of a page goes through: the in-memory indexes
(`EventIndexes::project_view_page`: the Segment store, and an offline snapshot without an SQLite
root through `GlobalLedgerMetadata::project_view_page`), the SQLite store's view reader
(`ViewReader::read_view_page`: the Runtime's writer and its reader pool) and the bounded offline
snapshot on an SQLite root (`sqlite/offline.rs`, the same view reader). The host's `QueryEvents`
(`read_events.rs`), `ledger-forensics`' `query_view_page` and the clients that show the groups read
those pages. No other code derives a group or repeats the rule: `lab-ops`' diagnose groups errors by
code, which is not this grouping, and the run listing, the run status and diagnose ask for their
pages without run recovery (#422 QR-2, QR-2b).

**At deploy.** A run that was stopped or paused no longer shows a run-recovery group for the stop's
own records; a run with other failures shows them as before, without the stop's records. Nothing
else of a page changes. Nothing is persisted: a rollback brings the earlier grouping back.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RGS-1 | `run_recovery`: a record whose outcome code is of the ladder class `planned_stop` is no failure of the grouping unless a failure kind knows it | read rule (no shape change) | RG-STOP | — | `since` 0.12.58; groups only; the class read from the embedded catalog |
| RGS-2 | [global-ledger-query.md](global-ledger-query.md), the paragraph on `run_recovery` | contract text | RG-STOP | — | what a failure of the grouping is, a run without one has no group, and the rule |

Tests (ledger gate row "#429 RG-STOP"), in `crates/ledger/src/global/tests/gate_429_rg_stop.rs` on
a formal root, each page of the run checked against the in-memory indexes' page of the same records
at the same snapshot (the same groups): `rg_stop_t1_a_run_that_was_only_stopped_has_no_group` (the
stop's records above: no group; its three records stay errors, rows of the page in the Errors view),
`rg_stop_t2_a_recovered_input_failure_then_a_stop_is_recovered_by_the_failure_alone` (an
`input.failed` and the `input.completed` of the same action, then the stop: one group, `recovered`,

`rg_stop_t3_a_warning_then_a_stop_keeps_the_warnings_group` (a `runtime.failed` of a warning code
without a recovery relation, then the stop: the group the warning had before the stop, its evidence
the warning alone, `missing_relation`, `unknown`),
`rg_stop_t4_a_run_failed_with_another_class_keeps_its_group` (a terminal and a `runtime.failed` of
`contained_task_deadline_exceeded`, class `budget_or_permission`: both listed, neither recovered,

code: `store_contract`'s query test pins a run's `command.rejected` error without an outcome code,
