### 1.338 Slice LOAD-P (0.12.59): the installer's `place` takes the loading templates directory (Workflow #451; a latent gap, no released bundle carries the directory; the coordinator's rulings of 11-13 on board #451, not the owner's words; coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-451-loadp.md`, read on main `a83e482b`)

1.338 is the coordinator's number. [install-cli.md](install-cli.md), "The Lab's rescue module"
(`place`), [package-reference.md](package-reference.md), "Standard package root" (`loading.json`),
and the notes of the row `place` of `lab-operations.json` are the contract. Added: one value of
the `pack_item` intent's and the plan document's `kind` (`loading`) and one word of the vocabulary
`standard_pack_problem` (`loading_pack_name`, with its catalog entry; the outcome code index was
regenerated and holds codes only, so it does not change). No outcome code, value key,
configuration key, step kind, intent member, interface revision, wire shape or record is added.
**A bundle without the directory on a root without it plans, journals and places exactly as
before.**

**What was latent.** `package bundle --loading` lays the root file `loading.json` and, beside it,
the directory `loading/` with the templates the file declares
(`crates/resource-tooling/src/package_directory.rs`; [package-reference.md](package-reference.md),
"Loading pages"), and `resource verify` zips both. `place` knew `loading.json` as a root file but
no member `loading/…`: its layout check refused such a zip `pack_invalid` naming the first
`loading/` member, so the bundle of a resource repository that starts carrying loading templates
could not be placed. No released bundle carries the directory, so nothing has failed yet.

**What `place` does with the directory** (crate `lab-rescue`, `src/install/place.rs`, `plan` and
`check_loading`):

- **The layout** takes the members `loading/<path>` (exact lower case: a member `Loading/…` stays
  unknown, `pack_invalid` naming it) and holds them, right after the notices directory's rules and
  before the root files are read, to the zip's own `loading.json`, read with the contract crate's
  `parse_standard_pack_loading` for the bundle's game. A declared template is a target's
  `template`, `loading/<file>.png`, relative to the directory of the file that declares it, which
  in the zip is the zip's root: the member of a template is the template path itself. In this
  order, all in the plan, before the hold and before any write:
  - a zip that carries no `loading.json`: its first `loading/` member in name order is refused
    `pack_invalid` naming it (`<zip>\loading/<path>`), as a member no layout knows is named;
  - the file itself refused by the reader: `pack_invalid` caused by `standard_pack_root_invalid`
    with its first issue (`path` `<zip>\loading.json`, the issue's word and pointer), as a root
    file's problem is refused (`package bundle --loading` checks the file first, so a zip it wrote
    never has one);
  - a `loading/` member that is not a declared template, a deeper path among them (a template
    path never holds a second `/`): `pack_invalid` naming the first such member, as above;
  - a template the file declares and the zip lacks: `pack_invalid` caused by
    `standard_pack_root_invalid` with `game`, `standard_pack_problem` `loading_template_invalid`
    (the word `standard-pack check` answers for a template that is missing or unreadable), the
    pointer that check gives, that of the first target in the file's order that reads the template
    (`/<family>/<index>/template`), and `path` the missing member below the zip
    (`<zip>\loading\<file>.png`, where the check names `loading.json`). A valid file declares one
    template at least (every page's `required` holds a template target), so a zip that carries
    `loading.json` without the directory is refused here; `package bundle` never writes one;
  - a bundle that carries the directory and lists a pack named `loading` in any ASCII case:
    `pack_invalid` caused by `standard_pack_root_invalid` `loading_pack_name`, `path`
    `<zip>\bundle.json`, `json_pointer` empty, `package_id` the pack's. No existing word said it
    (`notice_name` is the notices directory's), so the word is added. Placed, the two would share
    `<game root>\loading`; the contract already told a repository not to name a pack so.

  `place` reads the declaration and the names only: what a template shows (a PNG of more than one
  colour) stays `standard-pack check`'s, which `post_check` runs on the placed game root. The
  refusal of a root file's problem is now built by one helper, `root_refusal`, for the root files
  and `loading.json` alike; the outcome it builds for the root files is the one built before.
- **The bound.** The contract crate states no bound for a template file
  (`standard_pack_loading.rs` bounds a template's stem, 64 bytes, not its size), so a template is
  read as a pack's file is, whole (`Archive::read_of`), when it is digested and when its part is
  written.
- **The item.** One folder item of kind `loading` (`ItemKind::Loading`), `item` `loading`, `dst`
  `<game root>\loading`, its members `<file>` → `loading/<file>`, digested as a pack's folder is
  (the listing digest of each file's SHA-256), placed **after the packs and before the root
  files**, so the templates are in place before the `loading.json` that declares them. States
  `new`, `replace`, `unchanged`, and `retire` when the game root holds `loading\` and the zip
  carries none: set aside as `loading.old-<ms>` and kept, as `loading.json` itself is set aside when
  a zip no longer carries it (the directory's `retire` comes before the file's); not when a pack of
  the bundle is named `loading` in any ASCII case (that folder is the pack's). Its step is one more
  `pack_item`, its part `loading.new-<ms>.part` in the game root, where the leftover check already
  looks; no new step kind and no new intent member.
- **`post_check`** covers the item through its rerun (its listing digest, or its absence after
  `retire`); `standard-pack check` reads the placed `loading.json` with its templates as it has
  since LOAD-1. **`undo`** reverses the item by kind and digest: the placed directory set aside as
  `loading.rolledback-<ms2>` and the kept one renamed back; a retired one renamed back. Nothing is
  deleted.
- **A bundle without the directory** and without `loading.json` on a root without the directory
  reads neither and gets no item: the same canonical plan document and plan id, the same steps and
  the same journal.

**No revision moves.** The bundle format has carried the directory since LOAD-1 (0.12.37); this
slice lets the installer place what the builder already writes. `package` stays [3, 10];
`reserved_package_id` and `BundleIndex` are unchanged, so a reader of any `package` revision
accepts the bundles it accepted; the notices rules and their constants do not move.

**What programs of an earlier release do:**

| Program | A zip that carries `loading/` | A game root that holds `loading/` |
|---|---|---|
| rescue `place` before 0.12.59 | `pack_invalid` naming the first `loading/` member in name order (its layout check, after its `package` edge), before the hold: nothing paused, nothing written | a bundle without the directory is placed and `loading\` is left as it is (its `loading.json` set aside) |
| an earlier installer's `undo` of a `pack_place` journal with a `loading` item | — | cannot read the kind ([install-cli.md](install-cli.md), "Journals across versions"); undo with this build first |
| `standard-pack check` | reads no zip | reads `loading/` beside `loading.json`, as since LOAD-1 |
| the Runtime (actingd), check-config, the composer | read no zip | never read it |

`actingctl install` has no pack placement of its own (`actingctl install pack plan|place`, INST-4,
is not built), so it never opens such a zip.

**At deploy.** Nothing changes for a bundle without the directory. A bundle that carries it is
placed only by this release's `place`; an installer of an earlier release refuses it at its layout
check, naming the member, before anything is paused or written. No interface revision moves.
**Rollback** to a build before 0.12.59: an earlier installer cannot undo a `pack_place` that placed
or retired the directory; the Runtime of any release reads a root that holds `loading\` as before.

### 1.339 Slice PLACE-PKG (0.12.59): the installer's `place` reads a bundle's declaration by the bundle's own rule (Workflow #451; found by reading the code and the declaration a released bundle carries, never met in production; the coordinator's rulings of 11-13 on board #451, not the owner's words; coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-451-place-pkg.md`, read on main `ef94d950`)

1.339 is the coordinator's number; another slice of this release appends 1.338.
[install-cli.md](install-cli.md), "The Lab's rescue module" (`place`), is the contract;
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md), "Declaration" ("Resource bundle") and "Parse
rules", already gives a bundle's shape and makes the six v1 interfaces a Runtime's or UI's rule. No
outcome code, value key, vocabulary word, configuration key, step kind, intent member, wire shape,
record or interface revision is added or moved, and no outcome code fragment changes, so the index
is not regenerated.

**The defect.** `place` (crate `lab-rescue`, `src/install/place.rs`, the `package` edge of the
plan) read the zip's `interfaces.json` with `manifest::parse_declaration`, the reader of a
Runtime's or Tools' declaration, which answers nothing unless all six v1 interfaces are named, and
then refused `interface_edge`. A resource repository's release declares `package` alone:
`resource verify`'s `bundle` step writes `{schema_version actingcommand.component-interfaces.v1,
speaks {package [3, 3]}, validated_with {repository, commit}}`, with `package` [10, 10] when the
bundle carries `notices/` ([resource-verify.md](resource-verify.md), the bullet on the notices
directory and the `bundle` row of the step table; `apps/actinglab/src/resource_verify/bundle.rs`,
whose `Speaks` has that one member). So `place` refused every released bundle. Production never
met it: its bundles are placed by the coordinator's placement kit, and the module's `place` is not
used on the production root before LAB-7.

**Why the tests missed it.** The gates that place a bundle (`gate_434_lab3.rs`,
`gate_444_notices2.rs`) build its declaration from the fixture's `speaks()`, all six v1 interfaces
and `runtime-outcomes`: the shape of a Runtime's declaration, not of a released bundle's.

**The rule.** `manifest::parse_bundle_package` reads a bundle's declaration by the parse rules of
component-interfaces.md that every v1 reader applies: `schema_version` exactly
`actingcommand.component-interfaces.v1`; every value under `speaks`, under any name, an array of
two integers `[min, max]` with `min <= max`, a malformed one making the declaration unreadable (as
a malformed `package` does); and `package` named. Other names are otherwise neither required nor
checked, and other members (`validated_with`) are not read. (The coordinator's ruling on the open
point of this slice, 11-13 on board #451: the work order's sentence that other names under
`speaks` are not checked was wrong where it contradicts the parse rules.) `place` takes the
`package` pair it answers, and the rest of the edge is as before: the declared maximum lies within the running installer's `package` range, else
`interface_edge` with `path` `<zip>\interfaces.json` and `game`; a missing, unreadable or
malformed file, or one the reader refuses, is the same refusal (component-interfaces.md takes a
bundle without the file as [1, 1], which lies below every installer's `package` minimum since
0.12.0, so the answer agrees). The notices check (`notice_undeclared` when a bundle that carries
`notices/` declares a maximum below 10) reads the same pair. `manifest::parse_declaration` keeps
its rule for the Runtime's, the Tools' and the UI's declarations (the installer's own range, a
build's manifests, the release reader). **The other readers, checked:** `place`'s plan is the one
reader of a bundle's `interfaces.json` in the rescue module; `post_check` reruns the items'
digests and `undo` reverses the steps by kind and digest, and neither opens the zip's declaration;
the pack register's `package_range` comes from `state.json` (`null` for every root, `adopt.rs`),
never from a zip; `actingctl install` has no pack placement of its own.

**At deploy.** Nothing changes for production, which does not place with this module before LAB-7
(the coordinator's placement kit places its bundles). This release's `place` takes a released
bundle; an earlier release's refuses it `interface_edge` before anything is paused or written. A
bundle that declares all six interfaces plans as before.

### 1.340 Slice FL-1 (0.12.59): field lists, the declaration, the list builder, the gate and the kernel; `package` revision 11 (Workflow #450; the owner approved the feature on 11-13, board #450; the design note `rd-1113/design-list-from-fields.md`, design (a), read on main `abee78ed`, with the coordinator's decisions of its section 7 and the work order's rulings, not the owner's words; coordinator work order `rd-1113/brief-450-fl1.md`, read on main `98924e28`)

1.340 is the next free section on `98924e28`; the coordinator renumbers it if a slice of the same
release takes it first. The design note's slices FL-0 (the contract text), FL-1a (the declaration
and the pure list builder) and FL-1b (the gate, admission, the collector's bookkeeping, the
end-frame traces, the run kinds, the catalog and the `package` raise) are one pull request, because
FL-1a alone would be code no caller reaches. [resource-readings.md](resource-readings.md), "Lists
from fields", is the contract; [ocr-fields.md](ocr-fields.md), [instance-fact-store.md](instance-fact-store.md),
"List reading facts" and the capacity table, [selection-policy.md](selection-policy.md), "List
readings and field lists", and the `package` row 11 of
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) change the sentences that said a list reading
was the one producer of a record list.

**What it builds.** A task schema `0.8` or `0.9` task that declares `post_admission_ocr`
(`fields_v1`) and `scheduling_outcome` may declare one `field_lists` entry: a group of its fields,
keyed by a dictionary field, its columns other fields of the group, with the list's own confidence
floor, key, lifetime, `start` and `end`. The rule of the declaration is one function of the contract
crate (`validate_field_lists` in `taskflow.rs`, beside `MAX_LIST_READINGS`), shared by the
declaration gate (`Declaration::field_lists` for the structure, `Declaration::field_list_rules` for
the rule, `crates/pack-containment/src/source/declarations.rs`; the parser's cross-reference of the
conditions' targets, `validate_field_list_targets`, `source/mod.rs`) and admission
(`prepare_field_lists`, `crates/execution-kernel/src/contained_task/field_list.rs`, after the
fields are prepared). On each collected frame the fields collector keeps the key's and the
columns' readings with their confidences; the list judges `start` on its first frame and `end` on
each; on its end frame it is built (`field_list_of`) and recorded as a `read_list` step's list is
(`ListReadingFrame` when whole, then `ListReading`); a frame of the group after that fails the run;
at a successful end a list that met no end records `list_end_unseen`. Every repeat fails the list
(the coordinator's decision 2 of section 7: the core never folds, sums or picks one).

**Two facts of the code on `98924e28` the design note did not name, and how they are met without
moving the host.** (1) The host takes `ListReadingMiss` as a two-member value it also builds itself
(`list_bytes_exceeded`), so the frames a field list's miss names ride in memory on the list's
`ListReadingDeclaration` (`frame_indices`, empty for a `read_list` step and a whole list), and
`ListReadingMiss::outcome` adds them as the optional value `frame_indices`. (2) The host binds a
miss to the frame it captured last and stops on a mismatch (`resource_reading_poison`,
`contained_task_resource_reading_frame_mismatch`), and the kernel's success paths do not carry
that frame. For `list_end_unseen` the kernel therefore notes the device capture time of every frame
a run captures (the entry frame, every sample and observation frame, every agreement frame), only
for a task that declares a field list, and binds the miss to the latest. A declared operation's one
step (#412 Lab B-3), a bound recovery entry and `recognize_only` read no list.

**After an independent review (11-13, the coordinator's rulings, in this pull request).**
- *Which frames are list frames.* A list frame is a frame a step's field observation captures; the
  frame the kernel captures again before an input when an action gap is configured
  (`ObservationBeforeInput`, ACT-2) is not one, so the field lists are out of the collector for that
  one capture and back after it, and the fields report takes the frame as before. Before this, every
  item but the last reached the list twice under any gap and the list always failed
  `list_duplicate_key`; now which frames a list is made of does not depend on the gap's
  configuration. This is no fold by key and value: the core still never folds.
- *No new work for a package without the member.* The start of a run's capture record returns at
  once when no list is admitted (no lock), and the fields collector keeps the confidences only while
  the run reads a field list (no insert). What remains on such a package's run path is a test of an
  empty list or of an absent relay at each capture, at each collected frame and at the run's
  successful end: no lock, no allocation, no insert.
- *One frame per item.* The contract ("Lists from fields", "When the list is whole", item 5) warns
  package authors that an observation window, a wait step that holds a field page or a confirmation's
  wait page that is a field page collects one item on several frames inside one step, and that a
  stability termination ends a run only after steps whose frames did not change.
- *The revision a bundle declares.* `resource verify`'s `bundle` step keeps writing [3, 3], or
  [10, 10] for a notices bundle, as it wrote neither 8 nor 9: a bundle whose packs use a field list
  declares `package` [11, 11] itself (the resource repository's packer, FL-3).

|---|---|
| PKG-S2 | `PackageAdmitted.package_sha256` (keep `package_label`, `task_label`); `EntryRecoveryPackageAdmitted/Completed/Failed.package_sha256` → `package_label`; effective configuration `EntryRecovery.package_sha256` → `package_label`; `TaskSelectionPolicy.package_sha256`; Lab declared refusal `declared_package`, `verified_package` → optional `package_label`; Lab evidence `expected_package_sha256` / `actual_package_sha256` → `package_label`; `EvidencePackage.sha256`; OCR comparison report `truth_set_sha256` and its runtime-client reader; run status `package_ref` / `recovery_packages` → `package_label` / `recovery_package_labels`; run summary digest checks; reading facts' `resource_bundle_hash` = SHA-256(`"package:" + package_id`) (shape unchanged). **Done (PKG-S2):** all of them, §1.31 P2-1 to P2-11; also the run summary's `package_digest` (now `package_label`), the in-package `sha256` keys made optional and ignored (D5), and request replay by `package_label` (a recorded label must be the request's package's, or a configured prerequisite package's or the recovery binding's `package_id`, each admitted again) |
| PKG-S3 | `DispatchIntent.package_digest` (payload and storage equality); `ProcedureBinding.package_digest`; `binding_digest` tuple v3 = (`procedure_ref`, `operation_id`, `yield_points`); `PausedOn.package_digest` → content hashes parsed from the failure identity; suspension report members `paused_hash_prefix`, `current_hash_prefix`, `lifts_when: content_hash_changes`, `lifted_by: main_hash \| layer:<n> \| restart`. **Done (PKG-S3):** all of them, §1.47 P3-1 to P3-6; also the run identity check by path (the request's path against the binding's location) and `lifted[].effective` `next_evaluation` in place of `pending_restart` |
| PKG-S4 | IPC `expected_sha256` of `PackageDebugRequest`, `ContainedTaskRecoveryBinding`, `ContainedTaskRequest`, the Lab operation, online observation and saved-artifact OCR requests; `PackageDebugSummary.verified_sha256`; configuration `startup_package.expected_sha256`, `prerequisite_packages[].package_digest`, `policy.procedure_manifest[].package_digest`, the resource declaration's `package_digest`. **Done (PKG-S4):** all of them, §1.55 P4-1 to P4-6; also the actingctl, MCP and actinglab digest flags and arguments, the `takeover` hint's `--package-ref`, the `package validate` / `lab validate` digest outputs, the dry-run record's `package_label` and the identity check of a configured prerequisite package (D7) |
| PKG-S5 | bundle v4 `packs[] {package_id, server, entry_task_id, path = "packs/<package_id>", file_count, byte_count}` (the bundle-level maintenance declaration stays, coordinator 10-12); `RecordingArtifact.digest` / `.sha256` → `package_id`; `PackageRef`, `ContentDirectory` and the `sha256:` serializers. **Done (PKG-S5):** all of them, §1.64 P5-1 to P5-8; also bundle v4's optional `tables` (M-357a TB12) and its reserved `package_id` `tables`, the Lab output named `<package_id>.<ext>` and replaced in place (D9), `actinglab package digest` and the authoring receipt's `package_sha256` |

**Failure identity, format v2** (PKG-S3, M-PKG §3.4):
`<base>~v2~k<K>~m<I><H>[~p<I><H>]…[~r<Kh><I><H>]~f<F>`. `I` = the first 8 hex digits of the
SHA-256 of `package_id`; `H` = the first 12 hex digits of the package's content hash measured at
suspension (`x` when it could not be measured, D18); the `pre:<digest>` scope becomes `pre:<I>`.
A v1 string is not read. The content hash is measured only at suspension and at lift checks
(never on admission) and is stored only inside this string (the failure record's
`failure_identity`, §1.15 Q1) and in SR-3's suspension event key
`actual_digest`. A lift check of one package runs at most once per
`scheduling.suspension.lift_check_min_interval_ms` (§5).

### 1.243 Slice R-0b2 (0.12.36): `activity` on the instance rows of `actingctl overview` and `ac_overview` (R-0b, §1.238, fills `Status.activity`, and `actingctl status` prints it, but the overview's rows are built member by member and did not carry it, so the agents that run the devices could not see what an instance does now; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-r0b2.md`)

[runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) (the `overview` command row, the `ac_overview` tool row
and the output budget's "never cut" list) is the contract. The number 1.243 is the coordinator's;
§1.241 and §1.242 are in flight in the same release. Nothing persisted, no wire shape of the
Runtime, no configuration key, no outcome code and no interface revision changes.

**What.** (1) Each instance row carries the optional member `activity`, `{kind, request_id?,
package_id?, since_unix_ms}`, the `RuntimeInstanceStatus.activity` of the overview's one Status read
as the Runtime answered it, and no member while the instance has none. No Runtime request is added
and nothing is read from the ledger for it. A row has it whichever other reads fail, since the
Status read is the one the overview cannot do without. (2) MCP's output budget never cuts it; the
members cut and their order are unchanged. (3) The tool's description and result schema say so.

**What changes live.** The rows of a busy instance grow by the member (about 150 bytes for a run), so
an overview near the budget starts cutting a little earlier, in the order it already has.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.35). Nothing persisted: the member disappears from the rows.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0B2-1 | `instances[].activity?` | `actingctl overview` / `ac_overview` answer | R-0b2 | R-0b2 | `since` 0.12.36; from the one Status read; never cut |

### 5.1 Capacity of `config.parameters`

`config.parameters` is one runtime fact whose `record_list` holds at most 256 rows (M387 §5.9,
`runtime_fact.rs`). One row per key; list, object and decimal keys are one row each.

| Rows | Count |
|---|---|
| today (`apps/actingd/src/config/manifest.rs` at 706ead94) | about 55, plus 2 per instance |
| `ledger_observer.*` | 35 (21, #411 A51's two, P0-LO's two, one each of #422 LN-5, LN-TUNE and LN-8, #422 LN-9's three, #422 LN-WS's two and #422 LN-7c Q's two) |
| `recovery_ladder.*`, `host_claims.*` | 16 (and #411 A38's two, #411 B37's four, #411 A35's seven) |
| `performance.*`, `execution.defaults.*` | about 100 (some replace today's `performance_monitor.*` / `performance_control.*` rows) |
| `scheduling.*` (recognition, rerun, cost_commit, blackout, feature_lock, not_run, pack_admission, fact_refresh, suspension, random_delay) | 32 |
| Lab options | 2 |
| per instance: `recognition_package`, `start_emulator`, `scheduling.random_delay.*` (#405) | 5 per instance |
| **total** | **about 226 + 7 per instance** (three instances ≈ 247; five ≈ 261) |

The total stayed under 256 for up to eight instances (255 rows) before #405's three per-instance
keys (SR-1, §1.23); with them it passes 256 at five instances. So D1b implements the split (coordinator ruling, 2026-10-12): `config.parameters`
becomes one `config.parameters.<section>` fact per section (M387 §5.9), written and read that way
from D1b on, and each section fact holds at most 256 rows.
